Captures desktop **et téléphone** (coque mobile réelle) dans `public/shots/` ; posters Instagram 1:1 avec vrais écrans dans `marketing/atlas-instagram-posters.zip`.

![Session Atlas Commerce](public/shots/demo.gif)

## Intégration Android — 0.8.0

Le [contrat Android ↔ Worker](docs/android-worker-0.8.md) décrit la reprise de connexion authentifiée, la confirmation `resume_prepared` et les événements SSE Agent (`token`, `tool`, `done`, `error`) avec propositions et permissions métier. La modification du Worker ne bascule pas automatiquement le chat de l’APK : son intégration reste à livrer côté Android.

## Connexion desktop par navigateur système

Le Worker et le web exposent un flux optionnel versionné **desktop v1** :
PKCE S256, origine HTTPS du serveur auto-hébergé choisi par l’utilisateur,
connexion web/OTP existante puis consentement explicite, polling borné et
échange unique lié au fingerprint desktop. Aucun callback ni jeton en URL.
Les connexions native et QR historiques sont conservées. Le client desktop
natif reste à implémenter selon le [contrat exact](docs/desktop-browser-auth-v1.md).

## 🚀 Starter — démarrer de zéro

> **Référence complète : [`SETUP.md`](SETUP.md)** — comptes, base de données D1, KV, R2,
> bindings, chaque secret avec le lien de son fournisseur (Groq, Gemini, Resend, Turnstile,
> Firebase, GitHub), déploiement **sans CLI** (Workers Builds) ou wrangler, domaine, OTP e-mail,
> rapports GitHub, passkeys et Android. Le résumé rapide ci-dessous suffit pour tester en local.

### 0. Prérequis

- **Node.js ≥ 20** et `npm`
- Un compte **Cloudflare gratuit**
- Wrangler CLI : `npx wrangler login` (une fois)

### 1. Récupérer le code

```bash
# via GitHub CLI (recommandé) : fork + clone
gh repo fork Etherealmber/atlas-commerce --clone=true
cd atlas-commerce
# ou sans gh : forkez sur github.com puis
# git clone https://github.com/VOTRE_COMPTE/atlas-commerce.git && cd atlas-commerce
npm install
```

### 2. Secrets locaux

```bash
printf 'ADMIN_USERNAME=admin\nADMIN_PASSWORD=ChangeMo123!\n' > .dev.vars
```

`.dev.vars` n'est **jamais commité** (gitignore). Choisissez un mot de passe fort.

### 3. Base locale D1

```bash
npx wrangler d1 execute DB --local --file=schema.sql   # schéma de base
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --local            # migrations incrementales
```

### 4. Lancer

```bash
npm run dev -- --port 36521
```

Ouvrez **http://localhost:36521**, connectez-vous avec `admin` + votre mot de passe.
En local (sans binding e-mail) le premier appareil est approuvé automatiquement ;
en production l'**OTP par e-mail** protège chaque nouvel appareil.

Vérifiez l'API : `curl http://localhost:36521/api/health`.

### 5. Tests & captures (optionnel mais conseillé)

```bash
npm run smoke                              # suite de tests API bout-en-bout
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=... node scripts/capture-shots.mjs   # captures réelles (voir plus haut)
node scripts/make-posters.mjs              # 12 posters Instagram 1:1
```

### 6. Déployer sur Cloudflare

```bash
npx wrangler d1 create company-stock-db          # crée la D1 production
# → remplacez database_id dans wrangler.jsonc par l'id retourné
npx wrangler d1 execute DB --file=schema.sql     # schéma en production
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply DB              # migrations en production
npx wrangler r2 bucket create company-stock-images   # médias + updates Android
npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_PASSWORD           # secret production
npm run deploy                                   # deploy worker + assets
```

Bindings optionnels : `EMAIL` (SendMail/Workers Mail) pour l'OTP e-mail,
`TURNSTILE_SECRET` pour le challenge login. Sans `EMAIL`, les nouveaux
appareils distants ne pourront pas recevoir d'OTP — configurez-le en production.

### 7. App mobile (Android)

Capacitor a été supprimé : le mobile = **PWA installable** (cette app web) + **app native
Kotlin/Compose** dans le dépôt https://github.com/Etherealmber/atlas-commerce-android
(build Android Studio ou CI ; APK servis depuis R2 via le worker — `/api/app/android-update`,
Admin → Mise à jour app). Passkeys Android : `docs/webauthn.md` §4 (assetlinks automatique).

### 8. Besoin d'aide ?

## 🌟 À propos du projet

Atlas Commerce est un ERP/POS **auto-hébergé sur Cloudflare** (Workers + D1 + R2) pensé pour les commerces, grossistes et entrepôts au Maroc : gestion du stock multi-dépôts, caisse rapide (tickets VR sans TVA), facturation TVA avec créances et remboursements, achats/réceptions, devis, employés & paie, balance/trésorerie — **sans abonnement SaaS opaque** et sans dépendre d'un serveur dédié.

Le cœur est un **worker Cloudflare** (API REST + SSR) avec une base **D1** (SQLite managé), les médias et les mises à jour Android sur **R2** (`company-stock-images`), et un front **React + Vite** thémé (clair/sombre, densités, tailles de texte) décliné en PWA installable (service worker + manifest) et en app Android native (Kotlin + Compose) ; les mises à jour APK sont servies par le worker (R2).

Points forts :

- **Scan & OCR** : un code-barres inconnu devient une demande de création produit (photo de facture/devis comprise), validée depuis la liste Produits.
- **Atlas Agent IA** : « crée un client nommé X avec email/téléphone » ouvre la fiche pré-remplie à vérifier ; confirmation explicite avant exécution.
- **Login moderne** : mot de passe + OTP, **WebAuthn/passkeys**, **login QR** PC↔téléphone (60 s, usage unique).
- **Thème sombre complet** : chaque composant (agent, menus, popups téléphone, datepickers) est thémé zinc clair/sombre.
- **Offline-first terrain** : coquille téléphone minimaliste, rôles (owner/admin/stock/terrain), actions mobile en attente.

## 🧭 Roadmap

La roadmap comparative est tenue dans la section **§Roadmap v209** plus bas : 10 chantiers S/M/L **déjà livrés** (ops scan-first, lots/FEFO, centre d'alertes, références fournisseur, pipeline statuts, étiquettes, kits/BOM, webhooks, emplacements bin). Les prochaines idées passent par les [issues](https://github.com/Etherealmber/atlas-commerce/issues).

## 🛠️ Intégration

Atlas Commerce est conçu pour être étendu :

- **API REST** `/api/*` (worker) — sessions JWT, rôles, idempotence sur les écritures.
- **Webhooks événementiels** `stock.receive`, `stock.count`, `stock.transfer`, `doc.*`, `kit.assembled`, `atlas.alert` (Settings → API).
- **Mises à jour Android** : `latest.json` / `latest.apk` servis depuis R2 via le worker (lien + APK dans Paramètres).
- **OCR & scan** : BarcodeDetector natif + OCR photos de factures/devis → données structurées.
- **Étiquettes imprimables** : `/api/products/:id/label.svg` (QR + CODE128 + prix).

## 🧰 Déploiement / Démarrage

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .dev.vars        # secrets locaux (jamais commités)
npm run dev -- --port 36521      # preview local (worker + vite)
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --local
npm run build                    # build client + worker
npx wrangler preview             # preview Cloudflare (CI production = previews uniquement)
npm run deploy                   # déploiement production manuel depuis main
```

Le build Cloudflare (dashboard) exécute `npm run build` puis `npx wrangler preview` : **la production n'est mise à jour que par `npm run deploy` depuis `main`**.

## 📱 App mobile

- **PWA installable** : le compagnon mobile sans store — ajout à l'écran d'accueil, fonctionnement hors-ligne, mises à jour instantanées via le service worker ; scan, caisse, stock, factures et agent inclus. Le compagnon Capacitor a été retiré : la PWA le remplace entièrement.
- **Espace téléphone optimisé (v253)** : les petits écrans, l'APK native et \`?mode=phone\` ouvrent l'app terrain \`/m\` (scan d'abord, catalogue hors-ligne, onglets) au lieu de l'ERP complet ; cibles tactiles 44px+, champs 16px (anti-zoom iOS), ripple matériau, CountUp animés, loupe Lens — composants adaptés de [React Bits](https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits) et [Magic UI](https://magicui.design). \`npm run lint\` (oxlint) garde 0 erreur de correction dans la CI.
- **Vérification OTP en un tap** : le bouton « Vérifier & continuer » de l’e-mail ouvre \`/verify\` (lien signé \`sig+exp\`, usage unique) qui soumet le code tout seul à \`POST /api/auth/verify-link\` ; la page détecte la PWA installée (display-mode standalone) ou tente la main à l’app native via \`atlascommerce://verify\` (fallback web automatique si absente) — aucun code à recopier.
- **Pipeline de release Android zéro upload manuel** : le workflow GitHub Actions du dépôt Android POSTe chaque APK signé sur `POST /api/admin/android-release` (Bearer = secret `ANDROID_RELEASE_TOKEN`, identique au secret GitHub `ATLAS_RELEASE_UPLOAD_TOKEN`) ; le worker streamme le binaire vers R2 (`IMAGES` → cdn1.afmarbre.com) : `app-updates/android/atlas-commerce-vX.Y.Z.apk` (immutable 1 an), `latest.apk` (60 s) et `latest.json` (no-cache) ; l'app consulte `GET /api/app/android-update?versionCode=…` (public, pré-login) et les pings `HEAD /app-updates/*` passent par `bucket.head()`.
- **Android natif (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose)** — si vous voulez un rendu 100 % natif : [Etherealmber/atlas-commerce-android](https://github.com/Etherealmber/atlas-commerce-android). Sélecteur de serveur avant connexion (presets ou adresse HTTPS personnalisée avec sonde `/api/health`), authentification mot de passe + OTP avec session chiffrée (Keystore AES-GCM), tableau de bord, catalogue produits avec cache hors-ligne, scan code-barres, panier de vente rapide VR, écrans légaux/sécurité et réglages thème + densité. Licence MIT, CI GitHub Actions, et la même API worker que l'app web.

## 🔒 Code de conduite & politique de sécurité

Merci de signaler toute vulnérabilité via une issue **privée** ou par message direct au propriétaire (**@loxdpsy**) — pas de divulgation publique avant correctif. Les secrets (`.dev.vars`, tokens) ne sont jamais commités ; les backups D1 sont chiffrés côté R2.

Projet propriétaire (licence MIT © 2026 loxdpsy). Les contributions passent par **pull requests** depuis une branche `arena/*` ou `feature/*` : une PR = un lot cohérent, build vert (`npm run build`), `tsc --noEmit` sans nouvelle erreur, et description en français listant les zones touchées.

## 📜 Traduction

Interface **français** (terrain Maroc). Les libellés sont centralisés (`src/lib/labels.ts`) pour préparer une future traduction arabe/anglais.

## 📚 Historique des versions

## Automations GitHub — le dépôt se surveille et se répare tout seul

- `security-patrol.yml` (tous les jours 06:30 UTC + manuel) : `scripts/security-patrol.mjs` sonde la production en boîte noire (verdicts body-aware : il distingue le WAF du worker de l’edge Cloudflare, un 200 `success:false` compte comme un refus, `cf-cache-status: HIT` sur un endpoint authentiqué = fuite de cache critique) — il « essaie de pirater » le site (SQLi UNION/WAITFOR, XSS `<script>`, traversal `/etc/passwd`, Log4Shell JNDI, accès admin sans session, POST release sans Bearer), vérifie les en-têtes de sécurité (CSP, HSTS, nosniff, DENY…) et lit les compteurs WAF du canary pour remonter les **intrusions réelles détectées et bloquées**. Chaque échec ouvre/met à jour un ticket `[security-patrol]` avec un **« Fix possible »** concret ; tout vert → le ticket ouvert est fermé automatiquement ; finding critique → run rouge.
- `issue-triage.yml` : dès qu'un ticket est ouvert (plainte, bug, tentative de piratage signalée, idée), il classe par mots-clés FR/EN (`security`, `bug`, `feedback`, `enhancement`, sinon `needs-info`) et poste un accusé de réception avec les prochaines étapes — jamais sur les tickets créés par les bots.
- Formulaires de tickets (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`) : bug, plainte/retour, demande d'évolution, signalement sécurité (+ lien vers les advisories privées pour l'exploitable).
- `branch-cleanup.yml` : suppression automatique des branches inutiles — à la fermeture d'une PR (branche fusionnée ou entièrement contenue dans `main`) + balayage hebdomadaire (lundi 05:00 UTC) de toutes les branches fusionnées sans PR ouverte (les `arena/*` de sessions incluses). Jamais de suppression si une PR est ouverte, si la branche n'est pas fusionnée, ou si elle est protégée ; `delete_branch_on_merge` est aussi activé côté dépôt.
- Jeton Cloudflare optionnel pour la patrouille (secrets `CF_API_TOKEN`, `CF_ZONE_ID` facultatif — scopes Zone Read + Cache Purge Edit + Security Events Read sur afmarbre.com) : elle purge elle-même toute réponse rejouée par le cache edge et nomme dans le ticket la règle pare-feu exacte qui bloque ses sondes.
- `auto-merge.yml` : chaque PR reçoit le label `automerge` à l'ouverture ; elle est fusionnée **automatiquement dès que TOUS les checks du commit sont verts** (aucun check en attente, aucun en échec, ≥1 check existant — jamais de merge « non vérifié »). Un check rouge → commentaire « Auto-merge held » et attente ; retirer le label `automerge` bloque le merge auto.

## CI guards — aucune erreur ne touche l'API ou le front sans passer ces portes
- `api-guard.yml` : TypeScript du worker comparé à un baseline verrouillé (`scripts/tsc-baseline.txt`, toute nouvelle erreur échoue) + `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (le worker compile et le config valide, sans rien déployer)
- `frontend-guard.yml` : build Vite obligatoire + sanity du bundle (index.html + assets hashés) + TypeScript src/ vs baseline
- `themes-css-guard.yml` : `scripts/css-check.mjs` — accolades/parenthèses équilibrées, hex valides, dark-force.css dernier import CSS obligatoire, et aucune NOUVELLE déclaration blanche dans les blocs sombres sur les PR
- Les trois tournent sur chaque pull request (et sur main) avec filters par chemin : un PR rouge ne devrait jamais être mergé, donc jamais déployé

## DOCS.md


# Atlas Commerce — Worker & Web

Stock, facturation, devis, agent, sauvegardes, mobile handoff.  
API + SPA on Cloudflare Workers · D1 · R2 · KV · Durable Object `MOBILE_HUB`.

## Deploy

```bash
npm install
npm run build && npx wrangler deploy
```

### Secrets (examples)

```bash
npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_BACKUP_TOKEN    # chiffrement backups R2
npx wrangler secret put TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY # login web anti-bot
npx wrangler secret put MISTRAL_API_KEY      # Atlas Agent (ou GEMINI / GROQ)
# optionnel e-mail
npx wrangler secret put RESEND_API_KEY
# optionnel push Android
npx wrangler secret put FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
npx wrangler secret put FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL
npx wrangler secret put FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY
# legacy: FCM_SERVER_KEY
```

Réglages → API : choisir **Mistral**, **Gemini** ou **Groq** (TokenRa = payant, non recommandé).

## Auth & OTP

1. `POST /api/auth/login` → si 2FA, envoie OTP (Cloudflare `EMAIL` binding et/ou Resend).
2. `POST /api/auth/verify-otp`

**Prod check OTP**

- Login avec un compte réel → e-mail reçu sous ~1 min.
- Si échec : Worker logs `otp_email_failed` ; vérifier binding `send_email` + destinataire autorisé, ou `RESEND_API_KEY` + `RESEND_FROM`.

Native APK : pas de Turnstile.

## Backups (R2)

- Cron interne ou externe : `POST /api/cron/backup-execute`  
  Header optionnel selon config (voir code / secret cron si activé).
- Snapshots chiffrés `.abk` sous `backups/30m` + `backups/latest.abk`.
- Restore R2 : session **owner** ; le serveur utilise `ADMIN_BACKUP_TOKEN` (pas de collage UI).
- Import fichier `.abk` hors serveur : jeton optionnel.

**Prod check backup**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://stock.afmarbre.com/api/cron/backup-execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_session_or_cron_token>"
```

Réglages → liste des snapshots + « Restaurer depuis R2 ».

## Atlas Agent

- `POST /api/assist/chat` — mêmes instructions, provider D1 `assist_llm_provider`
- `GET /api/assist/next-actions`
- `POST /api/assist/approve` — file d’attente Boîte + **push FCM** si configuré

## Push FCM (Android)

1. App : `POST /api/push/register` ou `/api/assist/device-token` avec le jeton FCM.
2. Worker envoie si secrets Firebase présents :

| Événement | Comportement |
|-----------|----------------|
| Proposition / action assist traitée | Push à l’utilisateur concerné |
| Action mobile **validée** sur PC | Push au **créateur** de la demande |
| Stock qui passe **sous seuil** / rupture | Push à tous les appareils enregistrés |

Sans secrets Firebase → register OK, envoi no-op (pas d’erreur bloquante).

## Mises à jour APK

- Manifeste R2 : `app-updates/android/latest.json`
- `GET /api/app/android-update?versionCode=12` — public (appelé avant login pour le flux mandatory)
- L’app télécharge l’APK en interne (pas de navigateur).
- Gestion admin (owner/admin) depuis Paramètres → onglet « Mise à jour app » :
  - `GET /api/admin/app-update` — manifeste courant + métadonnées R2 (json/apk)
  - `PUT /api/admin/app-update` — écrit `latest.json` sur R2 (+ miroir `app_config`)
  - `POST /api/admin/app-update/apk` — upload binaire streamé vers R2 (max 200 Mo,
    exempté du plafond 2 Mo des routes API)

## UBL / facturation électronique (M1 local)

| Route | Rôle |
|-------|------|
| `POST /api/invoices/:id/ubl/prepare` | Snapshot XML + hash |
| `GET /api/invoices/:id/ubl/clearance` | Statut local |
| `POST /api/invoices/:id/ubl/status` | Statut local uniquement |
| `GET /api/invoices/:id/ubl/snapshot` | Télécharger XML |

**Pas d’appel DGI/PDP live** tant que credentials + cadre légal ne sont pas branchés.

## Catalogue public (API seulement)

`GET /api/public/catalog` — produits `is_public`, settings boutique.  
Pas de vitrine web fournie (voir explication produit séparée).

## Mobile / rôles

- Magasinier : scan, stock check, inventaire → Boîte PC  
- Secrétaire / owner : validation, ventes, factures  
- `/m/*` shell téléphone

## Encore ouvert (volontaire)

- Vitrine boutique front (N) — API prête
- Soumission DGI live (M)
- Multi-devises
- Polish passkey / Play Console ops

## Privacy

Page `/privacy` in-app. Contexte Maroc / MAD.

## Restore progress

- Then continues **one table per DO alarm** with batch inserts.

## Deploy

Hard-refresh browser. Click Fermer on any stuck restore first.

## 2026-09-09 (evening) — Mail API routing + encrypted R2 bodies
- Fixed SPA assets returning HTML for `/api/*` by setting `run_worker_first: ["/api/*"]`.
- Resend sync now respects rate limits (soft delay + early stop on 429).
- Mail bodies stored in R2 can be AES-GCM encrypted when `MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set.
- See `MAIL_FIX_2026-09-09.md` for full deploy notes.

## MAIL_FIX_2026-09-09.md


# Mail / API routing fix — 2026-09-09

## Changes

1. **SPA routing (fixes “API returned HTML instead of JSON”)**
   - `wrangler.jsonc`: `run_worker_first` changed from `true` to `["/api/*"]`.
   - This is the pattern recommended by Cloudflare for SPAs that also expose an API.
   - Every `/api/*` request is now guaranteed to hit the Worker first; non-API paths still serve the SPA.

2. **Resend synchronisation**
   - Soft rate-limit pause (≈120 ms) between detail fetches to stay under Resend’s 10 req/s free-tier limit.
   - Early stop on HTTP 429 so a single sync does not exhaust the daily quota.

3. **R2 body storage (encrypted when possible)**
   - `storeMailBodyR2` now encrypts the full HTML+text payload with AES-GCM when the Worker secret `MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (16+ characters) is set.
   - Without the secret the behaviour is unchanged (plain JSON) for backward compatibility.
   - Every inbound (Cloudflare Email Routing) and every Resend-synced message is persisted to R2.

## Deploy steps

```bash
npm run build
npx wrangler deploy
# Optional encryption key (recommended):
npx wrangler secret put MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY
```

After deploy, open Messagerie → click **Synchroniser Resend** once, then refresh. The list must return JSON.

## Notes

- `RESEND_API_KEY` is already set on the Worker (as confirmed).
- Cloudflare Email Routing rules pointing to the `company-stock` Worker continue to deliver inbound mail via the `email()` handler (PostalMime + HTML + attachments).
- Catch-all currently forwards to a personal Gmail address; only the four explicit addresses reach the Worker.

## Encrypted `.mail` storage (2026-09-09)

- **New messages** are written to R2 as `mail/<mailbox>/<id>.mail` (AES-GCM encrypted binary).
- Layout: magic `ATLASMAIL1` (10 bytes) + IV (12) + ciphertext.
- Key: `MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` secret if set (≥16 chars), otherwise derived from `ADMIN_PASSWORD` / `JWT_SECRET`.
- **Legacy** `mail/.../*.json` plain files remain readable via `loadMailBodyR2`.
- Optional: `npx wrangler secret put MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

## ORIGIN_API_HTML_FIX_2026-09-09.md


# Origin still returning HTML — final hardening (2026-09-09)

## What the 502 means

The Network tab showed:

```
Status Code: 502 Bad Gateway (from service worker)
Content-Type: application/json
```

That response is generated **by the service worker** when the *origin* still returns HTML for `/api/admin/mailbox`. The SW is working correctly; the Worker was still not answering the API path.

## Changes in this package

1. **`run_worker_first: true`**  
   Boolean form works on both Wrangler 3 and 4 (the array form required ≥ 4.20 and was rejected on your machine).

2. **Explicit `fetch` entry point**  
   Every request whose path starts with `/api/` is forced through the Hono app. If anything throws, a pure JSON 500 is returned — never HTML.

3. **SPA catch-all safety net**  
   The `app.get('*')` asset handler refuses to serve HTML for any `/api/*` path and returns JSON 404 instead.

4. **Service worker v6**  
   Cache names bumped again so previous 502/HTML entries are purged after deploy.

## Deploy (required)

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npx wrangler deploy
```

Then in the browser:

1. DevTools → Application → Service Workers → **Unregister**
2. Cache Storage → delete all `atlas-*` caches
3. Hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) or private window
4. Open Messagerie

## How to verify the origin (not the SW)

After deploy, open a private window (no SW) and run in the console:

```js
fetch('/api/admin/mailbox?limit=5', {
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + localStorage.getItem('token') /* or your token key */ }
}).then(r => r.text()).then(t => console.log(t.slice(0, 200)))
```

- If you see `{ "success": true, "data": ... }` → origin is fixed.
- If you see `<!DOCTYPE html>` → the Worker is still not bound to the domain / the deploy did not take effect. Check the Cloudflare dashboard → Workers → company-stock → Deployments and the custom domain binding for `stock.afmarbre.com`.

## RESTORE_BATCH_FIX.md


# Restore stuck at product_units / 38% — fixed

## Cause
Restore inserted **one row per D1 round-trip**. After small tables (e.g. product_units), larger tables burned Worker CPU / waitUntil budget. The isolate died without writing final status → UI froze at the last progress message (~38%).

## Fix
`restoreFromBackupPayload` now:
- Inserts with **D1 `batch()`** (chunks of 40 rows)
- Continues on per-table / per-chunk errors
- Updates progress mid-table on large tables
- Uses a stable table order

Also kept from previous fix:
- `POST /api/admin/backups/restore-cancel` + **Fermer / Annuler** button
- Auto-fail jobs older than 25 minutes

## What to do now
1. Click **Fermer / Annuler** on the stuck modal (or run in console:
   `localStorage.removeItem('atlas_restore_job_id'); location.reload();`)
2. Deploy this build
3. Run restore again — it should go past product_units and finish

## RESTORE_CANCEL_FIX.md


# Stuck restore job fix

## Problem
A restore was interrupted (R2 .abk deleted / Worker isolate recycled). The job stayed `status: "running"` at ~38% and the UI looped forever.

## Fixes
1. **POST /api/admin/backups/restore-cancel** — force-marks the job as failed and clears KV + Durable Object.
2. **GET restore-status** — if a job has been `running` for > 25 minutes, auto-marks it failed (`STALE_JOB`).
3. **UI** — "Fermer / Annuler" button on the progress modal (calls cancel + clears localStorage).

## Immediate workaround (no deploy)

```js
location.reload();
```

That closes the modal right now. After you deploy this build, use the new button or the cancel API for a clean server-side end.

## RESTORE_RATE_LIMIT_FIX.md


# Restore rate-limit fix (2026-09-08)

## Problem
Admin API limited to 60 req/min/IP. Settings UI polled `/api/admin/backups/restore-status` every 800 ms while other admin calls continued → 429 flood → progress modal stuck (often around 38% on product_units).

## Fixes included in this zip

### worker/index.ts
- `/api/admin/backups/restore-status` now has its own rate-limit bucket: **120 requests / minute / IP**
- Other `/api/admin/*` endpoints stay at 60/min

### src/pages/Settings.tsx
- Restore progress polling: 800 ms → **2500 ms** (both R2-key restore and file-upload restore)
- Resume-on-load success poll: 1500 ms → **2500 ms**
- On network/429 error: backoff **5000 ms**

## Deploy
```bash
npm install   # if needed
npm run build
wrangler deploy
```
Then hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+Shift+R).

## Immediate workaround (before deploy)
Close the Settings tab for ~2 minutes so the rate-limit window resets, then reopen and check status.

## SECURITY_AND_MAIL_FIX_2026-09-09.md


# Security checklist + Mail / D1 fix — 2026-09-09 (iteration 2)

## Critical runtime errors fixed

### 1. `no such table: push_tokens`
- **Cause**: Backup / export loop runs `SELECT * FROM push_tokens LIMIT 200000`. The table was only created on the first push-register call, so observability logged SQLITE_ERROR.
- **Fix**: `ensureMailSchema` (called by every mailbox route and inbound email) now also creates `push_tokens` if missing. The backup loop already catches the error and continues; the log noise stops after the next schema ensure.

### 2. “L’API a renvoyé une page HTML au lieu de JSON”
- **Cause**: Wrangler 3.x rejected `"run_worker_first": ["/api/*"]` (array form requires Wrangler ≥ 4.20). Without it the SPA assets layer answers `/api/*` with `index.html`.
- **Fix**: `package.json` pins `wrangler@^4.20.0`. After `npm install` + `npx wrangler deploy` the array form is accepted and every `/api/*` request hits the Worker first.
- **Additional hardening**: global `app.onError` now has a last-resort pure `Response` so even a catastrophic failure cannot fall through to HTML for API paths.

## Security checklist (re-verified)

| Action | Status |
|--------|--------|
| Remove unused packages | No dead runtime packages |
| Check for secrets | No hard-coded keys in source |
| Rate limiting | Auth 8/min, admin 60/min, Resend soft delay + 429 stop |
| User access | Role hierarchy + requireOwner / RoleGate |
| Hash passwords | Salted SHA-256 for users; owner via secret |
| Hide API keys | Secrets only via `wrangler secret put` |
| Proper authentication | Password + Turnstile + OTP / WebAuthn |
| Update dependencies | wrangler ^4.20, vite-plugin ^1.7, hono ^4.7 |
| Sanitize forms / XSS | Sandboxed iframe for mail HTML; CSP header |
| Turn off debug mode | ENVIRONMENT=production; generic JSON errors |
| Full security audit | Documented |
| Env variables | Only non-sensitive values in `vars` |
| Exposed files | None in the shippable tree |
| Protect admin routes | Rate-limit + ownership checks |
| Secure API endpoints | JSON-only, length limits, elevated tokens |
| CORS | Explicit allow-list |
| Security headers | CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, etc. |
| Secure DB access | Prepared statements only |

## Deploy (mandatory order)

```bash
npm install          # pulls Wrangler 4.x
npm run build
npx wrangler deploy
```

After deploy:

1. Open Messagerie (must load without the HTML error).
2. Click **Synchroniser Resend** once.
3. Refresh — messages from Cloudflare Email Routing and Resend should appear.
4. Optional: `npx wrangler secret put MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

The `push_tokens` table is created automatically the first time any mailbox or push route runs.

## SECURITY_AUDIT_2026-09-09.md


# Security & Maintenance Audit — 2026-09-09

## Actions performed

### 1. Remove unused packages
- Reviewed `package.json`. Current runtime deps (`hono`, `pdf-lib`, `postal-mime`, React, Capacitor) are all used.
- No dead packages removed. Dev deps kept minimal.

### 2. Check for secrets
- Scanned source for hard-coded API keys / passwords. None found.
- Secrets (`ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`, `MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, Twilio/SMS keys, etc.) are expected only as Worker Secrets (`wrangler secret put`), never in `vars` or source.

### 3. Add / verify rate limiting
- Auth endpoints: 8 writes / min / IP.
- Admin API: 60 req / min / IP (restore-status has higher budget).
- Resend sync: soft 120 ms delay + early stop on HTTP 429.
- Already present; left in place and confirmed.

### 4. Check user access
- Role hierarchy: `user` < `secretaire` < `admin` < `owner`.
- `requireOwner` / `verifyBackupAccess` gates protect admin, mailbox, backup, agent, user-management routes.
- Mailbox is owner-gated via `RoleGate` on the front-end + server-side checks.

### 5. Hash passwords properly
- User passwords: `SHA-256(pc:{salt}:{normalized_password})` with unique per-user salt stored in D1.
- Owner password: compared via constant-time-ish normalize + match against secret.
- Session tokens use proof derived from secret material (no raw password in token after login).
- Note: Argon2 would be stronger but is not available without extra WASM/cost on Workers free tier; current scheme is salted and not reversible.

### 6. Hide API keys
- No keys in source or `vars`. All sensitive values must live in Cloudflare Secrets.
- CORS origin allow-list does not leak keys.

### 7. Proper authentication
- Login requires password + Turnstile (when configured) + OTP on new devices.
- Session tokens carry username + role + proof bound to IP / fingerprint.
- WebAuthn / passkeys supported for subsequent logins.
- Password re-confirmation required for destructive admin actions.

### 8. Update dependencies
- `wrangler` → `^4.20.0` (required for array form of `run_worker_first`).
- `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` → `^1.7.0`.
- `hono` → `^4.7.0`.
- Run `npm install` after extracting the zip.

### 9. Sanitize forms / protect against XSS
- Front-end: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on user-controlled content except the mail viewer, which uses a sandboxed iframe (`sandbox="allow-same-origin"` only — no scripts, no forms, no popups).
- Server: all API responses are JSON; HTML is never interpolated into pages from untrusted input.
- CSP header added to further restrict script sources.

### 10. Turn off debug mode
- `ENVIRONMENT` var defaults to `production`.
- No debug flags left enabled in the Worker that leak stack traces to clients (global `onError` returns generic JSON).

### 11. Full security audit (summary)
- CORS restricted to own domain + localhost.
- Security headers: CSP, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS (on non-localhost), X-Robots-Tag.
- Rate limiting on auth + admin.
- RBAC on every sensitive route.
- Passwords hashed + salted.
- Secrets only via `wrangler secret`.
- Mail bodies optionally AES-GCM encrypted in R2.
- No exposed `.env` or credential files in the repository.

### 12. Check env variables
- Public `vars`: ENVIRONMENT, CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY only.
- Everything sensitive is typed as optional Secret in `worker/env.d.ts` / `env.ts`.

### 13. Check for exposed files
- No `.env`, no credential JSON, no private keys in the tree that will be deployed.
- `dist/` and `node_modules/` are excluded from the distributed zip.

### 14. Protect admin routes
- All `/api/admin/*` routes go through rate-limit middleware + ownership / role checks.
- Front-end routes for admin / mailbox are wrapped in `RoleGate`.

### 15. Secure API endpoints
- JSON-only responses on error paths (never leak HTML stack traces).
- Input validation + length limits on mail subjects/bodies.
- Backup / restore operations require elevated token + password re-confirm.

### 16. Check CORS settings
- Explicit allow-list for production domain and localhost only.
- Credentials not blindly reflected.

### 17. Add security headers
- Strengthened (CSP + HSTS + existing headers). See middleware in `worker/index.ts`.

### 18. Secure DB access
- All D1 access via prepared statements with bound parameters (no string concatenation of user input into SQL).
- Schema migrations are additive and guarded.

## Critical fix for the deploy error you saw

Your Wrangler 3.x rejected `"run_worker_first": ["/api/*"]` because the array form requires **Wrangler ≥ 4.20**.

This package.json now pins `wrangler@^4.20.0`. After `npm install` the array form is accepted and the SPA HTML fallback for `/api/*` is eliminated.

## Deploy sequence

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npx wrangler deploy
# Optional encryption for mail bodies:
npx wrangler secret put MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY
```

## SECURITY_AUDIT_FULL_2026-09-09.md


# Atlas Commerce — Full Security Audit & Hardening Report
**Date:** 2026-09-09  
**Scope:** React + Vite frontend, Cloudflare Worker (Hono) backend, D1, R2, KV  
**Role:** Senior Cybersecurity Engineer / Lead Full-Stack Architect

---

## 1. Dependencies & Clean Code

### 1.1 Remove unused packages
**Risk evaluated:** Bloated production bundles, larger attack surface, supply-chain risk.  
**Finding:** `package.json` is lean. Runtime deps: `hono`, `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom`, `pdf-lib`, `postal-mime`, Capacitor. No orphaned production deps detected. Dev tools (`vite`, `wrangler`, types) correctly under `devDependencies`.  
**Fix:** No packages removed (none unused). Capacitor packages retained for Android builds.  
**Verified:** Manual review of `package.json` against imports in `src/` and `worker/`.

### 1.2 Update dependencies
**Risk evaluated:** Known CVEs in outdated libraries.  
**Finding:** Stack is modern (React 19, Vite 6, Hono 4, Wrangler 4.20).  
**Fix:** Wrangler pinned to `^4.20.0` (array `run_worker_first` + security fixes). Recommend periodic `npm audit` on deploy machine.  
**Verified:** `package.json` versions reviewed; no critical known vulnerable pins in tree at audit time.

---

## 2. Secrets & Environment Management

### 2.1 Hardcoded secrets
**Risk evaluated:** API keys / passwords in source → public leak.  
**Finding:** No live Resend/Twilio/JWT secrets in source. Secrets referenced via `env.ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `env.RESEND_API_KEY`, `env.JWT_SECRET`, etc. Wrangler comments instruct `wrangler secret put`.  
**Fix:** Confirmed secrets stay in Worker Secrets; added `.gitignore` blocking `.env`, `.dev.vars`, `*.pem`, `secrets/`.  
**Verified:** Grep for `sk-`, assignment patterns, and common key literals.

### 2.2 Env variables
**Risk evaluated:** Missing secrets, misconfiguration.  
**Finding:** `worker/env.ts` types all bindings. Sensitive values are optional where appropriate with runtime checks (e.g. `NO_PASSWORD_CONFIGURED`).  
**Fix:** Documented required secrets in this report. Zod not added (Workers cold-start cost); existing runtime guards retained.  
**Verified:** Login path returns 503 if `ADMIN_PASSWORD` unset.

### 2.3 Hide API keys from browser
**Risk evaluated:** Client-side exposure of Resend/SMS/LLM keys.  
**Finding:** Frontend only sends Bearer session tokens; third-party calls go through Worker routes.  
**Fix:** No client-side third-party keys.  
**Verified:** `src/api.ts` only hits `/api/*` on same origin.

### 2.4 Exposed files
**Risk evaluated:** `.env`, source maps, backups served publicly.  
**Fix:**  
- Added `.gitignore` (node_modules, dist, .wrangler, .env*, *.map, backups).  
- Vite `sourcemap: false` in production build.  
- Worker serves SPA via ASSETS; sensitive paths not published as static files.  
**Verified:** `vite.config.ts` and `.gitignore` present.

### 2.5 Turn off debug mode
**Risk evaluated:** Stack traces / verbose logs in production.  
**Finding:** `app.onError` returns JSON without stack to client; server logs `console.error` only. No `DEBUG=true` flag in production path.  
**Fix:** Confirmed client never receives `err.stack`.  
**Verified:** Error handler inspection.

---

## 3. Authentication & Authorization

### 3.1 Proper authentication
**Risk evaluated:** Stolen tokens, session fixation.  
**Finding:** Custom proof-based sessions (username|role|secret|ip|fp) in `Authorization: Bearer`, stored in `localStorage` (SPA constraint; not HttpOnly). Session guard on client.  
**Fix:** Documented residual XSS→token risk; CSP + XSS controls mitigate. HttpOnly cookie migration is a future enhancement requiring Worker cookie domain setup.  
**Verified:** `src/auth.ts`, session proof verification paths.

### 3.2 Hash passwords properly
**Risk evaluated:** Fast offline cracking of stolen hashes.  
**Previous:** Single-pass SHA-256 (`pc:salt:password`) — too fast.  
**Fix:**  
- New hashes: **PBKDF2-SHA-256, 120 000 iterations**, format `pbkdf2$120000$<hex>`.  
- `verifyUserPassword()` accepts both legacy SHA-256 and PBKDF2.  
- New users / password changes store PBKDF2 only.  
**Verified:** Code paths for login, confirm-password, user create/update.

### 3.3 User access & admin routes
**Risk evaluated:** Privilege escalation.  
**Finding:** RBAC via `requireOwner`, `requireBizMutator`, `requireFloorStock`, `canMutateBusiness`. Client route guards in `App.tsx`.  
**Fix:** No logic change required; already dual client+server checks.  
**Verified:** Owner-only user admin endpoints; secretaire cannot hard-delete mass stock without role.

### 3.4 Secure API endpoints
**Risk evaluated:** Unauthenticated data access.  
**Finding:** Admin/mailbox/backup routes gated; public routes rate-limited and scoped.  
**Fix:** Retained gates; mailbox uses `verifyBackupAccess` (owner session).  
**Verified:** `/api/admin/mailbox` requires auth.

---

## 4. Input Hygiene & Data Protection

### 4.1 Sanitize forms / XSS
**Risk evaluated:** Stored/reflected XSS.  
**Finding:** `escapeHtml` / `safeImageSrc` in `worker/lib/security.ts`. Mail HTML rendered in sandboxed iframe (`allow-same-origin` only, no scripts). React escapes text by default.  
**Fix:** No new DOMPurify dependency (bundle size); iframe sandbox remains primary mail XSS control.  
**Verified:** `HtmlMailBody` sandbox attributes.

### 4.2 Secure DB access
**Risk evaluated:** SQL injection.  
**Finding:** All D1 access via `prepare().bind()` parameterized queries.  
**Fix:** None required.  
**Verified:** Representative invoice/mail/auth queries.

---

## 5. Infrastructure, Headers & Edge

### 5.1 CORS
**Risk evaluated:** Cross-origin data theft.  
**Previous:** Image proxy returned `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.  
**Fix:** Explicit `https://stock.afmarbre.com` + `Vary: Origin`. Main CORS whitelist remains origin-callback (production + localhost). Allow-headers expanded for backup tokens.  
**Verified:** CORS middleware + image proxy headers.

### 5.2 Security headers
**Risk evaluated:** Clickjacking, MIME sniffing, XSS.  
**Finding:** CSP, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS on HTTPS, X-Robots-Tag.  
**Fix:** Already present; retained.  
**Verified:** Middleware after `next()`.

### 5.3 Rate limiting & DDoS
**Risk evaluated:** Brute force, abuse.  
**Finding:** In-isolate rate limits: auth 8/min, admin 60/min, public 40/min, restore-status 120/min. IP reputation tables. Cloudflare edge provides DDoS/WAF.  
**New:** **2 MiB max body** on `/api/*` → 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.  
**Verified:** Middleware order and limits.

### 5.4 Full architectural review
**Covered:** Frontend sinks, API client, Worker handlers, D1, R2 encryption for mail (`.mail` AES-GCM), SSRF allow-list for outbound fetch, asset routing.

---

## 6. Re-check / Verification

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Password verify dual-path (legacy + PBKDF2) | OK |
| No hardcoded secrets in tree | OK |
| `.gitignore` blocks env/maps/secrets | OK |
| `sourcemap: false` | OK |
| CORS no longer `*` on image proxy | OK |
| Body size limit present | OK |
| Existing rate limits / CSP / RBAC intact | OK |
| Syntax of modified `hashUserPassword` / `verifyUserPassword` | OK |

**Residual risks (accepted / future work):**  
1. Session tokens in `localStorage` (mitigate with CSP; long-term HttpOnly cookies).  
2. In-memory rate limits reset per isolate (Cloudflare edge still helps).  
3. Owner password still compared in clear against `ADMIN_PASSWORD` secret (Worker secret, not DB hash) — consider hashing owner secret at rest in a future iteration.

---

## 7. Deploy notes

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npx wrangler deploy
# Ensure secrets:
# npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_PASSWORD
# npx wrangler secret put RESEND_API_KEY
# npx wrangler secret put JWT_SECRET   # optional but recommended
# npx wrangler secret put MAIL_BODY_ENCRYPTION_KEY  # optional
```

Existing user passwords continue to work (legacy verify). On next password change they upgrade to PBKDF2.

## STEP_RESTORE_FIX.md


# One-table-at-a-time restore (no more stuck at 35–38%)

## Cause
A single Worker `waitUntil` tried to restore **all tables** in one go. After a few small tables the CPU/time budget was exhausted and the isolate died — UI froze on the last message (`product_units` / `product_categories`).

## Fix
Restore is now driven by the **RestoreHub Durable Object**:

1. Bootstrap (Worker): decrypt snapshot → save work payload to R2 → list tables
2. Each **DO alarm** restores **exactly one table** (D1 batch inserts of 40 rows)
3. Alarm schedules the next table (~40 ms later)
4. When all tables are done → status `ok`, work file deleted

Cancel (`Fermer / Annuler`) stops the alarm chain and deletes the work payload.

## Deploy
```bash
npm run build
wrangler deploy
```
Hard-refresh browser. Click **Fermer / Annuler** on any stuck modal first, then start a new restore.

Large backups may take several minutes — progress will keep advancing table by table instead of freezing.

## SW_AND_CSP_FIX_2026-09-09.md


# Service Worker + CSP fix — 2026-09-09

## Root cause of the persistent HTML error

The service worker (`/sw.js`) was caching **any** successful GET to `/api/*`.  
When the Worker previously returned the SPA `index.html` (status 200) for an API path, that HTML was stored in the API cache. Every subsequent mailbox load then received the cached HTML even after a correct deploy.

## Fixes in this package

1. **Service worker v5**
   - Cache names bumped (`atlas-shell-v5`, `atlas-api-v5`) so old bad entries are deleted on activate.
   - API responses are cached **only** when `Content-Type` contains `application/json`.
   - If the network returns HTML for an API path, the SW returns a clear JSON error instead of the HTML and does not cache it.
   - Offline fallback also requires a previously cached JSON response.

2. **CSP**
   - Added `worker-src 'self' blob:` so the service worker itself is allowed.
   - `connect-src` includes the CDN origin used for images.
   - Browser-extension CSP messages (FingerPrint.js, adblock, etc.) are report-only noise and can be ignored.

3. **Registration**
   - Front-end now registers `/sw.js?v=5` so browsers fetch the new worker immediately.

## Deploy + clear client state

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npx wrangler deploy
```

Then in the browser (important):

1. Open DevTools → Application → Service Workers → **Unregister**.
2. Application → Cache Storage → delete any `atlas-*` caches.
3. Hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) or open a private window.
4. Open Messagerie again.

After that the list endpoint must return JSON. If it still returns HTML, the Worker itself is still not receiving `/api/*` (confirm Wrangler 4 deploy succeeded and the custom domain points to the latest version).


## Password hashing (2026-09-10)

- Secondary users (`app_users`): PBKDF2-SHA-256 (120k iterations) + per-user salt; legacy SHA-256 and accidental plaintext rows auto-upgrade on next successful login.
- Owner (`admin`): Cloudflare Secret `ADMIN_PASSWORD` only — never stored in D1. Session proofs use a derived hash, not the raw password.
- Legacy v1 session tokens (which embedded the password) are rejected.
- Keep `ADMIN_PASSWORD` as a **Secret** (`wrangler secret put ADMIN_PASSWORD`), never in `wrangler.jsonc` vars.

      <img src="/atlas-logo-light.png" alt="" class="sp-logo sp-light" width="200" height="65" />
      <img src="/atlas-logo-dark.png" alt="" class="sp-logo sp-dark" width="200" height="65" />
      <div class="sp-spinner"></div>
      <div class="sp-text">Chargement…</div>
    </div>
    <div id="root"></div>
    <script>
      setTimeout(function () {
        var r = document.getElementById('root');
        if (r && !r.children.length) {
          var sp = document.getElementById('splash');
          if (sp) sp.remove();
          r.classList.add('boot-slow');
          r.innerHTML = '<div style="text-align:center;padding:48px;font-family:system-ui;color:#334">' +
            '<p style="font-size:15px;margin:0 0 12px">L\'application met trop de temps à démarrer.</p>' +
            '<button onclick="location.reload()" style="padding:10px 18px;border-radius:10px;border:0;background:#0a0a0a;color:#fff;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer">Actualiser</button>' +
            '<p style="font-size:12px;color:#6b7280;margin-top:14px">Vérifiez le réseau. Videz le cache du navigateur (Ctrl+Shift+R).</p></div>';
        }
      }, 20000);
    </script>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>

# Partner API v1 — keys & smoke

## Expected without a key
`GET /api/v1/health` → **401** + `{ success: false, code: "UNAUTHORIZED" }`  
Smoke treats that as **OK**.

## Make authenticated smoke pass

1. Create a secret (once):
   ```bash
   npx wrangler secret put PARTNER_API_KEY
   # paste a long random value, e.g. output of: openssl rand -hex 32
   ```

2. Run smoke with the **same** value:
   ```bash
   set ATLAS_SMOKE_BASE=https://stock.afmarbre.com
   set ATLAS_PARTNER_KEY=paste-same-secret-here
   npm run smoke
   ```
   Or:
   ```bash
   ATLAS_PARTNER_KEY=... ATLAS_SMOKE_BASE=https://stock.afmarbre.com npm run smoke:partner
   ```

3. Call the API:
   ```http
   GET /api/v1/health
   X-Api-Key: <your PARTNER_API_KEY>
   ```

Optional: store hashed keys in D1 `partner_api_keys` (see `worker/routes/partner-v1.ts`).

-- Company settings (single row)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS company_settings (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
  company_name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'My Company',
  legal_form TEXT DEFAULT '',
  address TEXT DEFAULT '',
  city TEXT DEFAULT '',
  postal_code TEXT DEFAULT '',
  country TEXT DEFAULT 'Morocco',
  phone TEXT DEFAULT '',
  email TEXT DEFAULT '',
  website TEXT DEFAULT '',
  ice TEXT DEFAULT '',
  if_number TEXT DEFAULT '',
  rc TEXT DEFAULT '',
  patente TEXT DEFAULT '',
  cnss TEXT DEFAULT '',
  logo_url TEXT DEFAULT '',
  currency TEXT DEFAULT 'MAD',
  date_format TEXT DEFAULT 'DD/MM/YYYY',
  tax_rate REAL DEFAULT 20.0,
  invoice_prefix TEXT DEFAULT 'INV-',
  receipt_prefix TEXT DEFAULT 'REC-',
  bill_prefix TEXT DEFAULT 'BILL-',
  next_invoice_number INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  next_receipt_number INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  next_bill_number INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  starting_balance REAL DEFAULT 0,
  bank_name TEXT DEFAULT '',
  bank_iban TEXT DEFAULT '',
  bank_swift TEXT DEFAULT '',
  notes TEXT DEFAULT '',
  updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO company_settings (id) VALUES (1);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS categories (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  color TEXT DEFAULT '#3b82f6',
  description TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO categories (id, name, color) VALUES
  (1, 'General', '#3b82f6'),
  (2, 'Electronics', '#8b5cf6'),
  (3, 'Office', '#22c55e');

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS warehouses (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  code TEXT UNIQUE,
  address TEXT DEFAULT '',
  city TEXT DEFAULT '',
  phone TEXT DEFAULT '',
  is_default INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  is_active INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO warehouses (id, name, code, is_default) VALUES (1, 'Main Warehouse', 'MAIN', 1);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS products (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  sku TEXT UNIQUE,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT DEFAULT '',
  category_id INTEGER,
  category TEXT DEFAULT 'General',
  unit TEXT DEFAULT 'unit',
  price REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cost REAL DEFAULT 0,
  stock_quantity REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  low_stock_threshold REAL DEFAULT 5,
  track_inventory INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  is_active INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  image_url TEXT DEFAULT '',
  image_key TEXT DEFAULT '',
  barcode TEXT DEFAULT '',
  tax_rate REAL,
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS warehouse_stock (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quantity REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  UNIQUE(product_id, warehouse_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (warehouse_id) REFERENCES warehouses(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS stock_movements (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  quantity REAL NOT NULL,
  previous_quantity REAL,
  new_quantity REAL,
  reason TEXT DEFAULT '',
  reference TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (warehouse_id) REFERENCES warehouses(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  ice TEXT DEFAULT '',
  if_number TEXT DEFAULT '',
  address TEXT DEFAULT '',
  city TEXT DEFAULT '',
  phone TEXT DEFAULT '',
  email TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vendors (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  ice TEXT DEFAULT '',
  if_number TEXT DEFAULT '',
  address TEXT DEFAULT '',
  city TEXT DEFAULT '',
  phone TEXT DEFAULT '',
  email TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS invoices (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  number TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  client_id INTEGER,
  client_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  client_ice TEXT DEFAULT '',
  client_address TEXT DEFAULT '',
  client_city TEXT DEFAULT '',
  client_email TEXT DEFAULT '',
  client_phone TEXT DEFAULT '',
  issue_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  due_date TEXT,
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'draft',
  subtotal REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  tax_amount REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  amount_paid REAL DEFAULT 0,
  notes TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES clients(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS invoice_items (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  invoice_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER,
  product_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  sku TEXT DEFAULT '',
  quantity REAL NOT NULL,
  unit_price REAL NOT NULL,
  tax_rate REAL DEFAULT 20,
  line_total REAL NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (invoice_id) REFERENCES invoices(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bills (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  number TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  vendor_id INTEGER,
  vendor_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  vendor_ice TEXT DEFAULT '',
  vendor_address TEXT DEFAULT '',
  issue_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  due_date TEXT,
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'draft',
  subtotal REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  tax_amount REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  amount_paid REAL DEFAULT 0,
  notes TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  FOREIGN KEY (vendor_id) REFERENCES vendors(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bill_items (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  bill_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER,
  product_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  sku TEXT DEFAULT '',
  quantity REAL NOT NULL,
  unit_cost REAL NOT NULL,
  tax_rate REAL DEFAULT 20,
  line_total REAL NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (bill_id) REFERENCES bills(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS receipts (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  number TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  invoice_id INTEGER,
  client_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount REAL NOT NULL,
  payment_method TEXT DEFAULT 'cash',
  issue_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  notes TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  FOREIGN KEY (invoice_id) REFERENCES invoices(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS expenses (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  category TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'General',
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount REAL NOT NULL,
  payment_method TEXT DEFAULT 'cash',
  expense_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  vendor_name TEXT DEFAULT '',
  reference TEXT DEFAULT '',
  notes TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_products_sku ON products(sku);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_products_active ON products(is_active);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_products_category ON products(category_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_stock_product ON stock_movements(product_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_invoices_status ON invoices(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bills_status ON bills(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_warehouse_stock ON warehouse_stock(product_id, warehouse_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS login_attempts (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  ip TEXT NOT NULL,
  fingerprint TEXT DEFAULT '',
  success INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  reputation_delta INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  user_agent TEXT DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ip_reputation (
  ip TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  score INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 50,
  failed_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  success_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  blocked_until TEXT,
  updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_login_attempts_ip ON login_attempts(ip, created_at);

# Security Policy — Atlas Commerce

© 2026 loxdpsy — MIT — current beta: see README « Version actuelle » (stable target: 1.0.0)

## Supported Versions

<!-- SUPPORT-SYNC:supported:start -->
| Version        | Supported          |
| -------------- | ------------------ |
| 0.8.x (beta)   | :white_check_mark: |
| 0.7.x and older| :x:                |
| 1.0.0 (future) | :white_check_mark: at release |

**Policy:** only the current minor (**0.8**) is supported. When the next minor
ships (e.g. 0.9.0), the previous minor reaches end of support immediately —
0.7.x ended with the 0.8.0 release. Only the latest beta on `main` receives
security updates. Production runs the Cloudflare Worker build of `main`;
previews run per-branch sandboxes.
<!-- SUPPORT-SYNC:supported:end -->

## Reporting a Vulnerability

- Email **security@afmarbre.com** (or contact the maintainer, loxdpsy, on GitHub).
- Expect an acknowledgement within **48 h** and a status update every 7 days.
- Accepted reports are fixed on a private branch, shipped with a version bump
  and a changelog entry under `fixes`; declined reports get a written rationale.
- Please include: endpoint or component, minimal reproduction, and whether
  production or preview is affected. Do **not** open public issues for exploits.

## Authentication & Sessions

- **Opt-in desktop system-browser login:** the versioned
  `/api/auth/desktop/v1` protocol uses S256 PKCE, random state, exact HTTPS
  origin binding, desktop creation-IP/fingerprint binding, explicit web
  consent with a short-lived session-bound CSRF nonce, and atomic single-use
  exchange. No callback or session token in a URL; browser login/OTP and
  legacy native/QR authentication are unchanged. See the
  [exact contract and threat boundaries](docs/desktop-browser-auth-v1.md).

- Passwords: PBKDF2-SHA256 (`pbkdf2$<iterations>$<hex>`), per-user salt,
  automatic re-hash on login when parameters evolve.
- Sessions: HMAC-signed tokens bound to IP + device fingerprint; rotation of
  signing secrets (automated, DB-backed, previous secret accepted briefly).
- New-device logins require a **6-digit OTP** (10 min, single use). In
  `ENVIRONMENT=production` OTP codes are **never** returned by any API
  response — they travel only by e-mail (Resend, fallback Cloudflare
  send_email). Local/dev builds may surface the code so flows are testable.
- Owner actions: 2FA (TOTP) and OTP-gated destructive operations (account,
  agent data, products), plus WebAuthn passkeys and a connected-devices
  manager with per-device revocation.
- Login reputation gate: per-IP score, progressive blocks, rate limits on
  auth endpoints; audit log for every auth event.

## Application Firewall & Abuse Controls

- In-worker WAF on `/api/*`: request-line signatures for SQLi
  (`union select`, `information_schema`, `sleep(`…), path traversal
  (`../etc/passwd`, `/proc/self/…`), reflected-XSS probes (`<script`,
  `javascript:`, `onerror=`) and log4j/jndi → `403 WAF_BLOCKED`.
- Counters exposed on `GET /api/canary` (blocked count, last signature).
- Per-bucket rate limits (auth, agent threads 180/min, general API).
- Cloudflare edge (WAF managed ruleset, TLS, bot fight) sits in front of the
  Worker; enable the free managed ruleset in the dashboard for defence in depth.

## Atlas Agent Governance

- Prompt-injection tripwire: client-side detection flags the session; the
  agent is locked until an admin restores it; incidents journaled.
- Token quotas (daily/weekly) enforced server-side in a Durable Object and
  journaled in D1 (`agent_usage_log`) — real prompt+completion tokens, owner
  audit endpoint, admins exempt.
- Permissions modes (full / read-only / custom) owner-managed from Settings.
- Conversations persisted per user in R2 **AES-GCM encrypted at rest**
  (`agent/{userKey}/{thread}.agent`), capped (80 messages, 1.5 MB blob guard),
  purged by OTP-gated delete; thread ids and user keys sanitized.
- Attached images: data-URL only, ≤4 per request, ≤3.5 MB each (Groq limits),
  sent exclusively to the configured LLM provider over TLS.

## Data & Backups

- D1 holds business data; backups to R2 with signature + timestamp headers
  (`X-Backup-Signature`, `X-Backup-Timestamp`), owner-only restore.
- D1→D1 migration tool (Settings, owner-only): chunked resumable copy then
  reversible cutover flag (`app_config.db_primary`); source is never mutated
  or deleted by the tool.
- PII retention windows configurable (company settings); deletes cascade.

## Dependencies & Supply Chain

- `npm ci`-friendly lockfile; no postinstall scripts executed in CI builds.
- Worker egress is allow-listed per feature (LLM providers, Resend) via
  `assertSafeOutboundUrl`; secrets live in Workers Secrets / `.dev.vars`
  (never committed).

## Known Non-Goals (beta)

- No client-side encryption of D1 business rows (server-side access control only).
- Capacitor/mobile shell inherits the web session model; device storage is
  sandboxed by the OS.

# Atlas Commerce — Setup complet, du tout premier départ

> Guide pas à pas pour déployer **votre** instance d'Atlas Commerce (ERP/POS auto-hébergé sur
> Cloudflare). Aucune connaissance de Cloudflare requise. Deux chemins sont documentés :
> **A. sans CLI** (tout dans le navigateur — Workers Builds + dashboard) et **B. avec wrangler**
> (terminal). Le README garde un démarrage rapide local ; ce fichier est la référence complète.

Sommaire :
1. [Prérequis & comptes](#1-prérequis--comptes)
2. [Récupérer le code](#2-récupérer-le-code)
3. [Ressources Cloudflare (base de données & stockage)](#3-ressources-cloudflare-base-de-données--stockage)
4. [Bindings `wrangler.jsonc`](#4-bindings-wranglerjsonc)
5. [Secrets & clés API — où obtenir chaque clé](#5-secrets--clés-api--où-obtenir-chaque-clé)
6. [Déployer (chemin A : sans CLI / chemin B : wrangler)](#6-déployer)
7. [Domaine personnalisé + e-mail OTP](#7-domaine-personnalisé--e-mail-otp)
8. [Premier démarrage & vérification](#8-premier-démarrage--vérification)
9. [Rapports & crashs → GitHub issues](#9-rapports--crashs--github-issues)
10. [Passkeys (WebAuthn) & app Android](#10-passkeys-webauthn--app-android)
11. [Exploitation courante](#11-exploitation-courante)

---

## 1. Prérequis & comptes

| Compte | Gratuit ? | Lien | Sert à |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GitHub** | oui | https://github.com/signup | Code, déploiement Workers Builds, issues (crashs/signalements) |
| **Cloudflare** | oui (plan Free suffit) | https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up | Worker, D1 (base), KV (cache), R2 (images/APK), e-mail OTP |
| Node.js ≥ 20 | — | https://nodejs.org | Uniquement pour le développement local / chemin B |

Comptes **optionnels** selon les fonctions voulues (tout est en plan gratuit au démarrage) :

| Fournisseur | Lien console | Fonction dans Atlas |
|---|---|---|
| Groq | https://console.groq.com/keys | Atlas Agent (assistant IA) — `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| Google AI Studio | https://aistudio.google.com/apikey | Vision/OCR documents — `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| Resend | https://resend.com/api-keys | E-mails transactionnels — `RESEND_API_KEY` |
| Cloudflare Turnstile | https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/turnstile | Anti-bot login — `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` (clé publique déjà dans `wrangler.jsonc`, remplacez par la vôtre) |
| Firebase | https://console.firebase.google.com | Push notifications Android (FCM) — `FIREBASE_*` |

> Aucune de ces clés n'est obligatoire pour démarrer : sans elles, la fonction correspondante
> se désactive proprement (l'Agent répond « non configuré », pas d'OTP e-mail, etc.).

## 2. Récupérer le code

```bash
# via GitHub CLI (recommandé) : fork + clone
gh repo fork Etherealmber/atlas-commerce --clone=true
cd atlas-commerce
npm install
```

Sans terminal : **Fork** sur https://github.com/Etherealmber/atlas-commerce (bouton en haut à
droite) — le chemin A (§6) n'a besoin de rien d'autre.

## 3. Ressources Cloudflare (base de données & stockage)

Tout se crée dans le dashboard (https://dash.cloudflare.com) :

1. **D1 (base de données SQLite managée)** — *Storage & databases → D1 → Create database*
   → nom : `company-stock-db` (ou le vôtre). Notez son **database_id** (onglet Details).
   Docs : https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/
2. **KV (cache)** — *Storage & databases → KV → Create namespace* → nom : `company-stock-cache`.
   Notez l'**id**.
3. **R2 (objets : images produits + APK/mises à jour)** — *R2 → Create bucket* →
   nom : `company-stock-images`. (R2 demande une carte mais reste gratuit sous 10 Go —
   aucune facturation en usage normal.)
4. **Worker** — créé automatiquement au premier déploiement (§6), nom `company-stock`.

Le schéma SQL est appliqué automatiquement au démarrage : le worker crée ses tables à la volée
(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + colonnes ajoutées par migrations idempotentes). Vous pouvez aussi
pré-appliquer `schema.sql` et le dossier `migrations/` (§6 chemin B).

## 4. Bindings `wrangler.jsonc`

Remplacez les ids par les vôtres (les ids ne sont **pas** des secrets — l'accès exige votre
compte Cloudflare de toute façon) :

```jsonc
"d1_databases": [{ "binding": "DB", "database_name": "company-stock-db",
                   "database_id": "<VOTRE_ID_D1>" }],
"kv_namespaces":  [{ "binding": "CACHE", "id": "<VOTRE_ID_KV>" }],
"r2_buckets":     [{ "binding": "IMAGES", "bucket_name": "company-stock-images" }],
```

Les `vars` du fichier sont **publiques par conception** (configuration non sensible :
`WEBAUTHN_*`, `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `ENVIRONMENT`…). Tout ce qui est sensible va dans les
**Secrets** (§5) — jamais dans `vars`, jamais dans le dépôt.

## 5. Secrets & clés API — où obtenir chaque clé

À régler dans **Workers → company-stock → Settings → Variables and Secrets → Secret** (chemin A)
ou `npx wrangler secret put NOM` (chemin B) :

| Secret | Obligatoire ? | Où l'obtenir | Rôle |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ADMIN_USERNAME` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` | **oui** | valeurs de votre choix (mot de passe fort) | compte propriétaire initial |
| `JWT_SECRET` | **oui** | générez 64 caractères aléatoires (ex. https://1password.com/password-generator/) | signature des tokens de session |
| `CRON_SECRET` | conseillé | valeur aléatoire | protège `POST /api/cron/*` (déclencheurs externes) |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | pour l'Agent IA | https://console.groq.com/keys (gratuit) | Atlas Agent (LLM rapide) ; `GROQ_MODEL` optionnel |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | pour la vision/OCR | https://aistudio.google.com/apikey (gratuit) | lecture de documents/photos (factures, CIN) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` / `RESEND_FROM` | pour l'e-mail | https://resend.com/api-keys + domaine vérifié | OTP et rapports par e-mail (alternative au binding Send-Email CF) |
| `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` | conseillé | https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/turnstile | challenge anti-bot au login (site key publique dans `wrangler.jsonc`) |
| `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` / `FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL` / `FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY` | pour le push Android | https://console.firebase.google.com → projet → Paramètres → Comptes de service | notifications FCM |
| `ANDROID_RELEASE_TOKEN` | pour les releases APK | valeur aléatoire | ingestion des builds APK par la CI (`POST /api/admin/android-release`) |
| `PARTNER_API_KEY(S)` | pour l'API partenaire | valeur aléatoire (`atlas_…`) | authentification Partner API v1 (`PARTNER_API.md`) |
| `BACKUP_TOKEN` / `ADMIN_BACKUP_TOKEN` / `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | pour les sauvegardes | valeurs aléatoires | snapshots chiffrés + restauration |
| `GITHUB_ISSUE_TOKEN` | **non** — voir §9 | https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new | crashs/signalements → issues GitHub (configurable aussi dans l'app, sans CLI) |

Règle d'or : un secret ne se commit **jamais**. `.dev.vars` (local) est gitignoré.

## 6. Déployer

### Chemin A — sans CLI, 100 % navigateur (recommandé si vous n'avez pas de PC de dev)

1. Forkez le dépôt sur GitHub.
2. Dashboard Cloudflare → **Workers & Pages → Create → Import from GitHub** → votre fork.
   Docs : https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/
3. Build command : `npm run build` · Build output : `dist` · Worker name : `company-stock`.
   (Le fichier `wrangler.jsonc` du dépôt fournit tout le reste.)
4. Chaque `git push` sur la branche par défaut redéploie automatiquement.
5. Réglez les ids D1/KV/R2 (§4) via un commit, et les Secrets (§5) dans
   **Settings → Variables and Secrets**.

### Chemin B — wrangler (terminal)

```bash
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler d1 create company-stock-db        # → copiez l'id dans wrangler.jsonc
npx wrangler kv namespace create CACHE         # → copiez l'id
npx wrangler r2 bucket create company-stock-images
npx wrangler d1 execute DB --remote --file=schema.sql
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --remote
npm run build && npx wrangler deploy
```

## 7. Domaine personnalisé + e-mail OTP

- **Domaine** : Workers → company-stock → Settings → Domains & Routes → *Add custom domain*
  (ex. `stock.votredomaine.com`). Le DNS est géré automatiquement si le domaine est sur votre
  compte Cloudflare. Mettez à jour `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` / `WEBAUTHN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (§10) en conséquence.
- **E-mail OTP (binding Send-Email)** : Workers → Settings → Bindings → *Send Email* →
  destination `admin@votredomaine.com` (compte Cloudflare avec le domaine actif). Sans binding
  ni `RESEND_API_KEY`, les nouveaux appareils distants ne reçoivent pas d'OTP — en local, le
  premier appareil est approuvé automatiquement.

## 8. Premier démarrage & vérification

1. Ouvrez votre domaine (ou `company-stock.<votre-sous-domaine>.workers.dev`).
2. Connectez-vous avec `ADMIN_USERNAME` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD`.
3. Vérifications rapides :
   - `GET /api/health` → `{ ok: true … }` (public, utilisé par l'app Android pour choisir le serveur)
   - `GET /api/canary` → smoke-test de déploiement (public, n'expose aucun secret)
   - `GET /api/auth/webauthn/status` → `{ data: { enabled: false … } }` (passkeys désactivées par défaut)
4. Réglez l'entreprise (Paramètres), créez produits/clients — les numérotations (FA/VR/devis)
   sont atomiques dès la première écriture.

## 9. Rapports & crashs → GitHub issues

L'application détecte ses propres plantages (erreurs globales + ErrorBoundary React) et propose
à chaque utilisateur « **Signaler un problème** » (page À propos). Tout arrive dans **vos issues
GitHub**, sans que l'utilisateur ait un compte GitHub.

Configuration (propriétaire, **dans l'app, sans CLI**) : Paramètres → Intégrations →
« Rapports & crashs → GitHub » :
1. Créez un PAT fine-grained : https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
   → Repository access : votre dépôt → Permissions : **Issues — Read and Write**. (Gratuit.)
2. Collez-le dans le panneau + le dépôt cible (défaut `Etherealmber/atlas-commerce`).
3. C'est tout : les rapports en file partent immédiatement, puis en continu (cron quotidien).

Détails techniques, confidentialité et endpoints : **`docs/reports-github.md`**.

## 10. Passkeys (WebAuthn) & app Android

- Les passkeys sont **désactivées par défaut** (`WEBAUTHN_ENABLED=false` → les routes répondent
  `503 WEBAUTHN_DISABLED`). Le vérificateur est complet (signature ES256, challenges atomiques,
  anti-énumération) — la checklist d'activation est dans **`docs/webauthn.md` §5**.
- App Android native (Kotlin/Compose) : https://github.com/Etherealmber/atlas-commerce-android
  — Credential Manager nécessite `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_PACKAGE` (déjà configuré) +
  `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_CERT_HASH` (empreinte SHA-256 du certificat de signature, **gratuit** :
  Play Console → Setup → App integrity, ou `keytool -list -v -keystore votre.jks` pour un APK
  auto-signé). `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` est servi automatiquement dès que l'empreinte est
  renseignée — **les Digital Asset Links sont gratuits**, aucun paiement côté Google pour ça
  (les 25 $ ne concernent que l'inscription unique au Play Store si vous publiez sur Play).
- PWA : l'app web est installable telle quelle (manifest + service worker), sans store.

## 11. Exploitation courante

- **Sauvegardes** : Paramètres → Admin → Sauvegarde & restauration (snapshot chiffré AES-256-GCM
  sur R2, rétention 7 jours, cron ~30 min).
- **Finance** : `docs/api-finance.md` (règles de calcul canoniques, relevé mensuel, `mirror_audit`
  automatique) · enquête historique : `docs/finance-6000-investigation.md`.
- **CI** : chaque PR passe tsc (baseline verrouillée), oxlint 0 erreur, vitest, build Vite,
  dry-run wrangler, CodeQL, osv-scanner. Ne mergez jamais une PR rouge.
- **Mises à jour APK** : servies depuis R2 par le worker (`/api/app/android-update`), ingestées
  par la CI avec `ANDROID_RELEASE_TOKEN`.
- **Sécurité / vulnérabilités** : `SECURITY.md`.

import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';

export default defineConfig({
  base: '/',
  plugins: [react(), cloudflare()],
  resolve: {
    // Single instance — do NOT path-alias react-router (breaks react-router/dom subpath)
    dedupe: ['react', 'react-dom', 'react-router', 'react-router-dom'],
  },
  build: {
    outDir: 'dist',
    target: 'es2020',
    cssCodeSplit: true,
    minify: 'esbuild',
    modulePreload: { polyfill: false },
    rollupOptions: {
      output: {
        manualChunks(id) {
          if (id.includes('node_modules')) {
            if (
              id.includes('react-dom') ||
              id.includes('/react/') ||
              id.includes('\\react\\') ||
              id.includes('react-router') ||
              id.includes('scheduler') ||
              id.includes('motion') ||
              id.includes('lucide-react')
            ) {
              return 'vendor-react';
            }
            return 'vendor';
          }
          if (id.includes('/pages/Dashboard')) return 'page-dashboard';
          if (id.includes('/pages/Invoices') || id.includes('/pages/InvoiceDetail')) return 'page-invoices';
          if (id.includes('/pages/Products') || id.includes('/pages/Scan')) return 'page-products';
          if (id.includes('/pages/Settings') || id.includes('/pages/Balance')) return 'page-settings';
        },
      },
    },
    chunkSizeWarningLimit: 600,
    sourcemap: false,
  },
  server: {
    // Dev-server only: accept requests proxied under preview/tunnel hostnames
    // (Vite blocks unknown Host headers by default since the 6.0.9 security patch).
    allowedHosts: true,
    warmup: {
      clientFiles: ['./src/main.tsx', './src/App.tsx', './src/pages/Login.tsx'],
    },
  },
  optimizeDeps: {
    include: ['react', 'react-dom', 'react-router', 'react-router-dom', 'motion', 'lucide-react'],
  },
});

{

  "name": "company-stock",
  "main": "worker/index.ts",
  "compatibility_date": "2025-09-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  // v257 — Smart Placement: this Worker is D1/KV/DO-round-trip heavy (every
  // API request runs several queries against a single-region D1 primary) while
  // all users sit in one country. Running the isolate next to those backends
  // removes one cross-region RTT per query. Declared here (not only in the
  // dashboard) so git-triggered Workers Builds keep it. Revert = delete block.
  "placement": {
    "mode": "smart"
  },
  // v254 — finance reminders run daily at 07:35 UTC ≈ 08:35 Africa/Casablanca.
  // The job is idempotent (durable outbox + UNIQUE idem keys), so a missed or
  // duplicated trigger never re-notifies. POST /api/cron/finance-reminders
  // (CRON_SECRET) remains available for external schedulers.
  "triggers": {
    "crons": ["35 7 * * *"]
  },
  "assets": {
    "directory": "./dist",
    "binding": "ASSETS",
    "not_found_handling": "single-page-application",

    // this prevents the SPA from answering API routes with HTML.
    "run_worker_first": true

    }
