FILE: docs/ai-brief.md
================================================
# Atlas Commerce — the complete brief for any AI working on (or porting) this product

> Hand this document to any AI agent together with the repo. It explains how **everything**
> works — from the Dashboard to Settings, the Balance, the wizards, the popups — and how each
> piece must look and behave. Source of truth: `worker/index.ts` (the whole API) and `src/`
> (the React SPA). Never guess an endpoint — read the worker.

## 1. What the product is

**Atlas Commerce** is a French-language stock & invoicing ERP for small commerce (warehouses,
shops). It runs entirely on Cloudflare: a single **Hono Worker** (`company-stock`) + **D1**
(SQLite) + **R2** (`company-stock-images`, binding `IMAGES`, used for app updates) + Durable
Objects (avatar cache). Production: `https://stock.afmarbre.com`. Frontend: **React 18 + Vite
SPA** (no Tailwind — hand-written CSS in `src/styles/` + per-component CSS), installable as a
**PWA**, with a **native Android app** (separate repo `atlas-commerce-android`, Kotlin/Compose)
and a **desktop app** (`atlas-commerce-desktop`, Rust/egui/fastframe). License MIT © 2026
loxdpsy / Etherealmber. Versioning: `0.x` betas (currently frozen at **0.5.5-beta** — never
bump or change changelog dates unless the owner says "push to next update").

## 2. Accounts, roles, security

- **Roles**: `admin` (full ERP), stock role (`magasinier` — terrain duties, **never sees
  prices/money**), plus capability flags (`canSell`, settings access levels). The UI hides
  money columns/labels for stock roles everywhere (`isStockRole()`).
- **Login**: username + password → the worker may require **OTP by e-mail** (Resend; the mail
  template is the Bever-style orange/salmon design with a big code box). Reputation gate:
  login attempts below score 40 are refused. Injection-style inputs trigger lockout. Tokens
  are capped per user.
- **Session token v2** is bound to **(IP, device fingerprint)**; every API call sends
  `Authorization: Bearer` + `X-Device-Fingerprint`. The fingerprint is a stable SHA-256 per
  device (see `src/fingerprint.ts` / Android `DeviceIdentity.kt`).
- **One-tap e-mail verification**: the OTP mail button links to `/verify?user&code&sig&exp`
  (signed `sha256(otplink|user|otp|exp|secretMaterial)`, 10-min, single-use). The SPA page
  auto-submits `POST /api/auth/verify-link` (public, middleware-exempt), detects an installed
  PWA (`display-mode: standalone`) or hands off to the native app via
  `atlascommerce://verify` intents with `browser_fallback_url` back to the page.
- **QR pairing**: the PC shows a QR (`/login/qr`), the phone app claims/completes it
  (`/api/auth/qr/session/{token}` + claim/phone-bind/deny/complete). QR endpoints are exempt
  from the owner gate; anonymous ≠ owner everywhere (hard rule).
- **Deletes are OTP-gated** (a code by e-mail confirms destructive actions) — a delete never
  asks for the password. Trusted devices can skip re-OTP (`trusted_device`).
- Production never exposes an OTP in a response; the mailbox feature was **deleted** (the
  worker `email()` helper quietly discards). Agent data never leaks between accounts
  (per-user storage scoping).

## 3. Shells & navigation

- **PC shell** (`DesktopShell` in `src/App.tsx`): sidebar + topbar sharing ONE theme, content
  pane, persistent Atlas Agent panel on the right, notifications overlay, global search.
  Sidebar collapse state persists. "Focus pages" (Settings, Balance…) render with reduced
  chrome (`layout-settings-focus`).
- **Phone shell** (`PhoneShell` → `/m/*`, `src/mobile/`): narrow viewports (≤900px), the
  native APK and `?mode=phone` get the **minimized terrain app** — scan-first home, offline
  product catalog cache + outbox sync, bills, warehouse, agent, settings-lite, bottom tab
  bar (44–56px touch targets, ripple feedback, no selectable chrome text, 16px inputs).
  Everything else on phone shows the "Espace ordinateur uniquement" page with a jump to `/m`.
  **Directive: phones minimize, PC keeps everything.**
- **WhatsNew modal** (`src/pages/WhatsNew.tsx`): dark, ONE accent color, entry ids like
  `051d17`; every shipped change gets an entry; labels always `0.x`.

## 4. Screen-by-screen (what it does & how it looks)

- **Dashboard**: ONE period selector for the whole page (daily/weekly/monthly/custom), KPI
  cards (CA, ventes, stock bas, impayés), charts (pie ring color `--pie-ring #e8a317`),
  low-stock alert list, recent activity. Numbers animate (CountUp) on phone.
- **Produits**: dense table (32px thumb, sku, stock, price hidden for stock role), search +
  category/location filters + multi-select, pager (`ListPager`), create/edit as **step
  wizards**, drag-drop photos on the photo step (staged blob previews, first = ★ Principale),
  variants (price + initial stock), stock adjustment (in/out with reason), barcode/label
  printing, **OCR bills → product data** (Groq vision), delete = OTP-gated.
- **Ventes / POS**: cart building by scan or click, quantity steppers, client attach, quick
  sale numbering (`VR-` prefix, `prefix_year` / `prefix_year_slash` / `prefix_pad5` styles,
  4-digit pad), receipt printing (thermal 58/80mm — `src/lib/thermal.ts`), receipts carry a
  public verify link (`/api/public/verify?p=v1.invoice.TOKEN.exp.mac`).
- **Factures / Balance (Solde)**: invoice list with statuses, payments (espèces/carte/virement),
  credit notes (`WR-` prefix), unpaid totals per client, document viewers (invoice/receipt/
  client) with public verification pages, export PDF/print. The Balance page aggregates
  trésorerie: encaissements, dépenses, paie, COGS (`qté vendue × coût unitaire CMP ou
  standard`), marge. Bank reconciliation parses statement dates `dd/mm/yyyy`.
- **Clients (CRM) / Fournisseurs**: parties with contacts, balances, history; purchases
  generate draft buy-invoices with suggested quantities (**2× seuil − stock**); catalog cost
  is recalculated as a weighted average on reception (ancien stock × ancien coût + nouvel achat).
- **Dépenses**, **Bons de livraison**, **Rapports** (period reports: sales, stock, catégorie ×
  entrepôt matrix, COGS), **Pointage/Paie** (attendance weights per cycle; **paie suggérée =
  jours travaillés × taux journalier**, late counts as present), **Notifications** (role-based,
  deep-link into pages).
- **Atlas Agent IA**: ONE persistent conversation per account (threads stored per-user,
  never across accounts), page-context aware (knows which screen you're on), quota line
  visible in the panel, attachments appear as **chips only** (no bubbles), prefilled
  **confirm popup** before any write action the agent proposes, Groq-only backend.
- **Réglages**: profile (display name, email, avatar — Durable-Object blob-cached, fast),
  connected devices (revoke), theme (dark/light/system — circular-reveal switch), density
  (comfortable/compact), language, numbering prefixes with live examples, D1 migration runner
  (Settings-driven, no CLI), firewall/WAF status (free CF tier), read-replication is
  automatic, update channel info.

## 5. Interaction laws (non-negotible directives)

1. Create/edit popups are **step wizards**: « Continuer » stays on the same dialog level;
   **no « Retour » on the first step**; footer actions aligned **RIGHT in ALL popups**; the
   sticky footer must **never overlap content**; the Étape indicator is a **compact pill**;
   the footer is **rounded on top**; **no wizard may scroll** (content must fit per step).
2. **Errors display INSIDE the popups** (never a detached toast for form errors).
3. Clicking the overlay/outside a dialog = **cancel + reset** — never persists half-typed data.
4. Pickers are **Discord-style** (searchable lists, keyboard navigation); date picker has no
   white flash and closes on Escape.
5. **Dark theme on ALL elements**: no white pills/triggers/thead/checkboxes, no white flash on
   tap/focus, ONE zinc palette, see-through backdrops, buttons not too black, **no selectable
   button text**, motion enrichment app-wide (subtle, respects prefers-reduced-motion).
6. Scan-based product creation must **NOT ask for a price**; the mobile flow stays minimal.
7. Phones minimize, PC keeps everything. Sidebar theme = topbar theme.
8. Never delete changelog/doc content; never change changelog dates; no Kits/BOM; no Mailbox.

## 6. Visual language

- **Zinc monochrome dark** (mirrored by Android & desktop): bg `#111113`, surface `#1c1c1f`,
  hover `#27272a`, lines `#2a2a2e`, ink `#f4f4f5`, muted `#a1a1aa`, dim `#71717a`, primary =
  white with near-black `#0a0a0a` text; semantic only: danger `#f87171`, warning `#fbbf24`.
  No teal, no saffron/orange brand accent in the app (orange `#f4590c` + salmon `#ee8b6c`
  exist ONLY in the OTP e-mail template).
- Light theme: paper `#f5f2eb`-family (terrain app), same structure. `dark-force.css` is the
  LAST stylesheet and wins the cascade by design — never import after it.
- Type: Inter (desktop/Android), DM Sans (terrain app); tabular figures for numbers; pills
  `border-radius: 999px`; cards 10–22px radii; compact density option.
- Material touches on phone: ripple on tap (React Bits adaptation), CountUp stats, Lens
  magnifier for images (hover devices) — see `src/components/ui/Bits.tsx`.

## 7. API conventions

- REST under `/api/...`, JSON envelopes `{success, data?}` or `{success:false, error, code}`;
  error codes are stable strings (`LINK_EXPIRED`, `BAD_OTP`, `WR_PREFIX_INVALID`…).
- Hono middleware order matters: the auth gate protects only routes registered AFTER it;
  public endpoints must be added to the exemption list (verify-otp, verify-link, qr, health,
  canary). Authenticated responses are `no-store` (edge-cache leak rule).
- Rate limiting per IP; OTP rows are single-use; secrets: `RESEND_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`,
  optional `CF_API_TOKEN`, `ANDROID_RELEASE_TOKEN`.
- Deploy: Workers Builds auto-deploys `main` — never deploy by hand.

## 8. Quality gates (CI must stay green)

`tsc` error budget (`scripts/tsc-baseline.txt`, currently worker=72 src=74 — lower it when
you improve, never raise it) · **oxlint** `npm run lint` (correctness = 0 errors, src+worker)
· vitest · vite build + bundle sanity · wrangler dry-run · css-check (dark-force last, no new
white backgrounds in dark blocks) · CodeQL (suppression patterns documented in
`src/pages/Products.tsx` / `src/auth.ts`) · osv-scanner · security patrol (forged-token
probes). PRs ride the auto-merge pipeline: merge only when EVERY check is green.

# Android FCM bridge — paste-prompt & manual guide (v256)

The Atlas worker already sends pushes over **FCM HTTP v1** (`worker/lib/fcm.ts`)
and already accepts device tokens at **`POST /api/assist/device-token`**
(session-authenticated, upserts into `device_push_tokens`). What was missing is
the **native Android side**: the Firebase Messaging SDK, a messaging service,
and the token-registration call. This bundle adds exactly that.

Two files deliver it:

- **`docs/android-fcm-bridge.patch`** — ready-to-apply git patch for
  `Etherealmber/atlas-commerce-android` (base: `8c6d099`, v1.1.1).
- **This document** — a paste-prompt for an agent with write access to the
  Android repo, plus the Firebase console prerequisites.

---

## Paste-prompt (copy everything below into an agent on the Android repo)

> Apply the attached patch `android-fcm-bridge.patch` to this repo
> (`git apply android-fcm-bridge.patch`). It adds the FCM push bridge:
>
> 1. Root `build.gradle.kts`: `com.google.gms.google-services` 4.4.2 (`apply false`).
> 2. `app/build.gradle.kts`: firebase-bom 33.7.0 + `firebase-messaging` +
>    `kotlinx-coroutines-play-services` 1.9.0, and a **conditional**
>    `apply(plugin = "com.google.gms.google-services")` that runs only when
>    `app/google-services.json` exists — so the build never breaks without it.
> 3. `AndroidManifest.xml`: `<service .push.AtlasFirebaseMessagingService>` with
>    the `com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT` intent filter.
> 4. New package `ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.push`:
>    - `DeviceTokenRequest.kt` — Moshi DTOs for `POST /api/assist/device-token`.
>    - `PushTokenRegistrar.kt` — Hilt singleton; registers the FCM token with
>      the worker after every session activation; no-ops when Firebase is not
>      configured.
>    - `AtlasFirebaseMessagingService.kt` — `onNewToken` re-registration +
>      foreground/data-only notification display on channel `atlas_assist`.
> 5. `AtlasApi.kt`: `registerDeviceToken(@Body DeviceTokenRequest)` endpoint.
> 6. `AtlasApp.kt`: creates the `atlas_assist` notification channel (the worker
>    targets `channel_id: "atlas_assist"` on every push — without the channel
>    Android drops the notification).
> 7. `SessionManager.kt`: injects `PushTokenRegistrar` and calls
>    `onSessionActive()` whenever `SessionState.Active` is emitted (restore,
>    password login, QR pairing).
>
> After applying: do NOT commit a `google-services.json`. Bump the app to
> 1.2.0 (120) only if a release is cut. Build with `./gradlew assembleDebug`
> to verify. If `google-services.json` is absent the build must still succeed
> (that is the point of the conditional apply).

---

## Firebase console prerequisites (one-time, per deployment)

1. In the [Firebase console](https://console.firebase.google.com), create/open
   the project used by the Cloudflare Worker (its ID is the value of the
   worker secret `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`).
2. **Add an Android app** with package name `ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce`.
3. Download `google-services.json` → place it at `app/google-services.json`
   (git-ignored; never commit it).
4. In the same project: **Project settings → Service accounts → Generate new
   private key** → the JSON gives you the three worker secrets:
   - `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` = `project_id`
   - `FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL` = `client_email`
   - `FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY` = `private_key` (PEM; keep the `\n` escapes)

## Worker-side secrets (already supported — verify they are set)

```bash
# from the atlas-commerce repo root (web + worker)
npx wrangler secret list                 # shows which secrets exist
npx wrangler secret put FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
npx wrangler secret put FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL
npx wrangler secret put FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY   # paste PEM with \n newlines
# legacy fallback only (deprecated HTTP API):
npx wrangler secret put FCM_SERVER_KEY
```

Behavior when the secrets are missing: `sendFcmToUser()` finds no
`FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` → no access token → falls back to `FCM_SERVER_KEY`; if
neither exists it sends nothing and returns `{ sent: 0 }` (no crash, no error
to callers). Registered tokens stay in D1, so pushes start flowing as soon as
the secrets are set.

## Verification checklist

- [ ] `git apply --check docs/android-fcm-bridge.patch` passes in the Android repo.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds (with and without `google-services.json`).
- [ ] Sign in on a device → worker log shows `POST /api/assist/device-token` 200;
      row appears in `device_push_tokens` (`SELECT username, platform, updated_at FROM device_push_tokens`).
- [ ] Trigger a push (e.g. finance reminder cron or assist approval) →
      notification appears on channel “Assistant & notifications serveur”.

## Employee self-payroll (same release, no Android patch required yet)

`GET /api/me/payroll` is live on the worker (see `docs/api-finance.md`): any
signed-in session gets ONLY its own pay date/amount via the linked employee
file (`employees.user_username`, set by an admin in the employee form). Android
can call it with the existing Retrofit client — add the endpoint + a Profil
screen row when the next native release is cut.

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+package ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.push
+
+import android.app.NotificationManager
+import android.app.PendingIntent
+import android.content.Intent
+import androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat
+import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService
+import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage
+import dagger.hilt.android.AndroidEntryPoint
+import ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.AtlasApp
+import ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.MainActivity
+import ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.R
+import javax.inject.Inject
+
+/**
+ * v1.2 FCM bridge — receives worker pushes sent over FCM HTTP v1
+ * (`android.notification.channel_id = "atlas_assist"`).
+ *
+ * Background messages carrying a `notification` block are shown by the system
+ * tray automatically; this service covers foreground display, data-only
+ * messages, and token rotation (re-registration with the worker).
+ */
+@AndroidEntryPoint
+class AtlasFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService() {
+
+    @Inject
+    lateinit var registrar: PushTokenRegistrar
+
+    override fun onNewToken(token: String) {
+        registrar.onTokenRefreshed(token)
+    }
+
+    override fun onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage) {
+        val title = message.notification?.title
+            ?: message.data["title"]
+            ?: "Atlas Commerce"
+        val body = message.notification?.body ?: message.data["body"]
+        if (body.isNullOrBlank()) return
+        showNotification(title, body, message.data)
+    }
+
+    private fun showNotification(title: String, body: String, data: Map<String, String>) {
+        runCatching {
+            val intent = Intent(this, MainActivity::class.java).apply {
+                flags = Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_SINGLE_TOP
+                for ((key, value) in data) putExtra(key, value)
+            }
+            val pending = PendingIntent.getActivity(
+                this,
+                title.hashCode(),
+                intent,
+                PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT or PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE,
+            )
+            val notification = NotificationCompat.Builder(this, AtlasApp.ASSIST_CHANNEL_ID)
+                .setSmallIcon(R.drawable.ic_stat_update)
+                .setContentTitle(title)
+                .setContentText(body)
+                .setStyle(NotificationCompat.BigTextStyle().bigText(body))
+                .setPriority(NotificationCompat.PRIORITY_HIGH)
+                .setAutoCancel(true)
+                .setContentIntent(pending)
+                .build()
+            val nm = getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java) ?: return
+            nm.notify(title.hashCode(), notification)
+        }
+    }
+}

+package ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.push
+
+import com.squareup.moshi.JsonClass
+
+/** Body of POST /api/assist/device-token (worker upserts into device_push_tokens). */
+@JsonClass(generateAdapter = true)
+data class DeviceTokenRequest(
+    val token: String,
+    val platform: String = "android",
+)

+/** Worker ack: `{ success: true, data: { registered: true } }`. */
+@JsonClass(generateAdapter = true)
+data class DeviceTokenAckDto(
+    val registered: Boolean = false,
+)

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/app/src/main/java/ma/etherealmber/atlascommerce/push/PushTokenRegistrar.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+package ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.push
+
+import android.content.Context
+import com.google.firebase.FirebaseApp
+import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessaging
+import dagger.hilt.android.qualifiers.ApplicationContext
+import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
+import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
+import kotlinx.coroutines.tasks.await
+import ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.core.net.ApiProvider
+import ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.core.net.TokenHolder
+import ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce.di.ApplicationScope
+import javax.inject.Inject
+import javax.inject.Singleton
+
+/**
+ * v1.2 FCM bridge — registers this device's push token with the Atlas worker
+ * (`POST /api/assist/device-token`, Bearer session) so server-side pushes
+ * (assist approvals, finance reminders, stock alerts) reach Android.
+ *
+ * Graceful degradation: when `google-services.json` is absent (Firebase not
+ * configured for this checkout), every entry point is a no-op — the app still
+ * builds and runs normally, push simply stays inactive.
+ */
+@Singleton
+class PushTokenRegistrar @Inject constructor(
+    @ApplicationContext private val context: Context,
+    private val apiProvider: ApiProvider,
+    private val tokenHolder: TokenHolder,
+    @ApplicationScope private val scope: CoroutineScope,
+) {
+
+    fun firebaseConfigured(): Boolean =
+        runCatching { FirebaseApp.getApps(context).isNotEmpty() }.getOrDefault(false)
+
+    /** Called whenever a session becomes active (restore, password login, QR pairing). */
+    fun onSessionActive() {
+        if (!firebaseConfigured()) return
+        scope.launch { runCatching { register() } }
+    }
+
+    /** Called by [AtlasFirebaseMessagingService] when FCM rotates the token. */
+    fun onTokenRefreshed(token: String) {
+        if (!firebaseConfigured() || !tokenHolder.hasSession()) return
+        scope.launch { runCatching { post(token) } }
+    }
+
+    suspend fun register() {
+        if (!firebaseConfigured() || !tokenHolder.hasSession()) return
+        val token = runCatching { FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.await() }.getOrNull()
+        if (token.isNullOrBlank()) return
+        post(token)
+    }
+
+    private suspend fun post(token: String) {
+        if (!tokenHolder.hasSession()) return
+        runCatching {
+            apiProvider.api().registerDeviceToken(DeviceTokenRequest(token = token, platform = "android"))
+        }
+    }
+}
diff --git a/build.gradle.kts b/build.gradle.kts
index cdd290a..3124619 100644
--- a/build.gradle.kts
+++ b/build.gradle.kts
@@ -3,4 +3,6 @@ plugins {
     id("org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose") version "2.3.0" apply false
     id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.4" apply false

# Audit ciblé — envoi FCM Android

## Périmètre et état des preuves

Audit du dispatcher FCM, de l’enregistrement du jeton et du contrat de réception Android uniquement. Aucun changement d’authentification, d’OTP, de rôles/autorisations, de secrets, de Durable Objects ou de passkeys. Pas de changement de version ni du journal Nouveautés.

Sources Android examinées sur `Etherealmber/atlas-commerce-android` (main : `daceed03a02500ab90640f8b3b353aa7eb23cc05`) :
- `push/PushTokenRegistrar.kt`, `push/DeviceTokenRequest.kt` ;
- `push/AtlasFirebaseMessagingService.kt` ;
- `AtlasApp.kt`, `AndroidManifest.xml` ;
- `docs/firebase-and-background-notifications.md`.

| Vérification | Résultat |
| --- | --- |
| Récupération du jeton SDK à l’activation de session | Vérifiée dans le code Android : `FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.await()` |
| Rotation du jeton | Vérifiée dans le code : `onNewToken` appelle le registrar ; sans session, la prochaine activation relit le jeton SDK |
| Jeton courant réellement enregistré sur le Worker sélectionné | **Non vérifié en production** : aucun accès au téléphone, au contenu D1 de production ou au build installé |
| Projet Firebase / application du build installé | **Non vérifié** : `google-services.json` est hors Git et le jeton est opaque ; la configuration réelle du Worker n’a pas été lue |
| Payload serveur et classification des réponses FCM | Vérifiés par tests HTTP v1 simulés, y compris signature OAuth locale avec clé éphémère de test |
| Acceptation réelle d’un push par FCM | **Non vérifiée en production** : aucun envoi réel depuis cet environnement |
| Permission notifications Android et canal activés sur le téléphone | **Non vérifiés sur appareil** ; déclaration et création du canal vérifiées dans le code |

Ne pas confondre ces niveaux : l’accusé d’enregistrement du Worker n’est pas un accusé d’envoi FCM, et l’acceptation FCM n’est pas une preuve d’affichage Android.

## Constats et corrections

1. **Suppression trop large des jetons.** Le dispatcher supprimait sur tout HTTP 404 ou `NOT_FOUND`, y compris une erreur de projet/ressource. Désormais, en HTTP v1, seule une réponse d’échec contenant un détail typé `type.googleapis.com/google.firebase.fcm.v1.FcmError` avec `errorCode: UNREGISTERED` autorise la suppression. Tous les détails sont examinés, pas seulement le premier.
2. **Succès non inspectés.** Chaque réponse HTTP v1 est maintenant lue. Un envoi n’est compté accepté que sur réponse 2xx avec un `name` de message valide dans le projet ciblé. L’identifiant du message et le code HTTP sont journalisés ; un 2xx malformé n’est pas annoncé accepté.
3. **Erreurs à conserver sans purger.** `SENDER_ID_MISMATCH`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, erreurs de credentials, quota, 404 générique, 410, 429, 5xx et erreurs réseau ne provoquent pas de suppression. Pas de rafraîchissement arbitraire du jeton par le serveur : le SDK Android en est responsable.
4. **Payload visible.** Titre et corps non vides obligatoires ; aucune notification vide n’est envoyée. HTTP v1 conserve `notification.title`, `notification.body`, `android.notification.channel_id: atlas_assist`, et le click action existant. `data.event` est conservé ou dérivé des anciens champs `type`/`kind`, avec les IDs existants pour le clic. Aucun secret nouveau n’est ajouté au payload.
5. **Priorité.** Le comportement HIGH des alertes utilisateur sensibles au délai est conservé. L’option `priority: NORMAL` permet les envois non urgents ; elle ne remplace pas les réglages du canal Android.
6. **Pas de repli trompeur.** Quand un projet HTTP v1 est configuré, un échec OAuth ne bascule plus silencieusement vers une clé legacy potentiellement différente. Aucun secret n’est créé ou modifié.
7. **Legacy explicite uniquement.** Les déploiements sans projet v1 mais avec clé legacy gardent la compatibilité. La réponse par destinataire est examinée (un HTTP 200 peut être un échec). Seul `NotRegistered` autorise une suppression, jamais le statut HTTP seul. L’identifiant de canal et les métadonnées de clic sont aussi transmis.
8. **Journaux sûrs.** Aucun corps brut FCM/OAuth, exception brute, jeton d’enregistrement, jeton OAuth, clé privée, clé legacy ou contenu utilisateur dans les nouveaux logs. Les codes sont sur liste blanche ; les succès journalisent l’ID de message, pas le payload. L’échec d’enregistrement D1 ne journalise plus l’exception brute qui pourrait contenir les paramètres liés.
9. **Enregistrement fidèle.** Les jetons dépassant la limite existante de 512 caractères sont refusés explicitement au lieu d’être tronqués et enregistrés sous une valeur différente du SDK. Les jetons valides sont conservés tels quels et leur horodatage est mis à jour. Aucun nettoyage fondé seulement sur l’âge. L’ordre des jetons récemment enregistrés est déterministe en cas d’horodatage identique.
10. **Plusieurs bases.** La préparation de table est mémorisée par binding D1 au lieu d’un indicateur partagé entre toutes les bases.

`sendFcmToUser` conserve son résultat `{sent, purged}` : **sent = accepté par FCM**, pas « affiché ». Un échec sur un destinataire n’empêche pas l’essai des autres appareils ; il ne supprime pas son jeton.

## Vérification d’exploitation : deux validations séparées

### A. Enregistrement / projet / acceptation FCM

À effectuer localement par le propriétaire de l’environnement, sans publier de jetons ou credentials :

1. Sur **l’APK installé**, vérifier que Firebase est configuré. Comparer localement les identifiants non secrets de `FirebaseApp.getInstance().options` (`projectId`, `applicationId`, `gcmSenderId`) et le package du build avec l’application Android enregistrée dans Firebase. Le package attendu par le dépôt est `ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce` ; tenir compte d’un éventuel suffixe de build. Ne pas afficher l’ensemble de la configuration ni les clés.
2. Vérifier que le projet ciblé par la configuration existante `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` est le projet attendu par cette application. Un compte de service peut être autorisé sur un autre projet : ne pas conclure uniquement à partir de son adresse e-mail. Ne modifier aucun secret dans le cadre de cet audit.
3. Activer une session sur le Worker sélectionné. Le registrar doit relire le jeton SDK et recevoir `success: true, data.registered: true`. Vérifier l’horodatage de mise à jour de l’enregistrement côté D1. Ne pas exporter la colonne `token`, ni recopier un ancien jeton depuis des logs. Ne pas supprimer les autres enregistrements pour « forcer » le test.
4. Déclencher un événement métier déjà autorisé qui envoie à ce compte. Dans les logs Worker, rechercher `[fcm-send]` : `transport: v1`, `http_status: 200`, `outcome: accepted`, `message_id` non vide. Conserver uniquement cet ID et les codes pour l’audit.
5. Si `SENDER_ID_MISMATCH` apparaît : conserver le jeton et examiner le couple projet/app SDK et projet ciblé. Une acceptation FCM prouve le routage accepté dans ce projet, **pas à elle seule le package exact de l’application** : plusieurs applications peuvent appartenir au même projet.
6. Si FCM renvoie explicitement `UNREGISTERED`, le seul jeton concerné est supprimé. Faire relire/recréer et réenregistrer le jeton par le SDK Android, selon son cycle normal. Ne jamais générer un « nouveau token » côté Worker.

### B. Permission et canal Android — indépendant du succès FCM

Sur le téléphone test, ouvrir **Paramètres Android → Applications → Atlas Commerce → Notifications** :

- autorisation des notifications de l’application activée ;
- sur Android 13+, permission `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` accordée (la déclaration manifest seule ne suffit pas) ;
- canal **Assistant & notifications serveur**, ID `atlas_assist`, présent et non bloqué ; importance différente de `IMPORTANCE_NONE` ;
- vérifier séparément les modes silencieux/Ne pas déranger et les restrictions constructeur.

Pour un écran de diagnostic Android existant, relever uniquement les booléens/valeurs de : `NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()`, permission runtime sur API 33+, et `NotificationManager.getNotificationChannel("atlas_assist")?.importance` sur API 26+. Aucun jeton dans ces diagnostics.

Le dépôt Android crée `atlas_assist` avec importance HIGH. Cela ne réactive pas un canal que l’utilisateur a bloqué. Tester un push visible application ouverte puis en arrière-plan ; noter séparément : accepté par FCM / affiché sur le téléphone. Une application forcée à l’arrêt, Doze ou la politique batterie d’un constructeur peuvent empêcher ou retarder l’affichage malgré un envoi accepté.

## Limites laissées volontairement hors modification

- Aucun accès à l’APK installé ni à ses préférences système : les cases A et B restent à valider sur l’environnement réel, pas déclarées réussies par les tests simulés.
- La sélection des destinataires métier n’est pas modifiée. Le helper historique de diffusion de stock lit `push_tokens`, tandis que le registrar APK écrit `device_push_tokens`. Cet écart peut expliquer une absence d’appel d’envoi pour certains comptes ; fusionner les listes élargirait potentiellement les destinataires et nécessite un examen séparé des règles métier, exclu de cette demande.
- Certains appelants possèdent leurs propres statuts de file d’attente. Leur état ne remplace pas l’accusé `[fcm-send] accepted` ; les workflows métier ne sont pas remaniés ici.
- Aucun déploiement production, rotation de secret ou modification de l’application Android dans cette session.

## Validation locale de cette correction

- Suite complète : **332 tests passent**.
- Dispatcher : **25 tests** ciblés couvrent le payload visible, HIGH/NORMAL, les réponses HTTP v1, `UNREGISTERED` au-delà du premier détail, conservation sur erreurs génériques/projet/quota, logs sans jetons, réponse 2xx invalide, panne par appareil, OAuth sans repli legacy et réponses legacy par destinataire.
- Route d’enregistrement : rejet sans troncature, erreurs sûres ; tests de notifications stock ajustés pour distinguer un vrai `NotRegistered` d’un simple 404.
- Build Vite OK ; oxlint 0 erreur ; contrôle CSS OK.
- TypeScript : 71 erreurs Worker / 74 client, dans la baseline existante, aucune nouvelle erreur dans les fichiers modifiés.
- Ces tests utilisent uniquement des réponses réseau simulées et une clé de test éphémère. Ils ne constituent pas une confirmation d’acceptation FCM en production ni d’affichage sur Android.

FILE: docs/android-worker-0.8.md
================================================
# Android ↔ Worker — contrat 0.8.0

Version publique : **0.8.0**, canal beta. Aucune version suivante sans ordre explicite.
Ce document décrit le Worker de ce dépôt ; il ne signifie pas que l’APK a été modifié, compilé ou livré. Déployer le Worker avant de vérifier le contrat dans l’APK.

## 1. Connexion : verrouiller l’APK sans contourner l’OTP

La correction Android du drapeau « session restore disabled » reste côté APK. Le Worker n’active aucune restauration automatique : une reprise par mot de passe vérifie toujours les identifiants.

Préparation existante : `POST /api/auth/logout`, authentifié, avec le fingerprint de cette installation dans `X-Device-Fingerprint`.

Réponse additive, compatible avec les clients existants :

```json
{"success":true,"resume_prepared":true}
```

- `resume_prepared: true` : le marqueur du compte/appareil authentifié a été écrit pour 30 jours. Ce n’est ni un jeton de connexion ni une dispense permanente d’OTP.
- `success: true, resume_prepared: false` : aucun marqueur écrit (par exemple header fingerprint absent). L’application peut terminer son nettoyage local, mais ne doit pas annoncer une reprise préparée.
- Échec d’écriture : HTTP 503, `success: false`, `resume_prepared: false`, code `RESUME_PREPARATION_FAILED`.
- Authentification absente, invalide ou appareil révoqué : refus par le middleware, aucune exemption.

À la prochaine connexion, **le Worker seul décide `needs_otp`**. Avec 2FA désactivée, le même compte et le même fingerprint peuvent consommer un marqueur non expiré après vérification du mot de passe. La consommation est atomique : deux connexions simultanées ne peuvent pas réutiliser le même marqueur. Autre compte, autre appareil, mot de passe incorrect, marqueur absent/expiré ou appareil révoqué : pas de raccourci. Avec 2FA activée : OTP conservé.

Après un échec réseau, ne jamais simuler une réussite ni ignorer `needs_otp`. Un timeout est un résultat indéterminé : la requête peut avoir été traitée côté serveur avant la perte de l’accusé de réception. Il ne prouve ni création ni absence du marqueur.

Préserver côté Android : état SignedOut au nouveau processus, mot de passe requis, jeton précédent utilisé uniquement pour la préparation isolée, origine serveur strictement vérifiée, aucun jeton réinstallé globalement, nettoyage même en cas d’échec. Ne pas convertir une révocation en déconnexion volontaire. Ne pas modifier les flux QR/biométriques existants.

## 2. Atlas Agent : passer au SSE sans perdre les outils métier

La note « le Worker streaming n’a pas les outils métier » est dépassée : cette parité existe depuis la PR #156. La version 0.8.0 ajoute les propositions au contrat final et partage explicitement la sélection/l’autorisation des outils entre les routes classique et SSE.

### Requête

`POST /api/assist/chat/stream`, avec la session et le fingerprint habituels, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: text/event-stream`. Les headers de version Android restent inchangés. `X-Atlas-Client: android` ne dispense jamais de l’authentification.

Même corps que `/api/assist/chat` : `message`, éventuellement `user_message`, `response_language` (`fr`, `en`, `ar`), `thread_id`, `task`, `timezone`, `documents`, `images`. Ne pas ajouter un second endpoint ou un deuxième moteur de conversation.

### Événements

Chaque frame se termine par une ligne vide. `data` est un objet JSON **direct**, sans enveloppe `success/data` :

```text
event: token
data: {"t":"Bonjour "}

event: token
data: {"t":"à vous."}

event: done
data: {"reply":"Bonjour à vous.","model":"model-id","provider":"groq","usage":{"prompt":20,"completion":8},"documents":[],"thread_id":"android-thread","tool_trace":[],"proposals":[],"task":"general","history_turns":0}

```

- `token` : ajouter `t` au message provisoire immédiatement, sans attendre la fin du body HTTP.
- `tool` : progression d’une exécution serveur, avec `name`, `ok`, et selon le cas `data`, `error`, `proposal`. Ne pas exécuter cette proposition automatiquement.
- `done` : réponse finale de référence. **Remplacer** le texte provisoire par `reply` (ne pas le concaténer une seconde fois), conserver les métadonnées et traiter le message comme terminé.
- `error` : objet avec `code` et `error`. Terminer la génération en erreur ; ne pas présenter le texte partiel comme une réponse complète.
- Fin de connexion sans `done` ni `error` : réponse interrompue, pas une réussite.
- Ignorer proprement les noms d’événements/champs inconnus pour la compatibilité future. Le parseur doit supporter les frames et caractères UTF-8 répartis sur plusieurs lectures réseau.

Les outils autorisés par rôle et les outils mémoire/savoir sont partagés avec la route classique. Si le chargement des préférences échoue, les outils métier sont exclus (repli fermé). Un outil désactivé ou non autorisé ne peut pas être exécuté, même si le modèle invente son appel. Les propositions ne proviennent que des résultats réussis d’outils serveur ; elles ne sont jamais devinées depuis le texte du modèle.

### Propositions

Les routes classique (`data.proposals`) et SSE (`done.proposals`) retournent désormais les mêmes propositions produites par leurs outils. Exemple d’ajustement :

```json
{"type":"inventory_adjustment","product_id":1,"product_name":"Produit","sku":"P1","delta":2,"current_stock":20,"note":"Proposition assistant IA","requires_approval":true}
```

La génération de cette proposition ne modifie pas le stock. L’APK affiche une confirmation et utilise le parcours métier autorisé existant ; ne pas inventer d’identifiant de proposition ni appeler `/api/assist/apply` sans l’identifiant et le contrat réellement requis par cette route. Aucun auto-approve.

Pour `type: inventory_adjustment`, après confirmation explicite de l’utilisateur, le parcours disponible est `POST /api/stock-adjustment-requests` avec la session habituelle et ce corps :

```json
{"product_id":1,"direction":"in","quantity":2,"reason":"Proposition assistant IA confirmée","idempotency_key":"une-cle-unique-par-confirmation"}
```

Convertir le delta : positif → `direction: in`, négatif → `direction: out`, `quantity = abs(delta)` strictement positive. Réutiliser la même clé en cas de retry de la même confirmation. Cette route soumet une **demande** : elle ne modifie pas directement le stock. Réponse 201 à la création ou 200 au replay idempotent, avec `data.id`. La validation séparée reste réservée aux rôles autorisés via `POST /api/stock-adjustment-requests/:id/approve` (ou `/reject`, corps `{"note":"..."}`). Respecter les erreurs de validation et de rôle du serveur ; ne jamais appeler automatiquement la route d’approbation.

### Erreurs et limites

- Avant l’ouverture du flux : erreurs HTTP JSON habituelles (session, quota/suspension Agent, document refusé, configuration…). Vérifier le statut HTTP avant de lancer le parseur SSE.
- Après ouverture : événement `error`. Ne pas relancer automatiquement la même requête sur l’endpoint bufferisé : un outil peut déjà avoir eu un effet. Éviter les doublons de requêtes/actions.
- Les contrôles de session, suspension, quota et documents sont conservés. Le quota normal utilise la consommation réelle cumulée des tours outils.
- La vision conserve son chemin bufferisé : une image peut donc produire un seul événement `token`, suivi de `done`. Les raccourcis locaux peuvent aussi arriver en un seul token. Ce n’est pas un défaut du parseur Android.
- `done.reply` prévaut sur les fragments : il peut être normalisé, nettoyé ou venir d’un repli final. Ne pas exiger que tous les chemins spéciaux soient tokenisés mot à mot.

## 3. Validation d’intégration Android

- Mettre à jour la note obsolète sur les outils SSE et basculer le chat texte sur l’endpoint streaming existant.
- Vérifier affichage progressif, remplacement final sans doublon, progression outils et propositions confirmées explicitement.
- Vérifier utilisateur stock vs propriétaire, outil désactivé, interruption réseau et erreur serveur.
- Vérifier langue de réponse, identifiant de conversation et documents.
- Vérifier préparation de reprise, mot de passe, 2FA on/off, autre compte/appareil et révocation.
- Ne pas modifier la version de l’APK sans instruction ; le bump 0.8.0 de cette livraison concerne le produit Worker/web.

Aucun secret, jeton, mot de passe ou OTP ne doit être affiché dans les journaux d’intégration.

================================================
# API Finance, Paie & Rappels (v254)

Role-safe, server-authoritative finance endpoints for the Atlas Commerce worker.
Everything is computed **server-side from persisted ledger rows** — client-sent
totals, roles, periods-as-identity or demo data are never trusted for reads or
writes. All routes are additive: no existing route, field or client behaviour
changed.

> Demo mode (Android) stays fully local and must never call these endpoints.

---

## Authorization model

Identity and role come **only** from the verified session (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`,
re-validated inside every handler with `authFailReason` — defense in depth on top of the
global `/api/*` auth middleware). Roles:

| Role | Finance dashboard | Payroll | Monthly PDF | Reminders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` / `admin` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | report + finance + payroll |
| `secretaire` | ❌ 403 | ❌ 403 | ❌ 403 | invoices/bills reminders only (established finance access) |
| `stock` / `user` | ❌ 403 | ❌ 403 | ❌ 403 | never |

- `secretaire` keeps its **existing** invoice/client access on the pre-existing routes
  (`canMutateBusiness`); the finance/payroll/admin-report surface here is owner/admin only.
- Recipients of scheduled notifications are re-derived from `app_users` **at delivery
  time** (active + role re-checked): a demoted or deactivated user never receives a
  message enqueued while they still had access.
- Tenant scoping: this deployment is single-company (`tenant = 'main'`, identity from
  `company_settings`). No endpoint accepts a tenant/company parameter, so cross-company
  IDOR or enumeration is structurally impossible.

### Error envelope (stable)

```jsonc
// 401 — missing/invalid session
{ "success": false, "error": "Session invalide", "code": "UNAUTHORIZED", "reason": "bad_password" }

// 403 — valid session, role not allowed
{ "success": false, "error": "Réservé aux administrateurs (owner/admin).", "code": "FIN_FORBIDDEN" }

// 400 — bad period
{ "success": false, "error": "Période invalide — format attendu YYYY-MM.", "code": "BAD_PERIOD" }
```

---

## `GET /api/admin/finance/monthly?period=YYYY-MM`

Owner/admin only. `period` optional (defaults to the current month in the company
timezone). All amounts are numbers rounded half-up to 2 decimals, in
`currency` (default `MAD`, `company_settings.finance_currency`).

```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "period": "2026-09",
    "timezone": "Africa/Casablanca",
    "currency": "MAD",
    "opening_balance": 48210.5,
    "closing_balance": 51060.25,
    "sales_received": 18500.0,       // Σ invoice_payments.amount, paid_at in period
    "refunds": 650.0,                // Σ expenses(entry_type='expense', category='Remboursement client')
    "expenses": 9200.25,             // Σ expenses(entry_type='expense') — refunds included, shown separately
    "payroll_paid": 6000.0,          // Σ employee_payments.amount, paid_at in period (advances included)
    "supplier_paid": 2200.0,         // Σ bill_payments.amount, paid_at in period
    "receivables": {
      "total_outstanding": 12400.0,
      "total_overdue": 3100.0,
      "count": 8, "truncated": false, // documents capped at 200
      "documents": [
        { "id": 142, "number": "F-2026-0142", "party": "Client Alpha",
          "total": 5000.0, "paid": 2000.0, "remaining": 3000.0,
          "due_date": "2026-09-15", "state": "overdue" }
      ]
    },
    "payables": { /* same shape, from bills + bill_payments */ },
    "payroll": { "total_due": 9000.0, "employees": 3 },
    "reconciliation": {
      "source": "d1-live",
      "generated_at": "2026-10-01T07:35:12.480Z",  // ISO-8601 UTC
      "rules": "docs/api-finance.md#calculation-rules",
      "as_of_date": "2026-09-30"
    }
  }
}
```

`documents[].state` is exactly one of `unpaid | partial | overdue | paid` (paid docs are
omitted) — derived from `remaining = total − Σ persisted payments` and `due_date` vs the
company-local today. Excluded from receivables: quotes/devis, cancelled, `VR-`/`WR-`
documents and `doc_kind` in (`quick_sale`, `ticket`, `remboursement`) — the same filter
the in-app `/api/alerts` feed uses.

### Calculation rules (v258 canonical filters)

- `sales_received` excludes « Avoir … » audit rows in `invoice_payments`
  (credit-note cash effect = paired `Remboursement client` expense row).
- `expenses` excludes mirror ledger rows written by the bill-payment and
  payroll routes (`Règlement fournisseur`/`bill_id:…`, `Salaire`/`employee_id:…`)
  — those exist only for the Solde cash journal UI. Before v258 every supplier
  and payroll payment was subtracted twice from balances (see
  `docs/finance-6000-investigation.md`).

**v259 — `mirror_audit` (automatic double-count audit).** The monthly summary and the statement
both embed a `mirror_audit` block: counts/totals of the excluded mirror ledger rows (`bill_id:` /
`employee_id:` notes) vs the `bill_payments` / `employee_payments` source tables, plus a
`consistent: true|false` flag. It runs **in production automatically** on every request — no
wrangler CLI, no PC needed — so the 6,000 MAD double-count fix
(`docs/finance-6000-investigation.md`) is continuously verified from the app itself. If a future
feature re-introduces mirror double counting, `consistent` flips to `false` in the live response.

### Legacy calculation rules

- **sales_received** — `invoice_payments` rows with `paid_at` inside the period (partial
  payments count in the month they were recorded; late-recorded payments land in the
  month of their `paid_at`, never silently rewritten).
- **expenses** — `expenses` with `entry_type='expense'` by `expense_date`. The ledger's
  `entry_type='income'` rows (encaissements) mirror `invoice_payments` and are excluded
  to avoid double counting.
- **refunds** — subset of expenses with `category='Remboursement client'` (avoirs `WR-`
  refuse payments via the existing `WR_NO_PAYMENT` rule; a refund is cash-out, recorded
  as an expense, and shows here separately).
- **closing_balance** — cumulative over ALL history ≤ period end:
  `Σ sales − Σ expenses − Σ payroll_paid − Σ supplier_paid`.
- **opening_balance** — `closing_balance − (period sales − expenses − payroll_paid − supplier_paid)`.
- **payroll.total_due** — accrued obligations of active employees due by period end:
  anchor = `last_paid_at || joined_date`, cycle = 30 days for `monthly` (else
  `pay_cycle_days`), pro-rata `(elapsed/cycle) × pay_amount` capped at one cycle,
  advances (`Acompte` payments since the anchor) deducted. **Never inferred from sales
  or user balances.**
- Voided/cancelled invoices are excluded everywhere; paid-in-full documents drop out of
  outstanding lists the moment their payments cover the total.

### Timezone semantics

Business dates (`due_date`, `expense_date`, `paid_at`) are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` strings in
the company timezone (`company_settings.finance_timezone`, default `Africa/Casablanca`).
Period bounds are inclusive local date ranges — a payment recorded `2026-09-30` belongs
to September even if its UTC `created_at` is already October. Machine timestamps
(`generated_at`, `created_at`) are ISO-8601 UTC. Morocco has no DST; the `Intl`-based
local-date computation is DST- and month-length-safe for any configured zone.

---

## `GET /api/admin/employees/payroll?period=YYYY-MM&page=1&page_size=50&due_before=YYYY-MM-DD`

Owner/admin only. Deliberately minimal fields — no phone, national id, sales figures or
balances ever leave the server on this route.

- `period` sets the accrual cut-off (`as_of` = min(today, period end)).
- `due_before` keeps only rows with `due_date ≤ due_before`.
- `page_size` max 200; rows sorted by `due_date` then `employee_id`; stable paging.

```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "period": "2026-10", "as_of": "2026-10-25",
    "timezone": "Africa/Casablanca", "currency": "MAD",
    "totals": { "amount_due": 4500.0, "unpaid_count": 2, "count": 5 },
    "page": 1, "page_size": 50, "total": 5, "has_more": false,
    "rows": [
      {
        "employee_id": 12,
        "display_name": "Karim Ben",
        "amount_due": 1500.0,
        "pay_period": { "from": "2026-10-01", "to": "2026-10-31" },
        "due_date": "2026-10-31",
        "status": "unpaid",            // 'unpaid' = due by as_of and amount > 0; else 'paid'
        "last_payment": { "amount": 500.0, "paid_at": "2026-10-10", "period_label": "Acompte octobre" }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`amount_due` already deducts advances recorded since the pay-period anchor. Recording a
salary payment stays on the existing `POST /api/employees/:id/payments` workflow
(unchanged) — this route never mutates.

---

## `GET /api/admin/finance/monthly/report.pdf?period=YYYY-MM`

Owner/admin only. Returns the monthly treasury report as a **generated-on-demand,
streamed** PDF:

- `Content-Type: application/pdf`
- `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="rapport-mensuel-2026-09.pdf"`
- `Cache-Control: no-store`

Nothing is ever written to R2/public storage and there is no enumerable URL: the period
alone yields nothing without a verified owner/admin session (query-param `?token=`
print links are intentionally NOT accepted here). Each download writes an audit row
(`action: finance_report_pdf`, actor, ip, period).

Contents: period, currency, generation timestamp, opening/closing balances, sales,
expenses (with refunds broken out), payroll paid, supplier paid, outstanding client
amounts (total + overdue + up to 14 document lines), outstanding supplier amounts
(same), payroll still due (total + headcount), confidentiality footer. No unrelated
personal data — client/employee names only where they identify an obligation.

---

## Scheduled reminders (non-spammy by construction)

Trigger: wrangler cron `35 7 * * *` UTC ≈ **08:35 Africa/Casablanca** daily →
`scheduled()` → `runFinanceReminders`. An external scheduler can instead call:

```
POST /api/cron/finance-reminders
Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>        (or X-Cron-Secret: <CRON_SECRET>)
```

(503 `CRON_SECRET_MISSING` when the secret is unset, 401 `CRON_UNAUTHORIZED` on a wrong
secret — same contract as `/api/cron/backup-execute`.)

### Events & recipients

| Event | When | Recipients |
|---|---|---|
| `report_reminder:1:<period>` | day 1 of month, for the previous month | owner/admin — "rapport prêt" (or why not) + headline numbers |
| `report_reminder:2/3:<period>` | days 2 and 3 | owner/admin — **only what changed** since day 1 (stored snapshot diff: newly overdue, receivables/payables/payroll deltas) + link to the authorized report; "Aucun changement" otherwise |
| `invoice_due:<id>:<date>` | client invoice due **today** | owner/admin/secretaire — client *needs to pay* X today |
| `invoice_overdue:<id>:<due-month>` | client invoice overdue | owner/admin/secretaire — client *hasn't paid* / *partially paid*, amount + since when (once per due-month) |
| `bill_due:<id>:<date>` / `bill_overdue:<id>:<due-month>` | supplier bill due/overdue | owner/admin/secretaire — what **we** still need to pay |
| `payroll_due:<emp>:<due-month>` | salary obligation due | **owner/admin only** — secretaire never receives payroll |
| `payment_recorded:<id>:<date>` | a client payment is recorded (hooked into the existing payment handler) | owner/admin/secretaire — client *has paid* X, invoice soldée/partielle + remaining |

Client states are always explicit: *needs to pay* (due/overdue + remaining), *has paid*
(payment_recorded, soldée), *partial* (remaining after the recorded amount). Supplier
bills and payroll obligations are stated separately from client receivables.

### Delivery guarantees

- **Durable outbox**: `finance_outbox` table with `UNIQUE idem_key` where
  `idem_key = tenant|event|period|recipient`. Enqueue is `INSERT OR IGNORE` — duplicate
  cron runs, worker restarts, retried invocations and multi-instance races can never
  double-notify (structurally, not best-effort).
- **Retries**: FCM failures keep the row `pending` with exponential backoff
  (1 h → 2 h → 4 h → 8 h, `next_attempt_at` stored in D1) and give up at 5 attempts
  (`failed` + `last_error`). Every row carries a delivery audit trail
  (`status pending|sent|skipped|failed`, `attempts`, `sent_at`, `last_error`).
- **Re-authorization at delivery**: recipient must still exist, be `active`, and still
  hold the minimum role for that event — otherwise the row is `skipped`.
- **Privacy**: amounts appear in push bodies only while
  `company_settings.finance_push_amounts = 1`; set it to `0` and every digit run is
  masked (`—`) for lock-screen safety. Document numbers/titles stay (identifiers, not
  amounts).
- Channel: existing FCM push (`worker/lib/fcm.ts`, Android tokens); the in-app feed
  (`/api/alerts`) remains computed live and unchanged.

---

## Storage & migration

Created lazily and idempotently on first use (`ensureFinanceSchema`):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS finance_outbox (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  tenant TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'main',
  event TEXT NOT NULL, period TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  recipient TEXT NOT NULL, channel TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'push',
  title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', body TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  href TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', payload TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  idem_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  next_attempt_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', last_error TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')), sent_at TEXT
);
ALTER TABLE company_settings ADD COLUMN finance_timezone TEXT DEFAULT 'Africa/Casablanca';
ALTER TABLE company_settings ADD COLUMN finance_currency TEXT DEFAULT 'MAD';
ALTER TABLE company_settings ADD COLUMN finance_push_amounts INTEGER DEFAULT 1;
```

No existing table is modified beyond the three additive `company_settings` columns.

**Rollback**: remove the `triggers.crons` block from `wrangler.jsonc` and redeploy the
previous worker — the routes and table simply go unused; `DROP TABLE finance_outbox` is
optional and safe (nothing else references it). No data written by this feature is
required by any pre-existing flow.

---

## Android — required API/DTO additions

```kotlin
// GET /api/admin/finance/monthly?period=2026-09
data class FinanceMonthlyDto(
  val period: String, val timezone: String, val currency: String,
  @SerialName("opening_balance") val openingBalance: Double,
  @SerialName("closing_balance") val closingBalance: Double,
  @SerialName("sales_received") val salesReceived: Double,
  val refunds: Double, val expenses: Double,
  @SerialName("payroll_paid") val payrollPaid: Double,
  @SerialName("supplier_paid") val supplierPaid: Double,
  val receivables: OutstandingBucketDto, val payables: OutstandingBucketDto,
  val payroll: PayrollBucketDto, val reconciliation: ReconciliationDto,
)
data class OutstandingBucketDto(
  @SerialName("total_outstanding") val totalOutstanding: Double,
  @SerialName("total_overdue") val totalOverdue: Double,
  val count: Int, val truncated: Boolean, val documents: List<OutstandingDocDto>,
)
data class OutstandingDocDto(
  val id: Long, val number: String, val party: String,
  val total: Double, val paid: Double, val remaining: Double,
  @SerialName("due_date") val dueDate: String?, val state: String, // unpaid|partial|overdue
)
data class PayrollBucketDto(@SerialName("total_due") val totalDue: Double, val employees: Int)
data class ReconciliationDto(
  val source: String, @SerialName("generated_at") val generatedAt: String,
  val rules: String, @SerialName("as_of_date") val asOfDate: String?,
)

// GET /api/admin/employees/payroll?period=2026-10&page=1
data class PayrollPageDto(
  val period: String, @SerialName("as_of") val asOf: String,
  val timezone: String, val currency: String, val totals: PayrollTotalsDto,
  val page: Int, @SerialName("page_size") val pageSize: Int,
  val total: Int, @SerialName("has_more") val hasMore: Boolean, val rows: List<PayrollRowDto>,
)
data class PayrollTotalsDto(
  @SerialName("amount_due") val amountDue: Double,
  @SerialName("unpaid_count") val unpaidCount: Int, val count: Int,
)
data class PayrollRowDto(
  @SerialName("employee_id") val employeeId: Long,
  @SerialName("display_name") val displayName: String,
  @SerialName("amount_due") val amountDue: Double,

  @SerialName("due_date") val dueDate: String?,
  val status: String, // unpaid|paid
  @SerialName("last_payment") val lastPayment: LastPaymentDto?,
)
data class PayPeriodDto(val from: String, val to: String)
data class LastPaymentDto(
  val amount: Double, @SerialName("paid_at") val paidAt: String,
  @SerialName("period_label") val periodLabel: String,
)

// PDF: GET /api/admin/finance/monthly/report.pdf?period=2026-09
// → stream to file with the Authorization header (no ?token= support), then share/open.
```

Forbidden (403) and unauthorized (401) responses use the stable envelopes shown above —
map `code == "FIN_FORBIDDEN"` to "Réservé aux administrateurs" in French UI copy.
Push notifications arrive via the existing FCM channel with
`data = { href, kind, period }` where `kind` is the event name from the reminders table.

## `GET /api/admin/finance/statement?period=YYYY-MM&page=1&page_size=50` (v258)

Server-backed monthly statement, owner/admin gate (same `FIN_FORBIDDEN`
envelope). One canonical ledger over the five persisted cash sources — the
monthly summary, this statement and the PDF all derive from the same filtered
queries, so they cannot disagree:

- **credit** = `invoice_payments` excluding « Avoir … » audit trails (a credit
  note's cash effect lives in its paired `Remboursement client` expense row);
- **debit** = real `expenses` (mirror ledger rows excluded:
  `Règlement fournisseur`+`notes bill_id:…`, `Salaire`+`notes employee_id:…`),
  client refunds, `employee_payments`, `bill_payments`.

Response (additive, stable codes):

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "period": "2026-10",
    "timezone": "Africa/Casablanca",
    "currency": "MAD",
    "as_of": "2026-10-25",
    "status": "open",
    "opening_balance": 1234.56,
    "closing_balance": 2345.67,
    "totals": { "credits": 5000.0, "debits": 3888.89, "net": 1111.11 },
    "reconciliation": {
      "opening": 1234.56, "credits": 5000.0, "debits": 3888.89,
      "closing": 2345.67, "balanced": true,
      "rule": "opening + credits - debits = closing"
    },
    "page": 1, "page_size": 50, "total": 12, "has_more": false,
    "rows": [
      {
        "id": 41, "source": "bill_payments", "type": "supplier",
        "label": "Règlement achat ACH-500", "ref": "ACH-500",
        "debit": 6000.0, "credit": 0, "ts": "2026-10-05",
        "running_balance": -4765.44
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Row `type` ∈ `sale | refund | expense | payroll | supplier`. Labels/refs are
sanitized: payroll rows expose `emp_number` (or `EMP-<id>`) and the payment
label — never names, national ids or balances. `status` is `open` for the
current tenant-timezone month (rows stop at `as_of`) and `closed` otherwise
(full period). Pagination is over rows only; totals and reconciliation always
cover the whole period. Errors: `400 BAD_PERIOD`, `401 UNAUTHORIZED`,
`403 FIN_FORBIDDEN`, `500 FINANCE_ERROR`.

Investigation of the duplicated 6,000 MAD symptom (mirror ledger rows counted
twice before v258) and the production confirmation probe:
`docs/finance-6000-investigation.md`.

## `GET /api/admin/finance/period?period=YYYY-MM` (v264)

Owner/admin gate (same `FIN_FORBIDDEN` envelope). Cash & bank breakdown of the
selected period — **same timezone and canonical ledger rules as the
statement**, computed only from persisted rows:

- identical filtered sources (`invoice_payments` excluding « Avoir » trails,
  `expenses` `entry_type='expense'` excluding mirror rows,
  `employee_payments`, `bill_payments`);
- an OPEN month stops at `as_of` = today in the company finance timezone,
  a CLOSED month is the full calendar month;
- the embedded `statement` block is `computeStatement()`'s own output and
  `consistent_with_breakdown` re-checks the invariant on every call — this
  endpoint cannot disagree with `GET /api/admin/finance/statement`.

Payment-method buckets (canonical app rule — `src/pages/Balance.tsx`
`isCash`): `cash` = persisted `'cash'`/`''`/NULL (the schema DEFAULT, a
recorded value — not a guess); `bank`/`card`/`check` = the recorded
vocabulary of the payment selector; `other` = a recorded method outside that
vocabulary (surfaced as-is, never merged away); `not_recorded` = sources with
NO `payment_method` column (`employee_payments` — payroll is never guessed
cash or bank). Headline split: `cash` vs `bank` where **bank =
bank+card+check+other** (the app's caisse/banque view). Invariant per source:
`total = cash + bank + not_recorded`.

Owner movements (`entry_type` `owner_contrib`/`owner_draw`) and recorded misc
income (`entry_type='income'`) are real `expenses` rows but are **excluded
from statement cash** — they live in separate blocks
(`owner.contributions`, `owner.withdrawals`, `inflows.by_source.recorded_income`)
and are never folded into statement credits/debits.

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "period": "2026-09", "timezone": "Africa/Casablanca", "currency": "MAD",
    "as_of": "2026-09-30", "status": "closed",
    "inflows": {
      "total": 2350.0, "count": 5, "cash": 1500.0, "bank": 850.0, "not_recorded": 0,
      "by_method": { "cash": 1500.0, "bank": 600.0, "card": 250.0, "check": 0, "other": 0, "not_recorded": 0 },
      "by_source": {
        "invoice_payments": { "total": 1750.0, "count": 3, "cash": 1000.0, "bank": 750.0, "…": "…" },
        "recorded_income":   { "total": 600.0,  "count": 2, "cash": 500.0,  "bank": 100.0, "…": "…" }
      }
    },
    "outflows": {
      "total": 6015.0, "count": 6, "cash": 1065.0, "bank": 950.0, "not_recorded": 4000.0,
      "refunds_total": 90.0,
      "by_source": {
        "expenses": { "total": 515.0,  "count": 4, "cash": 365.0, "bank": 150.0 },
        "payroll":  { "total": 4000.0, "count": 1, "cash": 0, "bank": 0, "not_recorded": 4000.0 },
        "supplier": { "total": 1500.0, "count": 2, "cash": 700.0, "bank": 800.0 }
      }
    },
    "owner": {
      "contributions": { "total": 2000.0, "count": 1, "cash": 0, "bank": 2000.0 },
      "withdrawals":   { "total": 300.0,  "count": 1, "cash": 300.0, "bank": 0 },
      "net": 1700.0
    },

      { "category": "Loyer", "total": 350.0, "count": 2 },

    ],
    "categories_truncated": false,
    "statement": {
      "opening_balance": 0, "credits": 1750.0, "debits": 6015.0,
      "closing_balance": -4265.0, "net": -4265.0, "balanced": true,
```

`expense_categories` covers the statement's expense slice (refunds included,
sorted by total desc, capped at 100 rows with `categories_truncated`).
Errors: `400 BAD_PERIOD`, `401 UNAUTHORIZED`, `403 FIN_FORBIDDEN`,
`500 FINANCE_ERROR`. Tests: `worker/__tests__/finance.test.ts` (v264 blocks).

---

## Ledger write authorization (v264 audit fix)

`POST /api/expenses` and `POST /api/expenses/import` are **owner/admin only**
(`403 OWNER_ONLY`). Before v264 they sat behind the generic `/api/*`
authentication middleware only — any authenticated role (`stock`, `user`,
`secretaire`…) could insert ledger rows, including owner movements
(`entry_type` `owner_contrib`/`owner_draw`). The routes now live in
`worker/routes/expenses.ts` with defense-in-depth session re-validation
(`authFailReason`) exactly like every finance surface, plus an audit trail
(`expense.create` / `expense.import`). Validation contract unchanged:
`422 VALIDATION` (amount bounds), `400` (missing description), entry_type
whitelist coerces unknown values to `expense`. `DELETE /api/expenses/:id`
keeps its existing gate (secretaire+ with password confirm). Tests:
`worker/__tests__/expenses-auth.test.ts`.

---

## `GET /api/me/payroll` — employee-SELF pay date (v256)

Role-safe by construction: **any** authenticated session (`user`, `stock`,
`secretaire`, `admin`, `owner`) may call it, but it only ever returns the
payroll obligation of the ONE employee file linked to the caller's own login —
the username is taken exclusively from the verified session (no query params,
no body, no way to ask for someone else).

Linking: `employees.user_username` (new column, migration-safe) is set by an
owner/admin in the employee form ("Compte lié (identifiant de connexion)") or
via `POST/PUT /api/employees`. Matching is `LOWER(TRIM(user_username))`.

```http
GET /api/me/payroll
Authorization: Bearer <session>
```

Responses:

- `200` linked + payroll configured:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "linked": true,
    "payroll_configured": true,
    "employee_id": 12,
    "display_name": "Yasmine B.",
    "amount_due": 1450.00,
    "pay_period": { "from": "2026-09-26", "to": "2026-10-26" },
    "due_date": "2026-10-26",
    "daily_rate": 48.33,
    "status": "unpaid",
    "last_payment": { "amount": 2900.00, "paid_at": "2026-09-26", "period_label": "Salaire septembre" },
    "as_of": "2026-10-25",
    "timezone": "Africa/Casablanca",
    "currency": "MAD"
  }
}
```

- `200` linked but payroll not configured (`pay_amount` 0 or no anchor date):
  `{ linked: true, payroll_configured: false, employee_id, last_payment, ... }` —
  show "Date de paie non configurée" in the app.
- `404` `PAYROLL_NOT_LINKED` — no employee file linked to this login. French UI
  copy: "Aucune fiche employé liée à votre compte."
- `409` `PAYROLL_AMBIGUOUS` — two employee files share the same login (admin
  must fix the link).
- `401` `UNAUTHORIZED` — invalid/expired session (with `reason`).

Math is identical to the admin payroll route (pro-rata accrual, advances
deducted, capped at one cycle) — same `payrollObligation()` function, computed
as of today in the tenant timezone. The employee sees their own amounts; that
is their data, never another row's.

Android usage: call it on the Profil/Accueil screen for non-admin roles and
render `due_date` ("Prochaine paie : 26/10/2026") plus `status`; no admin
finance surface is exposed to employees.

## Tests

`worker/__tests__/finance.test.ts` (25 tests, vitest): period/leap/TZ-boundary math,
doc classification, gates for all five roles + anonymous, payroll accrual/cap/advances,
PDF byte structure, and real-SQLite integration for outbox dedupe, monthly summary math,

delivery-time re-authorization (demoted/deactivated skipped), day 1/2/4 report sequence,
payment-recorded dedupe, retry/backoff/attempt-cap, and lock-screen amount masking.

# Atlas Commerce — backend hardening (Workers / D1)

## Already in place
- **Auth**: Bearer session JWT-like tokens, role gates (`requireBizMutator`, owner-only)
- **Rate limits**: KV `rateLimit` on admin / auth / public routes
- **Idempotency**: `idempotency_keys` table + partner `Idempotency-Key`
- **Caching**: KV for settings & product lists (TTL)
- **Ephemeral purge**: OTP, WebAuthn challenges, login attempts, old idempotency
- **CORS / security headers** on Worker

## This pass
- **Schema**: `products.tax_rate`, `bulk_discounts`, indexes (sku/barcode/category/parent)
- **Schema**: `company_settings.tax_rate` via `ensureHrSettings`
- **Ensure** before product write & tax_rate SELECT
- **API**: friendlier D1/tax_rate client messages

## Cloudflare model (realistic scope)
| Pattern | On Workers/D1 |
|---------|----------------|
| Horizontal scaling | Automatic (Workers isolates) |
| Load balancing | Cloudflare edge |
| DB replication | D1 read replicas (platform) — not app-level sharding |
| Message queues | Optional Queues binding — not required for current ERP path |
| CAP | Prefer **availability + partition** at edge; strong consistency per D1 primary |

Not implementing custom consistent hashing / multi-region sharding in-app: platform owns that layer.
